Privacy Policy

Data Protection & Usage
Last Updated: Oct 22, 2026

At {{SERVER_NAME}} ("we", "us", "our"), protecting your privacy is a priority. This policy outlines exactly what data we collect from you when you play on our Minecraft Server or use our Webstore, and how we use it to improve your experience and ensure fair play.

1. Information We Collect

We collect data from two main sources: your interaction with our Game Server and your use of our Webstore.

Website & Store Data
  • Email Address: For purchase receipts and account auth.
  • Payment Data: Transaction IDs (we do not process cards directly).
  • Browser Data: IP address, cookies for login sessions.
  • Discord ID: If you link your account.
In-Game Server Data
  • Minecraft Username & UUID: To identify your player profile.
  • IP Address: Logged for security and ban evasion checks.
  • Chat Logs: Public chat and messages are logged for moderation.
  • Command Usage: We log commands for debugging and security.

2. Chat Logs & Moderation

To maintain a safe environment for all players, we retain logs of text chat, command usage, and gameplay interactions. These logs are:

  • Confidential: Only accessible by authorized staff members (Admins/Moderators).
  • Used for Evidence: To investigate reports of harassment, griefing, hacking, or other rule violations.
  • Retention: Logs may be kept indefinitely to track repeat offenders.

3. Cookies & Cookie Consent

When you visit our website, a Cookie Consent banner appears asking for your permission before any non-essential cookies are set. Your choice is saved in your browser's local storage under the key server_cookie_consent and is remembered for future visits.

Cookie Categories

Functional (Always On)Required

Essential cookies that keep the site working correctly. These cannot be disabled. They include login session tokens, shopping cart data, theme preference, and security tokens (Cloudflare Turnstile).

Analytics (Optional)Your Choice

Help us understand how visitors use the site — which pages are popular, how long visitors stay, and where they come from. Data is aggregated and anonymous. We may use Google Analytics for this purpose.

Advertising (Optional)Your Choice

Used to display relevant advertisements through Google AdSense. Google may use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this or other websites. You can opt out at google.com/settings/ads.

Changing Your Preferences

You can change or withdraw your consent at any time by clearing your browser's local storage for this site, or using your browser's built-in cookie controls. On most browsers: Settings → Privacy → Clear browsing data → Cookies and site data.

4. How We Use Data

Service Delivery

To automatically process your payments and grant in-game ranks/items via our plugin system.

Security & Safety

We use IP addresses to identify and block alternate accounts of banned players (Ban Evasion).

5. Third-Party Sharing

We do not sell your personal data. However, we share necessary data with trusted partners to operate the server:

  • Payment Processors: (e.g., Stripe, Paypal, Mobile Banking) to handle secure transactions.
  • Discord: If you link your account, we sync your roles with our Discord server.
  • Google AdSense: If you accept advertising cookies, Google may collect data to serve personalised ads. See Google's Privacy Policy.
  • Google Analytics: If you accept analytics cookies, aggregated usage data is shared with Google to help us improve the site.

6. Data Privacy Contact

If you wish to request deletion of your Webstore account data, please contact us. Note that we cannot delete in-game punishment history or public chat logs in accordance with our legitimate interest in server safety.

Discord support

By playing on {{SERVER_NAME}}, you agree to this Privacy Policy.

We reserve the right to update this policy as server features evolve.

Minecraft Java vs Bedrock: Which Should You Play?

Oct 18, 2026
joynalbokhsho

If you are new to the game, the biggest question is Minecraft Java vs Bedrock: which edition should you play? Both versions have the same blocks, mobs and survival gameplay, but they differ in devices, mods, servers and performance. In this guide we compare Minecraft Java vs Bedrock in simple language so you can choose the right edition, and see which one works best for joining servers like {{SERVER_NAME}}.

In this guide we break down the differences in simple language so you can choose the right edition. We also explain which one works best for joining servers like {{SERVER_NAME}}.

Minecraft Java vs Bedrock: Quick Answer

  • Choose Java Edition if you play on a PC and want mods, custom servers, minigames and the biggest community.
  • Choose Bedrock Edition if you play on a mobile phone, console or low-end device, or want to play with friends on different devices.

Here is the detailed comparison.

Minecraft Java vs Bedrock: Comparison Table

FeatureJava EditionBedrock Edition
DevicesWindows, macOS, LinuxWindows, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, Android, iOS
ModsHuge mod support (Forge, Fabric)Add-ons and Marketplace content
ServersThousands of custom servers with pluginsFeatured servers, Realms and many custom servers
PerformanceHeavier, needs a stronger PCLighter, runs well on low-end devices
Cross-playJava players onlyWorks across Bedrock devices
ControlsKeyboard and mouseTouch, controller, keyboard and mouse
CombatAttack cooldown, more skill-basedFaster, no attack cooldown
Skins & ContentFree custom skinsFree skins plus paid Marketplace packs

As the table shows, the Minecraft Java vs Bedrock choice mostly comes down to your device and the way you like to play.

1. Minecraft Java vs Bedrock: Devices and Platforms

This is the biggest difference.

Java Edition runs only on PC (Windows, macOS and Linux). If you do not have a computer, you cannot play Java.

Bedrock Edition runs on almost everything: Windows PC, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, and Android and iOS phones.

Winner for device choice: Bedrock. If you only have a phone or console, Bedrock is your only option.

2. Mods and Customization

Java Edition has the largest modding community in gaming. With tools like Fabric and Forge, you can add new dimensions, machines, magic systems, shaders and much more.

Bedrock Edition does not support traditional mods. Instead, it uses Add-ons and Marketplace content, which are easier to install but more limited.

Winner for mods: Java.

3. Minecraft Java vs Bedrock Servers and Multiplayer

Both editions have multiplayer, but the experience is different.

Java Edition is famous for custom servers. Server owners can use plugins to build:

  • Survival and SMP servers
  • Skyblock and Prison
  • Factions and PvP
  • Minigames like Bed Wars and Sky Wars
  • Economy and rank systems
Bedrock Edition servers exist too, and you can also play on Realms or join friends easily on different devices. Many Java servers also allow Bedrock players to join through special tools.

Winner for server variety: Java.

4. Minecraft Java vs Bedrock Performance and Lag

Bedrock Edition is generally lighter and runs smoother on low-end PCs and phones. If your computer is old or has low RAM, Bedrock often gives better FPS.

Java Edition needs more resources, but you can improve performance with optimization mods like Sodium and Lithium.

Winner for low-end devices: Bedrock.

5. Cross-Play with Friends

Want to play with a friend who uses a different device?

  • Bedrock players can play together across Windows, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and mobile.
  • Java players can only play with other Java players, unless the server supports Bedrock connections.

Winner for cross-play: Bedrock.

6. Combat and PvP

Combat feels different in each edition.

Java Edition has an attack cooldown. You need to time your hits, which rewards skill. Many PvP players prefer Java for this reason.

Bedrock Edition has faster, simpler combat without an attack cooldown, so players can click rapidly.

Winner for competitive PvP: most players prefer Java, but it comes down to your style.

7. Price and How to Get It

On PC, buying Minecraft for Windows gives you access to both Java and Bedrock editions through the official launcher. On phones and consoles, you buy Bedrock from the official store for your device.

Always buy Minecraft from the official Minecraft website or your device's official store to stay safe.

Minecraft Java vs Bedrock: Which Edition Should You Choose?

Pick Java Edition if you:

  • Play on a PC
  • Want mods and shaders
  • Like custom server modes and minigames
  • Enjoy skill-based PvP

Pick Bedrock Edition if you:

  • Play on a phone, tablet or console
  • Have a low-end PC
  • Want to play with friends on different devices
  • Prefer simple controls

Not sure? If you have a PC, you can try both and decide which one feels better for you.

Which Edition Works on {{SERVER_NAME}}?

Our server is built for the {{SERVER_REGION}}i Minecraft community, with survival, game modes, ranks and an active Discord.

Java Server IP: PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM
Bedrock Server IP: PE.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM | {{BEDROCK_PORT}}
Supported editions: [Java / Bedrock / Both]
Version: Latest

👉 Check our How to Join a Minecraft Server guide to connect step by step.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Which is better in Minecraft Java vs Bedrock?

Neither is better for everyone. Java is better for mods, custom servers and PvP. Bedrock is better for mobile, console, low-end devices and cross-play.

Can Java and Bedrock players play together?

Not by default. They use different versions of the game. However, some servers allow both editions to join the same server using special connection tools.

Is Minecraft Bedrock free?

No, Minecraft is a paid game. Do not download cracked or fake versions, because they can contain viruses and may not work on official servers.

Which Minecraft edition is better for low-end PCs?

Bedrock usually runs better on low-end devices. On Java, you can improve FPS with optimization mods such as Sodium.

Which edition has more servers?

Java Edition has the larger and more varied server community, with thousands of custom servers and game modes.

Can I play Minecraft on mobile?

Yes. Mobile players use Bedrock Edition, available on Android and iOS.

Final Thoughts on Minecraft Java vs Bedrock

The Minecraft Java vs Bedrock debate has no single right answer. Both editions are great ways to enjoy the game: Java gives you freedom with mods and servers, while Bedrock gives you flexibility across devices.

The best edition is the one that works on your device and lets you play with your friends.

/minecraft-guides/best-shovel-enchantmen.main:
Minecraft Guides

Best Shovel Enchantments in Minecraft: Max Combo

Nov 2, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Shovels do not get the same love as swords and pickaxes, but a good shovel saves more time than almost any other tool. Digging dirt, sand, gravel, and snow by hand is slow, and clearing land for a build or a farm can take hours with a plain shovel. This guide covers the best shovel enchantments in minecraft, including which enchantments combine, which ones conflict, and the cheapest anvil order for a maxed-out shovel.

The best shovel enchantments in minecraft are simple to remember: Efficiency V for speed, Unbreaking III for durability, Mending for repairs, and either Silk Touch or Fortune for loot, depending on the job. The rest of this guide explains why each one matters and how to get them without wasting levels.

Best Shovel Enchantments in Minecraft: The Maxed-Out Combo

For a general purpose shovel you will use every day, aim for this combo: Efficiency V, Unbreaking III, Mending, and Silk Touch. This is the best all-round shovel for digging, landscaping, and gathering blocks exactly as they are. Silk Touch lets you pick up grass blocks, snow layers, and gravel without breaking them into other items, which is perfect for building and decorating.

If you dig a lot of gravel for flint, or you want extra drops from dirt-like blocks, swap Silk Touch for Fortune III. Fortune increases drops from gravel and similar blocks, but it cannot be combined with Silk Touch on the same tool, so you need to pick one. Many experienced players keep two shovels: a Silk Touch shovel for building and a Fortune shovel for farming flint and drops. That is the smart way to use the best shovel enchantments in minecraft without giving up either option.

Every Shovel Enchantment Explained

Efficiency V

Efficiency is the most important shovel enchantment. Each level increases digging speed, and Efficiency V makes dirt, sand, gravel, and snow break almost instantly. With Efficiency V and a diamond or netherite shovel, you can clear huge areas in minutes. Always put Efficiency V first when you build your shovel, because speed is the whole point of the tool.

Unbreaking III

Unbreaking III gives your shovel a chance to ignore durability loss on each use. In practice, it roughly quadruples how long the tool lasts. A shovel without Unbreaking breaks surprisingly fast when you are clearing land, so this enchantment is essential for any shovel you plan to keep.

Mending

Mending repairs your shovel using experience orbs you collect while holding it. With Mending and Unbreaking III, a shovel can last forever if you collect experience regularly from mining, farming, or mob kills. Mending is the best long term investment for any tool, and it is especially good on a shovel because digging and farming generate experience all the time. The easiest way to get Mending is trading with a librarian villager, fishing, or finding it in loot chests.

Silk Touch

Silk Touch lets you mine blocks in their original form. A Silk Touch shovel picks up grass blocks, mycelium, podzol, snow, and gravel as whole blocks instead of breaking them down. This is vital for builders who want grass for landscaping or snow for decoration. It also lets you move gravel without it turning into flint, which matters when you need the block itself.

Fortune III

Fortune increases the number of drops from certain blocks. On a shovel, the main benefit is gravel, which drops flint more often with Fortune. Fortune III gives gravel about a 100 percent chance to drop flint, which makes it the best choice if you are farming flint for arrows or fletching. Fortune does not increase drops from dirt or sand, so it is a specialist choice, not a general one.

What about other enchantments?

Shovels cannot take Sharpness, Looting, or most combat enchantments, so do not waste books trying. Curse of Vanishing is an enchantment to avoid, since it makes the tool disappear when you die. The list above is complete for a practical shovel: Efficiency, Unbreaking, Mending, plus Silk Touch or Fortune.

How to Enchant a Shovel

There are two main ways to get the best shovel enchantments in minecraft: the enchanting table and the anvil with books.

For the enchanting table, place the shovel in the table surrounded by bookshelves. More bookshelves, up to 15, give higher level enchantments. Use lapis lazuli and experience levels to roll for enchantments. The table gives random results, so you may get Efficiency IV and need to combine books or tools to reach Efficiency V. This method is cheap early on, but random.

For a guaranteed maxed-out shovel, use enchanted books and an anvil. Get books from librarian villagers, fishing, loot chests, or an enchanting table, then combine them on the anvil in the cheapest order. The anvil method costs more levels, but you control exactly which enchantments go on the tool, which is why most late game players prefer it.

Cheapest Anvil Order

Anvil costs rise with each operation, and combining books in the wrong order can make a shovel too expensive to finish. A good cheap order is to combine the two cheapest books first, then combine that result with the next book, working from cheapest to most expensive. For example, combine Unbreaking III and Mending books first if they are cheap, then add Efficiency V, then add Silk Touch or Fortune last.

Another tip is to apply enchantments to a fresh, undamaged shovel. Repairing a damaged tool on the anvil adds to its prior work penalty, which raises future costs. Start with a new diamond or netherite shovel, add all your books in one planned session, and keep it repaired with Mending afterwards instead of anvil repairs. If an anvil says a combination is too expensive, you have hit the 39 level cap, so try a different combination order or use a fresh tool.

Using Your Maxed-Out Shovel

A maxed-out shovel changes how you play. Clearing land for a house, flattening a farm area, digging out a basement, or gathering sand for glass all become fast jobs instead of chores. Pair your shovel with a good pickaxe and axe, and you can reshape terrain in an afternoon.

In practice, the best shovel enchantments in minecraft shine most on big projects. Digging a trench, levelling a hill, or harvesting a snow biome is where Efficiency V saves real time. Keep your Silk Touch shovel for building jobs and your Fortune shovel for flint farming, and carry a spare unenchanted shovel for jobs where you do not want to waste durability on your good tools.

FAQ

Can you put Silk Touch and Fortune on the same shovel?

No. Silk Touch and Fortune conflict and cannot be combined on the same tool in normal survival. Pick Silk Touch for building and block gathering, or Fortune for extra drops like flint from gravel. Keep two shovels if you want both.

Is Efficiency V worth it on a shovel?

Yes, absolutely. Efficiency V is the single biggest speed upgrade for a shovel, and it turns slow digging into instant breaking for dirt, sand, gravel, and snow. It is the first enchantment to add to any shovel you plan to use often.

How do you get Mending for a shovel?

The most reliable way is trading with a librarian villager who sells a Mending book. You can also get Mending books from fishing, loot chests in End cities and other structures, and raid drops. Once you have the book, apply it with an anvil.

Diamond or netherite shovel: which is better?

A good seed is the difference between a world you abandon after one night and a world you still play months later. One honest warning before the list: world generation changes between Minecraft versions. A seed that spawns a mansion 250 blocks away on one version can look different on another, and Java and Bedrock generate different terrain from the same code. Treat these as strong, tested starting points, test each seed in a fresh world first, and keep a backup of any world you love. With that said, here are the best Minecraft seeds to try right now.

How to Use a Minecraft Seed

Best Bow Enchantments in Minecraft: Maxed-Out Combo

Oct 28, 2026
joynalbokhsho

A good bow can clear a pillager outpost, defend a base and hunt for food without ever getting close to danger. A great bow does all of that faster, quieter and from much further away. This guide covers the best bow enchantments in minecraft, the maxed out combo to aim for, the enchantments that will not combine, and the cheapest anvil order to build it without wasting levels.

If you only take one idea from this guide, take this: Power V is the heart of a combat bow, and everything else exists to support it. Damage wins fights. The rest is range, speed, durability and ammo.

The maxed out combo for the best bow enchantments in minecraft

For most players, the best bow enchantments in minecraft look like this:

  • Power V: the most damage per shot
  • Punch II: knocks enemies back, useful for keeping mobs and players at range
  • Flame I: sets arrows on fire, adding burn damage over time
  • Unbreaking III: slows durability loss, so the bow lasts much longer
  • Infinity I or Mending I: pick one, because they cannot be combined (explained below)
  • Curse of Vanishing is not recommended, since it destroys the bow when you die

That is the full combat bow. If you play mostly survival and hate crafting arrows, take Infinity. If you play with a steady supply of arrows and want a bow that repairs itself from experience, take Mending. Both are excellent. You cannot have both, so choose based on how you actually play.

Every bow enchantment, explained

Power V

Power increases arrow damage, and Power V is the maximum level. It is the single biggest damage upgrade on a bow, and it works on every shot. Always put Power on a combat bow before anything else. Without Power, even a fully enchanted bow feels weak against armored mobs and players.

Punch II

Punch knocks the target back when an arrow hits. Punch II is the maximum level, and it is excellent for defence: it pushes skeletons, zombies and pillagers away, and it can knock a player off a ledge or out of position. It is less useful for hunting, where knockback can push prey away, but for combat it is a clear win.

Flame I

Flame sets arrows alight, so the target burns for a few seconds after the hit. Burn damage adds up, especially against mobs with no armor, and it can cook food drops from animals. Flame only has one level, so there is no Flame II to chase.

Unbreaking III

Unbreaking gives each use a chance not to consume durability. Unbreaking III is the maximum level, and it roughly quadruples how long a bow lasts in practice. It pairs well with both Infinity and Mending, and it should be on every bow you plan to keep.

Infinity I

Infinity lets you shoot unlimited arrows as long as you carry at least one arrow in your inventory. It does not work with tipped arrows in the usual way, and it cannot be combined with Mending. Infinity is perfect for long fights, raids and exploration, where running out of arrows would end the adventure early.

Mending I

Mending repairs the bow using experience orbs you collect. Hold the bow, or keep it in your hand while you gain experience, and the bow repairs itself instead of adding levels to your bar. Mending is perfect if you farm experience often, or if you already carry plenty of arrows and do not need Infinity.

Curse of Vanishing

Curse of Vanishing destroys the item when you die, instead of dropping it. It has no benefit in normal play, and it cannot be removed on an anvil. Skip it unless you are building a themed map or a joke item.

What will not combine

The most important conflict for the best bow enchantments in minecraft is Infinity versus Mending. You can put one on a bow, but never both. If you try to combine an Infinity bow with a Mending book on an anvil, the game will refuse the combination.

Other rules are simpler. You cannot stack the same enchantment twice to go past its maximum level, so two Power III books do not make Power VI on an anvil in the normal way (combining two books of the same level raises the level by one, up to the maximum). You also cannot put a sword only enchantment, like Sharpness, on a bow. Use an enchanting table or an anvil, and check the result before you spend levels.

A bow also cannot use Multishot or Piercing, which are crossbow enchantments. If you love crossbows, that is a different build, and it deserves its own guide.

The cheapest anvil order

Anvil costs rise with each use, and a bow that has already been combined several times becomes very expensive to repair or upgrade. The cheapest way to build the best bow enchantments in minecraft is to combine books first, then put the finished book set on a fresh bow in as few steps as possible.

A practical order that works well:

  1. Combine Power books up to Power V on their own.
  2. Combine Punch books up to Punch II on their own.
  3. Combine Unbreaking books up to Unbreaking III on their own.
  4. Combine the smaller books together in pairs, keeping the most expensive book for last where possible.
  5. Apply the combined set to a new, unenchanted bow.
  6. Add Infinity or Mending as the final step, on a bow that has been combined as few times as possible.

If a bow says "Too Expensive" on the anvil, it has been combined too many times. In survival, that bow is effectively finished, so it is better to start a fresh bow than to keep paying rising costs. Keep a backup bow for daily use, and save your maxed bow for fights that matter.

How to get these enchantments

Enchanting table

An enchanting table with bookshelves around it can roll Power, Punch, Flame, Unbreaking and Infinity directly, with luck and levels. Mending cannot be rolled on an enchanting table, so you will need another source for that one.

Villager trading

Librarian villagers sell enchanted books, and resetting their trades by breaking and replacing a lectern can reroll the book on offer. This is the most reliable way to get exact books like Power V or Mending I, though it takes time and emeralds. It is also the method most experienced players use for a maxed bow.

Fishing, loot chests and raids

Fishing with a Luck of the Sea rod, looting dungeons, temples, mineshafts and trial chambers, and clearing raids can all drop enchanted bows and books. These are fun, but random, so treat them as bonuses, not a plan. If you get a good bow early, use it and upgrade it later, rather than waiting for a perfect drop.

Grindstone

A grindstone removes enchantments from a bow and returns some experience, which is useful if you find a bow with a curse or a bad mix. It cannot remove curses, so a Curse of Vanishing bow stays cursed. Use the grindstone to clean up loot bows before you rebuild them.

Power bow versus Infinity bow: which should you build first?

If you are early in a survival world, build a Power IV or Power V bow with Unbreaking first, and add Infinity when you find it. Damage and durability matter more than a perfect combo, and a simple Power bow already handles most early fights.

If you play on a server or in a team, Infinity becomes more valuable, because long fights burn through arrows fast. On {{SERVER_NAME}} Survival, for example, an Infinity bow means you can defend a base or join a raid without carrying stacks of arrows. Mending, on the other hand, shines in long term worlds where you farm experience every day and want one bow to last for months.

There is no wrong choice here. The best bow enchantments in minecraft are the ones that match your routine, and both Infinity and Mending bows are strong enough for endgame play.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Putting Mending and Infinity on the same plan, then discovering they cannot combine.
  • Enchanting a nearly broken bow, then paying high anvil costs to repair it.
  • Skipping Unbreaking, then watching a great bow break in the middle of a fight.
  • Using Punch on a hunting bow, where knockback pushes animals out of range.
  • Forgetting a shield or a melee weapon, because even the best bow is weak at close range.

Keep your bow as a ranged tool, not your only weapon. A sword or axe for close fights, a shield for skeletons, and a bow for distance is a balanced loadout that works in almost every situation.

FAQ

What are the best bow enchantments in minecraft for a beginner?

Power V, Unbreaking III and Infinity I are the simplest strong combo. They give you damage, durability and unlimited arrows, without needing a Mending farm or a complex anvil plan.

Can a bow have both Infinity and Mending?

No. Infinity and Mending are mutually exclusive on a bow. You must pick one. Infinity suits long fights and exploration, while Mending suits players who gain experience often and carry plenty of arrows.

Is Flame worth it on a bow?

Yes, in most cases. Flame adds burn damage, it only takes one enchantment slot, and it can cook animal drops. It is less useful against fire resistant mobs, but it rarely hurts to have it.

How do I repair a maxed bow without losing enchantments?

Use an anvil with another bow, or use Mending with experience orbs. Do not use a grindstone, because it removes enchantments. If the anvil says "Too Expensive", start a fresh bow with your saved books instead.

Should I enchant a bow or a crossbow?

Bows shoot faster and are better for sustained damage, while crossbows hit harder per shot and can use Multishot and Piercing. For most survival players, a maxed bow is the safer first choice, and a crossbow is a fun second weapon later.

Build your bow, then test it

Now you know the best bow enchantments in minecraft, the maxed out combo, what will not combine, and the cheapest way to build it. Start with Power and Unbreaking, add Punch and Flame when you can, then finish with Infinity or Mending based on how you play.

Then test it where it counts. Join a Survival session on {{SERVER_NAME}}, bring your new bow to a raid or a base defence, and see how it feels in a real fight. Share your build with other players on {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}, and tell us which finish you picked: Infinity or Mending? Your answer might help the next player choose their own maxed bow.

Minecraft House Blueprints: 10 Easy Houses & Layouts

Oct 29, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Intro

If you stare at an empty plot and have no idea where to put the first block, minecraft house blueprints are the fastest fix. A good blueprint tells you the footprint, the wall height, where the door goes, and roughly how many blocks you need, so you can build with confidence instead of tearing walls down three times. This guide collects 10 easy minecraft house blueprints, from a first-night hut to a modern glass house, each with a simple materials list and a step-by-step layout you can follow in Survival or Creative.

Every build below uses common blocks, keeps the footprint small, and works on Java and Bedrock. Sizes are given in blocks, and you can scale any house up by adding one block to each side if you want more room.

How to Read Minecraft House Blueprints

Most minecraft house blueprints follow the same simple logic. Start with the footprint, which is the rectangle of blocks on the ground. Then build the walls up to a set height, usually 3 or 4 blocks. Then add the roof, the door, windows, and light sources. Interior rooms come last, because moving a bed or a chest is much easier than moving a wall.

A few habits make every blueprint easier. First, count your materials before you start, and gather about 10 percent extra for mistakes. Second, place torches or lanterns early, so mobs cannot spawn inside your half-built house at night. Third, build the frame first and fill the walls second, so you can see the shape before you commit blocks.

1. The First-Night Hut (5 by 4)

This is the fastest of all minecraft house blueprints, and it exists for one job: keeping you alive on night one. The footprint is 5 blocks long and 4 blocks wide, with walls 3 blocks high and a flat roof of dirt or planks.

Materials: about 40 planks, 1 door, 1 crafting table, 1 furnace, 1 bed, and 4 torches. Build the rectangle, add the door on a short side, put the bed in a corner, and light every corner. It is ugly, and that is fine. You can upgrade it later or keep it as a storage shed.


Alt text: Small starter house interior with bed and furnace for minecraft house blueprints

2. The Classic Oak Cottage (7 by 5)

The oak cottage is the most popular starter base in the game, and one of the most reused minecraft house blueprints for good reason. The footprint is 7 by 5, walls are 3 blocks high, and the roof is a simple pitched roof made of stairs, with a one-block overhang on each side.

Materials: about 2 stacks of oak planks, 1 stack of oak stairs, 20 cobblestone for the foundation, 8 glass panes, 1 door, and 8 torches. Layout: door in the middle of a long side, bed in one corner, crafting area in the opposite corner, and chests along the back wall. Add a small porch of slabs in front of the door, and the whole build looks finished.

3. The Modern Glass House (9 by 7)

Modern builds look harder than they are, because they use flat roofs and big windows instead of complex shapes. This blueprint is 9 by 7, with walls 4 blocks high, a flat roof with a one-block overhang, and glass panes on at least two sides.

Materials: about 1 stack of white concrete or quartz blocks, 1 stack of glass panes, 40 dark oak or spruce planks for accents, 20 slabs for the roof edge, and 10 lanterns. Layout: open-plan living space, kitchen corner with furnaces, bedroom behind a half-wall of planks, and a small balcony of slabs on one side. Keep the glass on the side that faces your best view, and use lanterns instead of torches to keep the clean look.


Alt text: Modern glass house with flat roof and large windows for minecraft house blueprints

4. The Farmhouse With Crops (9 by 6)

A farmhouse earns its keep. The house itself is 9 by 6, and a fenced garden of 9 by 5 sits beside it, with rows of wheat, carrots, and potatoes, plus a water channel down the middle.

Materials: about 2 stacks of spruce or oak planks, 1 stack of fences, 1 stack of stairs for the roof, 1 composter, 1 water bucket, and seeds. Layout: kitchen and storage on the ground floor, bedroom upstairs under the pitched roof, and the garden door opening straight onto the crops. A composter near the garden turns spare seeds into bone meal, which speeds up every harvest.

5. The Underground Bunker Base (8 by 8)

If you like safety more than views, dig down. The bunker is an 8 by 8 room dug 3 blocks below the surface, with a ladder or stair entrance hidden under a trapdoor.

Materials: about 1 stack of stone bricks or deepslate bricks for lining, 1 ladder, 1 trapdoor, 8 torches, and chests. Layout: entrance shaft in one corner, storage wall opposite, bed and enchanting corner on the far side, and a small farm room with water and glowstone if you want to stay underground longer. Mobs cannot see you, phantoms cannot reach you, and the surface stays clear for farms.

6. The Treehouse (6 by 6 Platform)

Treehouses are fun, cheap, and safe from most ground mobs. Pick a large oak or jungle tree, and build a 6 by 6 platform around the trunk, about 8 blocks above the ground.

Materials: about 1 stack of planks, 40 fences for railings, 1 ladder, 1 trapdoor for the floor entrance, and 6 torches. Layout: platform with fence railings on all open edges, a small hut of 4 by 4 on one half, and a chest and crafting table on the other half. Add a second platform later for a bedroom, connected by a plank bridge, and you have a growing treetop base.

7. The Mountain Cabin (8 by 6)

Cabins suit snowy and mountain biomes, where stone and spruce look natural. The footprint is 8 by 6, walls are 3 blocks high, and the roof is a steep pitched roof of spruce stairs, which sheds the snowy look nicely.

Materials: about 2 stacks of spruce planks, 1 stack of spruce stairs, 1 stack of cobblestone or stone bricks for the chimney, 1 campfire for the fireplace, and 8 lanterns. Layout: fireplace on one short wall, bed in the far corner, storage along the long wall, and a small porch with a view over the valley. Add snow layers on the roof edge for a cozy winter finish.

8. The Desert Sandstone House (7 by 5)

Desert builds should use local blocks, and sandstone is perfect. The footprint is 7 by 5, walls are 3 blocks high, and the roof is flat with a sandstone slab edge.

Materials: about 1 stack of sandstone, half a stack of cut sandstone for trim, 8 glass panes, 1 acacia door, and 8 torches. Layout: cool interior with a small indoor garden of cactus in pots, storage along one wall, and a shaded porch of slabs outside the door. Keep the palette to sandstone, cut sandstone, and acacia wood, and the house will blend beautifully with the biome.

9. The Small Glass Dome (5 by 5)

An underwater or lakeside glass dome is a great showpiece, and the small version is easier than it looks. Build a 5 by 5 glass box, 3 blocks high, on a lakebed or in a dug-out pond, with a door of glass or an entrance tunnel from the shore.

Materials: about 1 stack of glass blocks, 20 planks for the floor and furniture, 1 door, and 4 sea lanterns or glowstone blocks for light. Layout: bed and storage inside, a few potted plants for color, and a bubble column entrance if you want to get fancy later. Build the glass shell first while holding a water breathing potion or with doors placed to create air pockets, and the rest is simple furnishing.

10. The Cozy Village House (9 by 7)

The last of these minecraft house blueprints copies the village style, which is ideal if you want your base to fit in with nearby villagers. The footprint is 9 by 7, with a pitched roof, a small front garden, and a path of slabs to the door.

Materials: about 2 stacks of oak planks, 1 stack of oak stairs, 1 stack of cobblestone for the foundation, 10 glass panes, 1 flower pot or two, and 8 torches. Layout: living area by the door, bedroom at the back, storage room on one side, and a garden of flowers and a fence outside. This style also works well as a trading outpost if you add a lectern or a workstation for a villager.

Tips for Customizing Any Blueprint

Once you have built one of these minecraft house blueprints, make it yours. Swap the wood type to match your biome, add a basement for storage, extend the roof overhang by one block for shade, or add a second floor by repeating the wall pattern. Lighting matters as much as shape, so mix torches, lanterns, and glowstone to keep every room bright and mob-free.

Keep a chest of spare planks, stairs, and glass near your build site. Running out of one block mid-roof is the most common reason a build stalls, and a spare chest fixes it.

FAQ

What are the easiest minecraft house blueprints for beginners?

The first-night hut, the classic oak cottage, and the farmhouse are the easiest starting points. They use common blocks, small footprints, and simple pitched roofs, so you can finish them in one play session.

How many blocks do I need for a starter house?

A small starter house of 7 by 5 needs roughly 2 stacks of planks, 1 stack of stairs for the roof, plus glass, a door, and torches. Gather about 10 percent extra for mistakes and repairs.

Do minecraft house blueprints work on both Java and Bedrock?

Yes. All 10 blueprints in this guide use standard blocks and shapes that work on both editions. Redstone or farm mechanics may differ between editions, but house shapes do not.

How do I stop mobs spawning inside my house?

Light every room so no dark corners remain, and light the roof and porch too. Torches, lanterns, and glowstone all work, and a well-lit house stays safe even on hard difficulty.

Final Word

The best of these minecraft house blueprints is the one you actually finish, so start small, claim your land, and build the oak cottage or the farmhouse first. Once the basics are up, add a second floor, a garden, or a modern wing, and your starter hut can grow into a base you are proud of. Best Crossbow Enchantments in Minecraft: Max Combo

Oct 30, 2026
joynalbokhsho

The crossbow is Minecraft's hardest hitting ranged weapon, and the best crossbow enchantments in minecraft turn it from a slow, single shot tool into a fast, multi arrow machine. A well enchanted crossbow can one shot many mobs, clear a pillager outpost from a distance, and hold its own in PvP. The problem is that crossbow enchantments conflict with each other, and picking the wrong combination wastes levels and books. This guide ranks every crossbow enchantment, gives you the maxed out combo, and shows the cheapest anvil order to build it.

Why the Crossbow Deserves Its Own Build

Bows are faster and easier to enchant, but crossbows hit harder per shot and can be preloaded, which means you can fire instantly when a fight starts. You can carry a loaded crossbow in your off hand, swap to it mid fight, and fire without any draw time. That trick alone makes the crossbow a favorite for PvP players and for anyone exploring pillager outposts and trial chambers.

Crossbows also use fireworks as ammunition, which opens up a whole different playstyle, and that is part of why the best crossbow enchantments in minecraft matter so much: the right build changes what the weapon can do. Add the right enchantments and the crossbow becomes a weapon that bows simply cannot match for burst damage.

The Best Crossbow Enchantments in Minecraft, Ranked

Here is the full ranking of the best crossbow enchantments in minecraft, from must have to situational, so you can decide what matters for your playstyle.

Quick Charge III is the single most important crossbow enchantment. It cuts the loading time from 1.25 seconds down to 0.25 seconds at level III, which means you spend far less time exposed while reloading. Every crossbow build starts here, no exceptions.

Multishot is the second must have for most players. It fires three arrows or rockets at once, at the cost of only one arrow from your inventory, though it does use three durability points per shot. For mob farms, outposts, and crowd control, Multishot is unmatched.

Piercing IV is the alternative to Multishot, and the two cannot be combined. Piercing lets one arrow pass through up to four extra entities, so a single shot can hit a whole line of mobs. It is brilliant in tight corridors, dungeons, and trial chambers where enemies line up.

Unbreaking III is the durability workhorse. Crossbows have 465 durability, and Multishot eats through it fast, so Unbreaking III roughly quadruples your shots before repair. Pair it with Mending and your crossbow becomes nearly permanent.

Mending is the long term investment. It repairs the crossbow with experience orbs you pick up, so you never need to craft a replacement. Mending and Infinity cannot both go on a bow, but crossbows have no Infinity, so Mending is a free win here.

The Maxed Out Combo

For most players, the best crossbow enchantments in minecraft combine into this single build: Quick Charge III, Multishot, Unbreaking III, and Mending. This is the crowd control build, perfect for survival, outposts, and general exploration. It loads fast, fires three arrows at once, lasts for ages, and repairs itself as you play.

  • Hotbar Slot 1 (#0): Crossbow Standby (Enchantments: Unbreaking III, Mending, Quick Charge III, Multishot)
  • Hotbar Slot 2 (#1): 64x Arrow
  • Hotbar Slot 3 (#2): 64x Firework Rocket
  • Hotbar Slot 4 (#3): Totem Of Undying

If you prefer precision and corridor fighting, swap Multishot for Piercing IV and keep the other three. That build is: Quick Charge III, Piercing IV, Unbreaking III, and Mending. It is weaker against spread out groups but stronger when enemies line up, and it uses less durability per shot than Multishot.

  • Hotbar Slot 2 (#1): 64x Arrow
  • Hotbar Slot 3 (#2): 16x Ender Pearl
  • Hotbar Slot 4 (#3): Totem Of Undying

A third option is the firework build for PvP and fun: Quick Charge III, Multishot, Unbreaking III, and Mending, loaded with firework rockets instead of arrows. Firework rockets deal splash damage and ignore the Multishot arrow cost rules in a useful way, since one rocket fires three rockets with Multishot. This is expensive to maintain, but it is the highest burst damage a crossbow can deal.

Multishot vs Piercing: Which One Should You Pick?

This is the one real choice in crossbow building, because Multishot and Piercing are mutually exclusive. Pick Multishot if you fight groups, explore outposts, or play PvP where enemies rarely line up neatly. Pick Piercing if you fight in corridors, dungeons, and trial chambers, or if you want to save durability and arrows.

A practical tip for players comparing the best crossbow enchantments in minecraft: build one of each if you have the books. A Multishot crossbow for open combat and a Piercing crossbow for dungeons covers every situation, and both share the same Quick Charge, Unbreaking, and Mending core. Two crossbows also let you preload both and fire twice in a row without reloading, which is a huge advantage in a tough fight.

Cheapest Anvil Order

Anvil costs rise fast if you combine books in the wrong order, and the prior work penalty can make a crossbow too expensive to repair. The cheapest order is to combine the cheapest books first, then add the result to the crossbow, saving Mending for last if you can.

A good order is: first combine Quick Charge III with Unbreaking III into one book, then combine Multishot or Piercing IV with Mending into a second book, then apply the first combined book to the crossbow, then the second. This keeps the prior work penalty low and usually leaves the final crossbow repairable for a reasonable XP cost. Always check the anvil cost before confirming, and if it says "Too Expensive", split the combination differently rather than wasting the books.

You can get the books for the best crossbow enchantments in minecraft from librarian villagers, enchanting tables, loot chests in dungeons and trial chambers, and fishing. Librarian trading is the most reliable route for Quick Charge III and Multishot, so set up a librarian hall if you plan to enchant several crossbows.

Crossbow Tips for Survival and PvP

Preload your crossbow before a fight, and keep a second loaded crossbow in your inventory for an instant follow up shot. Use arrows for everyday combat and save firework rockets for bosses, PvP, and emergencies, since rockets are costly to craft in bulk. Keep a stack of arrows in your inventory, because a crossbow without ammunition is just a heavy stick.

In PvP, Quick Charge III is non negotiable in any list of the best crossbow enchantments in minecraft: a slow crossbow gets you killed while reloading. In survival, Mending matters more than raw damage, since a crossbow you can keep forever beats a slightly stronger one that breaks. And on servers like {{SERVER_NAME}}, a loaded crossbow is a great defensive tool for base protection, since you can fire instantly from behind cover.

FAQ

Can Multishot and Piercing go on the same crossbow?

No, they are mutually exclusive. You must pick one or the other for each crossbow.

Does Quick Charge work with firework rockets?

Yes, Quick Charge speeds up loading for both arrows and firework rockets.

What is the best crossbow for PvP?

Quick Charge III, Multishot, Unbreaking III, and Mending, loaded with arrows for reliability or firework rockets for burst damage.

How do I get Mending on a crossbow?

Mending comes from librarian villagers, loot chests, fishing, or raid drops. Apply it with an anvil, since enchanting tables do not offer Mending.

Ready to Build Yours?

Now you know the best crossbow enchantments in minecraft, the maxed out combo, and the cheapest way to build it. Start with Quick Charge III, pick Multishot or Piercing for your playstyle, and add Unbreaking and Mending to finish the build. Then take your crossbow out on {{SERVER_NAME}}, preload it before your next adventure, and see how fast it clears a fight. Share your build in the {{SERVER_NAME}} Discord and compare notes with other ranged players.

Best Armor Enchantments in Minecraft: Full Protection

Oct 27, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Intro

A great sword wins fights, but great armor lets you survive them. If you want the toughest set in Survival, you need the best armor enchantments in minecraft on every piece, not just a lucky helmet or chestplate. This guide breaks down the best armor enchantments in minecraft piece by piece, explains which protection types conflict, and gives you the full maxed-out set so you can walk into the Nether, the End, and deep caves with confidence.

The Maxed-Out Armor Set

Here is the target set for the best armor enchantments in minecraft:

  • Helmet: Protection IV, Respiration III, Aqua Affinity, Unbreaking III, Mending
  • Chestplate: Protection IV, Unbreaking III, Mending (plus Thorns III if you want it, see below)
  • Leggings: Protection IV, Swift Sneak III, Unbreaking III, Mending
  • Boots: Protection IV, Feather Falling IV, Depth Strider III, Soul Speed III, Unbreaking III, Mending

Every piece carries Protection IV, Unbreaking III, and Mending. Those three are the backbone of the best armor enchantments in minecraft, and the piece-specific enchantments on top of them are what make the set truly complete.

Protection: Pick One Type Per Piece

Protection IV is the best general choice, and it is the default for the best armor enchantments in minecraft. It reduces all types of damage, from melee hits and arrows to explosions and fire, which makes it useful everywhere.

The specialist options are Fire Protection IV, Blast Protection IV, and Projectile Protection IV. Each one reduces its own damage type more than Protection does, but each one is weaker against everything else. The key rule is that you can only have one protection type on each armor piece: Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection, and Projectile Protection are mutually exclusive.

For a main set, use Protection IV on all four pieces. Build specialist pieces later if you need them, for example a Fire Protection chestplate for long Nether trips, or a Blast Protection set for creeper farms. Never mix protection types on the same piece, because the anvil will simply refuse the combination.

Durability: Unbreaking and Mending

Unbreaking III gives each armor piece a chance to avoid losing durability when you take damage, and Mending repairs armor using XP orbs you pick up. Together, they are the best durability setup in the game, and no guide to the best armor enchantments in minecraft is complete without them.

Mending on armor works while you wear it, so XP from mining, smelting, farming, and mob kills slowly repairs your set as you play. If several worn pieces carry Mending, the game picks one at random for each XP orb, so a full Mending set repairs evenly over time. Like Mending on tools, you cannot get it from an enchanting table. You need a Mending book from a librarian villager, a fishing catch, or loot chests.

Helmet: Respiration and Aqua Affinity

Respiration III lets you breathe underwater much longer, which is essential for ocean monuments, underwater ruins, and building under water. Aqua Affinity removes the mining speed penalty under water, so you can actually break blocks at normal speed while swimming. Both are helmet-only enchantments, and both belong on your main helmet in the best armor enchantments in minecraft.

If you also want a turtle shell helmet, note that it already gives a short water breathing effect on its own, but a diamond or netherite helmet with Respiration III and Aqua Affinity is still the more flexible choice for long underwater work.

Boots: Feather Falling, Depth Strider, and Soul Speed

Boots carry the most movement enchantments, and getting them right changes how you travel. Feather Falling IV greatly reduces fall damage, which saves you from cliffs, End pillars, and bad landings in the Nether. It does not remove fall damage completely, but it turns falls that would kill you into falls you walk away from.

Depth Strider III lets you move much faster under water, which pairs perfectly with a Respiration helmet. Soul Speed III lets you move faster on soul sand and soul soil, which is a huge help in the Nether, especially in soul sand valleys. Soul Speed has a durability cost on boots, so Mending and Unbreaking matter even more on a Soul Speed pair.

One conflict to remember: Depth Strider and Frost Walker are mutually exclusive on boots. Depth Strider is the better pick for most players, because Frost Walker turns water into ice under your feet, which can be awkward in farms and dangerous near deep water. Pick Depth Strider for your main boots, and keep Frost Walker only as a fun second pair.

Leggings: Swift Sneak

Swift Sneak III increases your movement speed while sneaking, up to nearly normal walking speed at level III. It is a leggings-only enchantment, and it comes from ancient city loot, not from an enchanting table. Swift Sneak is especially useful in the Deep Dark, where sneaking quietly matters, and in any build where you crouch on edges or scaffolding. It is a smaller upgrade than Protection or Mending, but it completes the best armor enchantments in minecraft for leggings.

Thorns: Worth It or Not?

Thorns III damages attackers when they hit you, which sounds great, but it comes with real costs. Thorns drains extra durability from your armor every time it triggers, and it can push mobs away or trigger effects you did not want, such as angering piglins or damaging a mob you were trying to keep alive. Many experienced players leave Thorns off their main set, or put it only on the chestplate.

If you like Thorns, add it to the chestplate only, and make sure that piece has Unbreaking III and Mending to handle the extra durability loss. If you prefer control and long armor life, skip Thorns entirely. Your set is still maxed out without it, and it will last longer.

The Cheapest Anvil Order

Armor follows the same anvil rules as tools: costs rise with each step, and a bad order can make the final step too expensive. For the best armor enchantments in minecraft, use this approach on each piece:

  1. Enchant the armor piece at the table, or start with a clean diamond or netherite piece.
  2. Combine enchanted books together first, cheapest first, before putting anything on the armor.
  3. Add the expensive books, such as Protection IV or Mending, in the final merge if you can, so the prior work penalty stays low.
  4. If a step says "Too Expensive," stop and rebuild with a better order instead of wasting XP.

Because armor has four pieces, you will repeat this process four times. Keep spare books, especially Protection IV and Unbreaking III, so one bad combine does not stall the whole set.

How to Get Each Enchantment

  • Enchanting table (level 30, with 15 bookshelves): Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection, Projectile Protection, Unbreaking, Respiration, Aqua Affinity, Feather Falling, Depth Strider, Soul Speed.
  • Librarian villagers: trade for specific books, including Mending, Protection IV, and Unbreaking III.
  • Fishing and loot chests: a chance at Mending and other treasure enchantments.
  • Ancient cities: the only source of Swift Sneak books.
  • Grindstone: removes unwanted enchantments from armor, but destroys the item in the process and returns only some XP.

Enchanting books instead of armor gives you control over the final result. Store good books, combine them in the right order, and put the finished book on the piece you want to keep.

Using Your Maxed Armor on {{SERVER_NAME}}

Once your set is complete, take it somewhere that tests it. Join the {{SERVER_NAME}} Survival world and explore deep caves, Nether fortresses, and End cities with real confidence. {{SERVER_NAME}} has run as a {{SERVER_REGION}}i Minecraft community since 2018, with Survival and Bedwars among its game modes, and land claims use the GriefPrevention plugin with a golden shovel. Join through PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and find the community on Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}.

FAQ

What are the best armor enchantments in minecraft for a full set?

Protection IV, Unbreaking III, and Mending on every piece, plus Respiration III and Aqua Affinity on the helmet, Swift Sneak III on leggings, and Feather Falling IV, Depth Strider III, and Soul Speed III on boots.

Can you put Protection and Fire Protection on the same piece?

No. Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection, and Projectile Protection are mutually exclusive, so each armor piece can only carry one protection type.

Is Thorns worth it on armor?

It depends on your playstyle. Thorns damages attackers, but it drains extra durability and can cause unwanted effects. Many players skip it or use it only on the chestplate.

How do you get Mending on armor?

Mending does not come from the enchanting table. Get Mending books from librarian villager trades, fishing, or loot chests, then combine them onto your armor at an anvil.

Final Word

The best armor enchantments in minecraft are not complicated, but they do take planning. Start with Protection IV, Unbreaking III, and Mending on every piece, add the movement and breathing enchantments that fit how you play, and combine books in an order that keeps anvil costs down. Build this set once, keep it repaired with Mending, and it will carry you through every dimension in the game. Join {{SERVER_NAME}} at PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and show off your full set on Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}.

Best Axe Enchantments in Minecraft: Maxed-Out Combo

Nov 1, 2026
joynalbokhsho

The axe is the most underrated tool in Minecraft. It chops wood faster than anything, strips logs, breaks pumpkins and melons in a snap, and in Java Edition it hits harder than a sword. The right enchantments turn a plain diamond or netherite axe into a tool you will carry every day. This guide ranks the best axe enchantments in minecraft, explains what each one does, and gives you the cheapest anvil order for a maxed-out axe.

Best Axe Enchantments in Minecraft: The Maxed-Out Combo

The best all-round axe carries Sharpness V, Efficiency V, Unbreaking III, Mending, and either Silk Touch or Fortune III. That is the full maxed-out combo, and it covers combat, chopping, and long-term durability in one tool. Silk Touch and Fortune cannot go on the same axe, so you have to pick one. Most players choose Silk Touch for their main axe, because it lets you collect grass blocks, bookshelves, and ore blocks intact, and they keep a separate Fortune axe for farming drops. If you mostly chop wood and fight mobs, Silk Touch is the safer first pick.

What Each Enchantment Does

Sharpness V

Sharpness adds melee damage, up to 3 extra damage at level V on Java Edition. On Java, axes deal more base damage than swords, so a Sharpness V netherite axe is one of the hardest-hitting melee weapons in the game. On Bedrock, axes do not get the same combat bonus, but Sharpness still makes your axe a decent weapon when you are caught without a sword. For a tool you carry everywhere, Sharpness is the damage enchantment to choose.

Efficiency V

Efficiency is the reason your axe feels fast. At level V, it chops wood, strips logs, and breaks other axe-friendly blocks much faster. Any list of the best axe enchantments in minecraft puts Efficiency near the top for builders. Combined with Haste from a beacon, an Efficiency V axe can clear a forest in minutes. If you build a lot, Efficiency V is non-negotiable. Without it, even a netherite axe feels slow compared to what it could be.

Unbreaking III

Unbreaking III gives each use a 75 percent chance to not consume durability, which roughly quadruples the life of your axe. It is cheap, it goes on everything, and it pairs perfectly with Mending. Every maxed-out tool should have it, and the axe is no exception.

Mending

Mending repairs your axe using experience orbs you pick up, as long as the axe is in your hand or off-hand when you collect the experience. With Mending and Unbreaking III together, an axe can last for your whole playthrough if you collect experience regularly from mining, farming, or mob kills. Get Mending from villager trading, fishing, or loot chests, since it cannot be rolled on an enchanting table.

Silk Touch or Fortune III

Silk Touch lets you mine blocks in their original form: grass blocks, stone, glass, bookshelves, and ores drop as blocks instead of items. Fortune III increases drops from blocks like coal, diamonds, and crops, and it boosts drops from pumpkins and melons when you break them with an axe. Pick Silk Touch for your main axe and Fortune III for a second axe if you farm a lot. Never try to put both on one axe, because the game will not allow it.

Enchantments That Do Not Combine

A few combinations are blocked, and knowing them saves you wasted levels. Sharpness, Smite, and Bane of Arthropods are mutually exclusive, so you can only have one damage enchantment on an axe. Sharpness is the best general choice because it works on all mobs, while Smite only boosts damage against undead and Bane of Arthropods only helps against spiders, silverfish, and similar mobs. Silk Touch and Fortune are also mutually exclusive, as noted above. Everything else in the maxed-out combo stacks freely.

There are also enchantments that technically fit on an axe but are not worth it. Knockback on an axe sounds fun, but it pushes mobs away and slows your chopping rhythm in combat. Fire Aspect does not apply to axes at all. Looting only works on swords, so do not waste books trying to add it to an axe. Stick to the combo above and your levels go further.

How to Enchant Your Axe

Start with an enchanting table surrounded by 15 bookshelves for level 30 enchantments. When you plan the best axe enchantments in minecraft for your own tool, start with the table roll and fix the gaps with books. Enchant a fresh diamond or netherite axe and take the best roll you get, then fix the missing pieces with enchanted books from villagers or fishing. The anvil is where the maxed-out axe comes together. Combine books onto the axe one at a time, starting with the cheapest books, because anvil costs grow with each operation. The "too expensive" limit is real, so plan your order before you start combining.

A cheap anvil order that works well is: first combine Efficiency and Unbreaking onto the axe, then add Mending, then Sharpness, and finally Silk Touch or Fortune last. If you are combining two enchanted axes instead, combine the one with fewer enchantments into the one with more. Keep a grindstone nearby for mistakes: it removes enchantments and returns some experience, which helps when a random table roll gives you something useless.

Axe Combat Tips

On Java Edition, axes have a slower attack speed than swords but deal more damage per hit, and a charged axe hit can disable an opponent's shield for a few seconds. Even with the best axe enchantments in minecraft, timing matters on Java: time your swings instead of spam-clicking, because a fully charged hit deals far more damage. That makes the axe a strong PvP and PvE weapon, especially with Sharpness V. On Bedrock Edition, axes have no cooldown and no shield-disable effect, so they behave more like fast tools, and a sword is usually the better dedicated weapon there. Either way, an enchanted axe is a fine backup weapon, and it saves you an inventory slot when you are out chopping.

FAQ

What are the best axe enchantments in minecraft for a first axe?

For your first good axe, aim for Efficiency III or higher, Unbreaking III, and Mending if you can trade for it. Add Sharpness when you have the books. That combination chops fast, lasts long, and still works in a fight, which is exactly what a daily-carry axe needs.

Should I put Smite or Bane of Arthropods on an axe?

Only if you have a dedicated axe for one mob type, such as a Smite axe for a wither skeleton farm. For a general axe, Sharpness is better because it boosts damage against every mob, not just one group.

Can an axe have both Silk Touch and Fortune?

No. Silk Touch and Fortune are mutually exclusive on every tool, including axes. Make two axes if you want both effects, or pick Silk Touch for your main axe and use a Fortune pickaxe for ore farming.

Is a netherite axe worth enchanting?

Do the best axe enchantments in minecraft work the same on Java and Bedrock?

Mostly yes. Efficiency, Unbreaking, Mending, Silk Touch, and Fortune work the same on both editions. The enchanting advice in this guide applies to both editions.

Best Sword Enchantments in Minecraft: Maxed-Out Combo

Oct 27, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Intro

If you want the strongest melee weapon in the game, you need to know the best sword enchantments in minecraft before you spend a single level. A plain diamond or netherite sword is fine for the early game, but the right enchantments turn it into a weapon that hits harder, drops more loot, repairs itself, and lasts through long fights. This guide gives you the full maxed-out combo for the best sword enchantments in minecraft, explains what will not combine, and shows the cheapest anvil order so you do not waste XP.

The Maxed-Out Sword Combo

Here is the best all-round sword in Survival, and the target for the best sword enchantments in minecraft:

  • Sharpness V
  • Sweeping Edge III (Java Edition only)
  • Looting III
  • Fire Aspect II
  • Knockback II
  • Unbreaking III
  • Mending

That is seven enchantments on one sword. Each one earns its place, and together they cover damage, drops, durability, and crowd control. If you play Bedrock Edition, drop Sweeping Edge, since it does not exist there, and the rest of the combo stays the same.

Damage Enchantments: Sharpness, Smite, and Bane

Sharpness V is the best general damage enchantment, and it is the core of the best sword enchantments in minecraft. It adds extra damage against every mob, from zombies and skeletons to the Ender Dragon and the Wither. That flexibility is why Sharpness beats the specialist options for a main sword.

Smite V and Bane of Arthropods V hit harder against specific mobs. Smite is stronger against undead mobs such as zombies, skeletons, and wither skeletons, while Bane of Arthropods is stronger against spiders, cave spiders, silverfish, and endermites. The catch is that Sharpness, Smite, and Bane of Arthropods are mutually exclusive: a sword can only carry one of them. Keep Sharpness on your main sword, and build a separate Smite sword later if you farm the Wither or run a zombie farm often.

Looting, Fire Aspect, and Knockback

Looting III increases mob drops, which makes it one of the most valuable parts of the best sword enchantments in minecraft. More drops means more gunpowder from creepers, more bones from skeletons, more ender pearls from endermen, and more wither skeleton skulls over time. If you farm anything, Looting pays for itself fast.

Fire Aspect II sets mobs on fire when you hit them, adding damage over time and cooking meat drops from animals automatically. It is handy in combat, but skip it on a sword you use for enderman farming, since burning endermen tend to teleport away.

Knockback II pushes mobs back when you hit them. That distance is useful against creepers and fast melee mobs, and it can save you from being swarmed. Some players dislike Knockback because it pushes mobs out of reach, so if you prefer tight combat, leave it off. It is optional, not essential.

Sweeping Edge: The Java-Only Bonus

Sweeping Edge III increases the damage of the sweep attack, which is the wide swing that hits several mobs at once. If you play Java Edition and fight groups of mobs, Sweeping Edge is a big part of the best sword enchantments in minecraft, because it turns crowded fights into quick work. Bedrock players do not have sweep attacks in the same way, so this enchantment simply does not exist on Bedrock. Do not trade for a Sweeping Edge book on Bedrock, and do not expect to find it in a Bedrock enchanting table.

Durability: Unbreaking and Mending

Unbreaking III gives your sword a chance to avoid losing durability on each hit, which makes it last much longer. Mending is even better: it repairs your sword using XP orbs you pick up, as long as the sword is held or in your main hand. Together, Unbreaking and Mending mean a good sword can last your whole playthrough. That is why every list of the best sword enchantments in minecraft includes both.

To get Mending, you cannot use an enchanting table. You need a Mending book from a librarian villager trade, a fishing catch, or loot from chests in places such as dungeons, temples, and End cities. A librarian with a Mending trade is the most reliable route, so protect that villager and keep emeralds ready.

What Will Not Combine

Enchantment conflicts waste books and XP, so check this list before you combine anything for the best sword enchantments in minecraft:

  • Sharpness, Smite, and Bane of Arthropods: pick only one.
  • Sweeping Edge (Java only): no direct conflict, but it is Java only.
  • Fire Aspect and Knockback: these two can combine, so no problem here.
  • Mending and Infinity: this conflict matters for bows, not swords, but never put Infinity on a sword anyway.

Also remember that a sword cannot hold more than the available enchantment slots allow in practice, and each anvil step adds a prior work penalty. Combining in a bad order can make the final step cost too much XP, or even become too expensive to complete.

The Cheapest Anvil Order

Anvil costs grow with each step, so combine the cheapest items first and save the most expensive step for last. A simple order that works well for the best sword enchantments in minecraft is:

  1. Start with your unenchanted diamond or netherite sword.
  2. Combine the two cheapest enchanted books together first, for example Sweeping Edge and Knockback, if you have them as books.
  3. Combine the next pair of books, such as Fire Aspect and Looting.
  4. Add Unbreaking and Mending to the growing book, since these are usually easy to get as books.
  5. Add Sharpness last, or add the Sharpness book to the sword first if Sharpness is your most expensive book, then merge the combined book onto the sword in one final step.

The golden rule is simple: merge books together before merging them onto the sword, and always combine the two cheapest items at each step. If a step says "Too Expensive," stop, get more XP, or rebuild the sword with a better order instead of wasting levels on a dead end. On Java Edition, the anvil caps at 39 levels per operation in Survival, so a bad order can genuinely block you.

How to Get Each Enchantment

  • Enchanting table (level 30, with 15 bookshelves around it): Sharpness, Sweeping Edge, Looting, Fire Aspect, Knockback, Unbreaking. Use lapis lazuli and plenty of XP, and enchant books when you do not want to gamble on a sword directly.
  • Librarian villagers: trade for specific books, including Mending, Sharpness V, and Looting III, if you level up librarians and refresh their trades.
  • Fishing and loot chests: a chance at Mending and other treasure enchantments.
  • Grindstone: use it to remove unwanted enchantments from a sword or book, but note that it destroys the item and returns only some XP.

Enchanting books instead of the sword gives you control. You can store good books, combine them in the right order, and put the finished result on the sword you actually want to keep.

Using Your Maxed Sword on {{SERVER_NAME}}

Once your sword is ready, test it where it counts. Join the {{SERVER_NAME}} Survival world and take it into caves, farms, and boss fights, and see how fast Looting fills your chests. {{SERVER_NAME}} has run as a {{SERVER_REGION}}i Minecraft community since 2018, with Survival and Bedwars among its game modes, and land claims use the GriefPrevention plugin with a golden shovel. Join through PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and find the community on Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}.

FAQ

What are the best sword enchantments in minecraft for a main sword?

Sharpness V, Looting III, Unbreaking III, Mending, Fire Aspect II, and Knockback II, plus Sweeping Edge III on Java Edition. That combo covers damage, drops, and durability in one weapon.

Is Sharpness or Smite better?

Sharpness is better for a main sword because it works against every mob. Smite is better only as a second, specialist sword for undead mobs such as wither skeletons.

Can you put Mending and Unbreaking on the same sword?

Yes. They combine fine, and together they are the best durability setup in the game. Mending repairs with XP, and Unbreaking slows durability loss.

Why is my anvil step too expensive?

Each anvil use adds a prior work penalty, and costs rise fast. Combine books together first, combine the cheapest items first, and keep the final merge as cheap as possible.

Final Word

The best sword enchantments in minecraft are not about luck at the enchanting table. They are about picking Sharpness over the specialist damage options, adding Looting and Mending early, and combining books in an order that keeps XP costs down. Build the combo in this guide, keep a spare set of books, and your sword will carry you from your first cave to the End and beyond. Best Hoe Enchantments in Minecraft: Max Combo

Nov 3, 2026
joynalbokhsho

If you spend any time farming in Minecraft, your hoe deserves the same attention as your sword or pickaxe. A plain hoe tills one block at a time and breaks fast, but a fully enchanted hoe clears fields in seconds, drops extra crops, and lasts almost forever. This guide covers the best hoe enchantments in minecraft, what each one actually does, and the cheapest order to combine them on an anvil so you do not waste levels.

The Best Hoe Enchantments in Minecraft at a Glance

Here is the maxed-out combo for a diamond or netherite hoe:

  • Efficiency V: tills and breaks blocks much faster
  • Fortune III: more drops from crops and other blocks
  • Unbreaking III: the hoe lasts roughly four times longer
  • Mending: repairs the hoe with XP you collect

That is the full set. The best hoe enchantments in minecraft are these four, and nothing else belongs on a farming hoe. Silk Touch is a niche option we cover below, but for most players the four above are the goal.

Efficiency V: The Speed Upgrade

Efficiency is the single biggest quality of life upgrade for a hoe. At Efficiency V, tilling a field feels instant, and harvesting crops, leaves, and other soft blocks goes far quicker. You get Efficiency from an enchanting table at level 30, from librarian villagers, or from loot chests in structures like ancient cities and bastions. Put Efficiency on first in your anvil order, since it is the most common enchantment and the cheapest to add early.

Fortune III: More Crops From Every Harvest

Fortune is what turns a good farm into a great one. Fortune III increases drops from crops like potatoes and carrots, and it also boosts drops from blocks such as glowstone and melons. A Fortune III hoe means fewer replanting rounds and fuller chests, which matters a lot when you are stocking up for a big build or feeding a whole server. Note that Fortune does not work on wheat itself, since wheat drops a fixed amount, but it shines on potatoes, carrots, beetroots, and nether wart.

Unbreaking III: Make It Last

Unbreaking III gives each use only a 25 percent chance of costing durability, which effectively quadruples your hoe's lifespan. This matters because a hoe used on a large farm burns through durability fast, and nobody wants to rebuild a netherite tool. Combine Unbreaking with Mending and your hoe becomes close to permanent.

Mending: The Must Have Finisher

Mending uses XP orbs you pick up to repair the tool in your hand, instead of adding to your XP bar. Hold your hoe while you harvest, trade with villagers, or kill mobs, and it repairs itself as you play. Mending cannot be found on an enchanting table, so you need a librarian villager selling a Mending book, a raid drop, or loot from fishing and structures. It is the last enchantment to add in the anvil order because Mending books are the rarest and the most expensive.

Silk Touch: The Niche Option

Silk Touch lets a hoe pick up blocks whole, like grass blocks, mycelium, or bee nests if you are careful. The catch is that Silk Touch and Fortune cannot sit on the same tool. For a farming hoe, Fortune wins in almost every case, since crop drops matter more than collecting blocks. Only build a separate Silk Touch hoe if you specifically need grass blocks for a build.

What Not to Put on a Hoe

Combat enchantments like Sharpness, Smite, and Bane of Arthropods do not belong on a hoe. They cannot be applied through normal enchanting, and even if you could, a hoe is a terrible weapon. Likewise, do not waste levels on Curse of Vanishing, which destroys the tool when you die. Stick to the four core enchantments and your hoe will serve you for thousands of harvests.

The Cheapest Anvil Order

Anvil costs rise with every combine, so order matters. The cheapest way to build the best hoe enchantments in minecraft is:

  1. Start with a fresh diamond or netherite hoe.
  2. Combine Efficiency V first.
  3. Add Unbreaking III second.
  4. Add Fortune III third.
  5. Add Mending last.

Combining books together before applying them to the tool can also save levels, so if you have two books, merge the cheaper pair first. Avoid adding enchantments one at a time in random order, since the prior work penalty climbs with each anvil use and can make the final combine cost more than 39 levels, which the anvil refuses.

How to Get These Enchantments

The fastest reliable route is villager trading. Cure a zombie villager or breed villagers until you get librarians selling Efficiency, Fortune, Unbreaking, and Mending books, then trade paper, books, or other goods to buy them. The enchanting table is a solid backup for Efficiency, Fortune, and Unbreaking at level 30 with a full bookshelf setup. Fishing with a Luck of the Sea rod and looting end cities are slower but free sources of enchanted books.

FAQ

Can a hoe have Fortune and Silk Touch together?

No. Fortune and Silk Touch are mutually exclusive on every tool, including hoes. Pick Fortune for farming and keep a separate Silk Touch hoe only if you need whole blocks.

Is a netherite hoe worth it?

For a dedicated farmer, yes. Netherite adds durability, works in lava, and never burns in a fire accident. Upgrade a diamond hoe with a netherite ingot at a smithing table after enchanting, so you keep your enchantments.

What is the best hoe enchantment for XP farms?

Mending, without question. When you collect XP from any farm while holding the hoe, Mending repairs it first, so a Mending hoe almost never breaks.

Do hoes need Efficiency for tilling?

Efficiency speeds up tilling and breaking blocks, so it makes large fields far less tedious. It is not required, but once you try Efficiency V you will not go back.

Ready to Farm?

Now that you know the best hoe enchantments in minecraft, build your maxed-out hoe and put it to work. If you play on {{SERVER_NAME}}, bring your enchanted hoe to our Survival world and show off your farm, or ask other players for trading tips on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM. Join us on Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}} to share your farm screenshots, and check /rules before you start building near other players. Happy harvesting, and may your chests always be full.
