A pickaxe is the tool you use more than any other in Minecraft, so its enchantments matter more than almost any other gear choice. The right combination mines faster, drops more resources, and lasts far longer, while the wrong one wastes levels on the anvil or locks you out of better options. This guide covers the best pickaxe enchantments in minecraft, the maxed-out combination for both Fortune and Silk Touch builds, which enchantments cannot combine, and the cheapest order to apply them on the anvil.

The Maxed-Out Pickaxe: Best Pickaxe Enchantments in Minecraft

For a general purpose endgame pickaxe, the strongest combination is Efficiency V, Unbreaking III, Mending, and either Fortune III or Silk Touch. Efficiency V makes mining dramatically faster, Unbreaking III roughly quadruples the tool's effective life, Mending repairs it from experience, and the Fortune or Silk Touch choice decides what you get from each block. No pickaxe can carry both Fortune and Silk Touch, so most serious players build two pickaxes: one Fortune pickaxe for ores and farming, and one Silk Touch pickaxe for moving blocks intact.

Every Enchantment Explained

Here is what each of the best pickaxe enchantments in minecraft does, and why it earns its place.

Efficiency V

Efficiency V is the single biggest speed upgrade. Combined with Haste II from a beacon, it lets you instantly mine stone and deepslate, which transforms large digging projects. Always max this first on a pickaxe you use daily.

Fortune III or Silk Touch: Pick One

Fortune III multiplies drops from ores: a single diamond ore can drop up to four diamonds, and coal, redstone, and lapis drops multiply too. Silk Touch drops the block itself instead, which is perfect for moving ore blocks to a Fortune setup later, or collecting grass, glass, or ice. Because these two conflict, choose based on your current goal, and build the other pickaxe when you can afford it. When players debate the best pickaxe enchantments in minecraft, this choice is usually the heart of the argument.

Unbreaking III

Unbreaking III gives each use a chance to cost no durability, which effectively multiplies your pickaxe's lifespan several times over. It pairs with Mending perfectly: Unbreaking slows damage, Mending repairs it, and together they keep a pickaxe going almost indefinitely.

Mending

Mending repairs your pickaxe from experience orbs while you hold it, so mining, smelting, and killing mobs all top it up. A Mending pickaxe with Unbreaking III rarely needs an anvil visit, which saves levels for other gear. If you have not found a Mending book yet, see our guide on getting one from librarian villagers.

What Will Not Combine

Fortune and Silk Touch conflict, so the anvil will refuse to combine them. Mending conflicts with Infinity, but Infinity only applies to bows, so it never affects a pickaxe. Every other pickaxe enchantment combines freely, which means your only real choice is the Fortune versus Silk Touch decision.

The Cheapest Anvil Order

Anvil costs grow with each use, and the "too expensive" limit can block late combinations, so apply enchantments in the right order. The cheapest approach is to combine books together first, starting with the most expensive book, then apply the combined book to the pickaxe in as few steps as possible. As a rule: combine Efficiency, Fortune or Silk Touch, Unbreaking, and Mending books into as few books as you can, then add them to a fresh pickaxe before you have used the anvil on it before. Adding Mending last to an already heavily worked pickaxe is the most common way players hit the "too expensive" wall, so plan the full combination before you spend your first level. For players chasing the best pickaxe enchantments in minecraft on a budget, this order saves dozens of levels.

Fortune Build vs Silk Touch Build

Use a Fortune III pickaxe for mining ores, farming crops like carrots and potatoes, and gathering glowstone. Use a Silk Touch pickaxe for relocating ore blocks, harvesting glass, ice, and grass blocks, and collecting stone for building. Keep both in your ender chest if you can, and switch based on the job.

Common Mistakes

Do not waste a Fortune pickaxe on plain stone digging, since Fortune only helps ore and crop drops. Do not enchant a pickaxe at the enchanting table hoping for a perfect roll: the table never offers Mending, and its other results are random. Do not combine enchantments one book at a time onto the same pickaxe, or anvil costs will spiral. And do not forget Unbreaking: a fast pickaxe that breaks quickly is worse than a slightly slower one that lasts.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best pickaxe in Minecraft?

A netherite pickaxe with Efficiency V, Unbreaking III, Mending, and Fortune III or Silk Touch is the best all-round pickaxe. Diamond is a strong second choice if you have not reached the Nether yet.

Is Fortune or Silk Touch better?

Fortune is better for gathering resources, Silk Touch is better for moving blocks intact. Most endgame players keep one of each, and the best pickaxe enchantments in minecraft for your world depend on which job you do more.

Can you put Fortune and Silk Touch on the same pickaxe?

No. They conflict, and the anvil will refuse the combination.

Why does my anvil say "too expensive"?

Each anvil use raises the work penalty on an item. Combine your books before applying them, and apply them to a fresh pickaxe, to keep the final cost within reach.

Does Mending work on a pickaxe?

Yes, Mending is one of the best pickaxe enchantments in minecraft for long term use, since mining itself generates the experience that repairs the tool.

Final Thoughts

Now you know the best pickaxe enchantments in minecraft, from the maxed-out combo to the cheapest anvil order. Build your Fortune pickaxe first for resources, add a Silk Touch pickaxe for building jobs, and keep Mending on both. Best Trident Enchantments in Minecraft: Maxed-Out Combo

Oct 29, 2026
joynalbokhsho

The trident is the most versatile weapon in Minecraft: a melee spear, a ranged weapon, a flight tool and a lightning rod all in one slot. But a plain trident is just a sharp stick, and the wrong enchantment combination wastes a rare drop. This guide ranks the best trident enchantments in Minecraft, explains which ones refuse to work together, and gives you the two maxed-out builds worth your experience levels.

Every Trident Enchantment, Ranked

Loyalty III: The One You Almost Always Want

Loyalty makes a thrown trident fly back to you after it hits something. At Loyalty III the return trip is fast, which turns the trident into a reusable ranged weapon instead of a one-shot throw you have to chase. For most players, Loyalty is the single best trident enchantment in Minecraft, because a trident you cannot get back is a trident you will lose in a cave, a lake or a fight.

Impaling V: The Damage Enchantment

Impaling adds extra damage against aquatic mobs: guardians, elder guardians, drowned, turtles, dolphins and axolotls, plus any mob standing in water or rain. At Impaling V the bonus is large, and it makes ocean monuments, drowned farms and rainy-day fights much faster. Note the limit: Impaling does nothing against dry-land mobs, so it is a specialist enchantment, not a general damage boost like Sharpness on a sword.

Channeling I: Lightning on Demand

Throw a Channeling trident at a mob during a thunderstorm and lightning strikes the target. That is how you make charged creepers for mob heads, and how you turn villagers into witches or pigs into zombified piglins. Channeling has no levels beyond I, and it only works in thunderstorms, so it is a tool for specific projects rather than everyday combat.

Riptide III: Flight in Water and Rain

Riptide launches you in the direction you throw the trident, but only while you are standing in water or rain. At Riptide III the launch is strong enough for real travel: chain throws in a rainstorm and you can fly across a map faster than an elytra in some cases, and underwater it makes ocean exploration quick and fun. The catch is the conflict below.

Unbreaking III: Make It Last

A trident has 250 durability, and throwing and melee both wear it down. Unbreaking III roughly quadruples its effective life, which matters because tridents are rare: they only drop from drowned, and only a small share of drowned carry one. Every serious trident build includes Unbreaking III.

Mending I: The Repair Enchantment

Mending turns experience orbs you collect into durability repairs. Paired with a good XP farm, a Mending trident effectively never breaks. Mending is one of the best trident enchantments in Minecraft for any weapon you plan to keep forever, and it beats carrying a second trident as a backup.

The Conflict You Must Know: Riptide vs Loyalty and Channeling

Riptide cannot be combined with Loyalty or Channeling. This is the single most important rule when choosing the best trident enchantments in Minecraft, because it forces a real choice between two different weapons:

  • A Loyalty trident is a ranged weapon that always comes back, and it can carry Channeling for lightning tricks.
  • A Riptide trident is a movement tool that launches you through rain and water, but you must pick it up after every throw.

There is no enchantment combination that gives you both. Pick the build that matches how you actually play, not the one that sounds best on paper.

Build 1: The Storm Combat Trident (Most Players)

Loyalty III, Channeling I, Impaling V, Unbreaking III, Mending. This is the best all-round answer to the best trident enchantments in Minecraft question: it throws, it returns, it calls lightning in thunderstorms, it shreds aquatic mobs, and it repairs itself from XP. Use it for ocean monuments, drowned farms, charged creeper projects and general combat. Its only weakness is dry-land damage, where a maxed sword still wins, so carry a sword alongside it.

Build 2: The Riptide Travel Trident (Explorers)

Riptide III, Impaling V, Unbreaking III, Mending. This is the movement build: rain and water become your highway, and Impaling keeps it dangerous against aquatic mobs. It is the best trident enchantments in Minecraft choice for ocean exploration, rainy-day travel and elytra-free flight. Keep a Loyalty trident or a bow as your ranged backup, because this one will not come back to you.

How to Get Each Enchantment

Tridents cannot be enchanted at an enchanting table, so every enchantment comes from books. The best sources are librarian villagers, fishing, and loot chests in structures like ocean monuments, desert temples and woodland mansions. Librarians are the reliable route: place a lectern, check the trade, break and replace the lectern until the villager offers the book you need, then lock the trade in by trading once. For Mending specifically, librarians and fishing are your best bets, and raid drops can help too.

For the cheapest anvil order, combine books in pairs before touching the trident: merge your two cheapest books, then merge that result with the next book, and so on, then apply the finished combined book set to the trident in as few anvil steps as possible. Anvil costs grow with every operation on an item, so combining books first keeps the final application affordable. Once Mending is on, stop using the anvil for repairs entirely: let XP orbs do the work, because repeated anvil repairs eventually hit the "too expensive" limit.

Trident vs Sword and Bow: When to Use What

A maxed trident is not a replacement for everything. Swords still win for dry-land melee damage and looting, bows still win for long-range precision, and crossbows still win for burst damage. The trident wins in water, in rain, and anywhere you want one weapon that covers melee, ranged and movement. If you want the full per-item series, our guides to the best sword, bow, pickaxe and armor enchantments cover the rest of your kit.

On {{SERVER_NAME}}, tridents shine in Survival: ocean bases, guardian farms and rainy-day travel all reward a good trident build. Land claims use the GriefPrevention plugin, so claim your ocean base with a golden shovel before you build the farm. Join us at PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and find the community on Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}.

FAQ

What are the best trident enchantments in Minecraft?

For most players: Loyalty III, Channeling I, Impaling V, Unbreaking III and Mending. For travel: swap Loyalty and Channeling for Riptide III, because Riptide conflicts with both.

Can you put Loyalty and Riptide on the same trident?

No. Riptide is incompatible with Loyalty and with Channeling. You must choose one build or carry two tridents.

Can you enchant a trident at an enchanting table?

No. Tridents only take enchantments from books applied at an anvil. Get books from librarian villagers, fishing, loot chests and raid drops.

How do you get a trident?

Tridents drop from drowned, but only drowned that spawn holding a trident can drop one, and the drop chance is low. A Looting sword helps, and a drowned farm makes the grind much faster.

Is Impaling worth it?

Yes if you fight in or near water. Impaling V is a big damage boost against aquatic mobs and anything standing in water or rain, but it does nothing against dry-land mobs, so pair it with a sword for general combat.

Final Word

The best trident enchantments in Minecraft come down to one decision: Loyalty for a weapon that returns, or Riptide for a weapon that flies you. Build the storm combat trident first, add a Riptide travel trident when you can afford a second one, and keep Mending on both so neither ever breaks. How to Boost FPS in Minecraft: Best Settings Guide

Oct 24, 2026
joynalbokhsho

If your game stutters every time you turn around, this guide on how to boost fps in minecraft will help. Low FPS usually comes from a few hungry settings, not a bad PC, and most fixes take under a minute each. Below you will find the exact video settings to change, the free mods that transform performance, and the Windows and laptop tweaks that matter most on low-end machines.

How to Boost FPS in Minecraft: The Settings That Matter Most

These in-game settings give the biggest gains for the least effort. Change them first before touching anything else.

Java Edition video settings

  • Graphics: Fast (not Fancy or Fabulous). This single change can double FPS on weak GPUs.
  • Render Distance: 6 to 8 chunks on low-end PCs. This is the heaviest setting in the game.
  • Simulation Distance: 4 to 6 chunks. Lower than render distance is fine.
  • Particles: Minimal or Decreased.
  • Clouds: Off or Fast.
  • Smooth Lighting: Off or Minimum.
  • Entity Distance: 50 to 75 percent. Villages and animal farms get much cheaper.
  • Mipmap Levels: 0 or 1.
  • Biome Blend: 5 by 5 or Off.
  • Entity Shadows: Off.
  • Max Framerate: Unlimited, or match your monitor's refresh rate.
  • VSync: Off, unless screen tearing bothers you.

Bedrock Edition video settings

Bedrock has a simpler menu but the same logic applies: drag Render Distance down to 8 to 12 chunks, turn off Fancy Graphics, Beautiful Skies, and Fancy Leaves, and set Particles to Minimal. On phones and tablets, also lower the screen resolution in your device settings if the option exists.


The video settings menu is where the biggest FPS gains hide.

Free Mods That Transform Performance (Java)

Settings alone can only do so much. For a real jump in how to boost fps in minecraft, mods do the heavy lifting, and the best ones are free:

  • Sodium is the current king of FPS mods. Paired with Lithium (better game logic performance) and FerriteCore (lower memory use), it can triple FPS on modest hardware. It runs on the Fabric or Quilt mod loader.
  • OptiFine is the classic alternative. It adds zoom, connected textures, and shader support, but it is generally heavier than Sodium and can conflict with other mods.
  • Install through Prism Launcher, which handles mod loaders and updates cleanly. Always match the mod version to your exact game version, and do not stack two rendering mods at once.

How to Boost FPS in Minecraft on a Low-End PC or Laptop

This section is for the huge number of players on older laptops and budget desktops. Here is how to boost fps in minecraft when the hardware itself is the limit:

  1. Close background apps. Browsers with many tabs eat gigabytes of RAM. Close them before playing.
  2. Plug in the charger. Laptops throttle hard on battery. Set the Windows power plan to Best Performance while plugged in.
  3. Update your GPU drivers. Intel, NVIDIA, and AMD all ship free driver updates that regularly improve Minecraft performance.
  4. Use the right GPU. On laptops with two graphics chips, open Windows Graphics Settings and force Minecraft to use the dedicated (High performance) GPU.
  5. Lower the game resolution. Playing in a smaller window or at 1280 by 720 instead of full HD is one of the fastest FPS wins available.
  6. Keep it cool. Dust-clogged vents cause thermal throttling. Clean the vents and give the laptop room to breathe.

An older laptop can still run Minecraft smoothly with the right settings.

RAM and Java Tweaks

Throwing more RAM at the game is the most misunderstood part of how to boost fps in minecraft. The sweet spot for vanilla or lightly modded Minecraft is 2 to 4 GB. Giving the game 8 or 12 GB can actually cause longer garbage-collection pauses, which feel like random stutters.

  • Set 2 to 4 GB in your launcher's Java settings (Prism Launcher and the official launcher both allow this).
  • Modern Minecraft versions need Java 21, and launchers install the right version automatically. Do not force an old Java 8 install on new versions.
  • Advanced users on big modpacks can experiment with G1GC garbage-collector flags, but for most players the default settings plus 3 GB of RAM are perfect.

Myths That Do Not Help

  • "More RAM always means more FPS." False beyond about 4 GB for most setups, as explained above.
  • Random "FPS booster" downloads. Texture packs and "boosters" from shady sites are a classic malware vector. Get mods only from Modrinth or CurseForge.
  • Registry tweaks and system-file deletions. These risk breaking Windows for zero in-game gain. Skip them entirely.

FAQ: how to boost fps in minecraft

What FPS should I aim for?
60 FPS feels smooth for Survival and building. For PvP and Bedwars, 120 or more gives you a real edge if your monitor supports it.

Sodium or OptiFine, which gives more FPS?
On modern versions, Sodium plus Lithium usually wins by a clear margin. OptiFine wins if you specifically want shaders.

Why does my FPS drop in villages?
Villagers, animals, and item frames are entities, and entities are expensive. Lower Entity Distance and Particles to fix it.

Will these settings help on Bedrock or mobile?
Yes. The render-distance, graphics-quality, and background-app steps apply on every platform.

Does playing on a server like {{SERVER_NAME}} affect FPS?
Server lag and FPS are different things. These settings fix your FPS; if blocks break slowly but your FPS counter is high, that is connection lag, not your PC.

Play Smooth, Play Better

You now know how to boost fps in minecraft from every angle: the settings that matter, the mods that multiply them, and the laptop habits that keep performance steady. A stable 60 FPS makes everything better, from precise Bedwars fights to long Survival building sessions. How to Get Mending in Minecraft: Librarian, Fishing, Loot

Oct 25, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Mending is the one enchantment every serious Minecraft player wants on their best gear. Instead of wearing out, a tool or armor piece with Mending repairs itself from the experience orbs you collect, so your diamond pickaxe, elytra, or netherite sword can last forever if you look after it. The catch is that you cannot get Mending from an enchanting table, no matter how many bookshelves you place around it. If you want to know how to get mending in minecraft, you need villagers, fishing, or loot chests instead. This guide ranks every method, explains the odds in plain terms, and shows you the fastest route to your first Mending book.

What Mending Actually Does

Mending is a treasure enchantment, which is the game's label for enchantments that never appear on an enchanting table. When you gain experience while holding or wearing a Mending item, the experience first repairs that item, restoring 2 durability for every experience point, and only the leftover experience goes to your level bar. If the item is already fully repaired, all the experience goes to your levels as normal. Mending works on almost every kind of gear: tools, weapons, armor, elytra, fishing rods, and more. It does not make an item unbreakable, though. If durability reaches zero, the item still breaks, so keep an eye on heavily used gear and top it up with experience before it gets critical.

How to Get Mending in Minecraft: Every Method Ranked

There are three real ways to learn how to get mending in minecraft, and they are not equal. Ranked from best to worst, they are librarian villagers, fishing, and loot chests. Here is how each one works and which one you should start with.

1. Librarian Villagers: The Best Method

Trading with a librarian villager is the only reliable, repeatable way to get a Mending book, and it is the method most experienced players use. Place a lectern near an unemployed villager and it will take the librarian job. Check its first trade: if it offers an enchanted book, look at which enchantment it is. If it is not Mending, break the lectern and place it again to reroll the trade. You can repeat this until the villager offers a Mending book, but only before you trade with it for the first time, because the first trade locks its offers in place.

A Mending book is an expensive trade, so stock up on emeralds first. Paper from sugar cane, or books from a cow and sugar cane farm, trade well with librarians and give you a steady emerald income. If you cure a zombie villager first, you can also unlock big discounts, which makes the Mending trade far cheaper. Once you have your librarian, you can buy more Mending books whenever you need them, which is why this method beats every other option. For players asking how to get mending in minecraft on a fresh world, this is the answer to aim for.

2. Fishing: The Patient Method

Fishing can reward you with enchanted books as treasure catches, and Mending is one of the enchantments those books can carry. The chance of a treasure catch is small, but a fishing rod with Luck of the Sea III raises it noticeably, and Lure III shortens the wait between bites. This method costs almost nothing to start, which makes it a good early game option while you set up villagers. The downside is luck: you might fish for an hour and catch nothing but fish and junk, or you might land a Mending book on your tenth cast. If you enjoy relaxed play, or you want to learn how to get mending in minecraft without building a trading hall, fishing is a fair way to try.

3. Loot Chests: The Lucky Find

Enchanted books turn up in loot chests all over the world: dungeons, desert temples, jungle temples, mineshafts, strongholds, woodland mansions, ancient cities, and End cities. Any of these chests can hold a Mending book, and End cities are a particularly good late game hunting ground because their chests often carry strong enchanted gear and books. Treat this method as a bonus, not a plan. You cannot control what a chest contains, so exploring for a Mending book can take many trips. Still, if you are already out raiding structures, always check the chests: many players find their first Mending book this way. Players searching for how to get mending in minecraft often overlook this method, but it costs nothing extra if you are exploring anyway.

4. Methods That Do Not Work

Save yourself wasted effort: the enchanting table never offers Mending, even at level 30 with full bookshelves. You also cannot craft a Mending book, and wandering traders do not sell enchanted books. If a guide promises Mending from enchanting, it is wrong. Treasure enchantments only come from trading, fishing, loot, or combining books you already own.

How to Use Mending Once You Have It

Combine the book with your gear on an anvil and pay the experience level cost. For the best value, put Unbreaking III on the item first, since a higher durability pool means fewer repairs overall. After that, just use the item: every experience orb you pick up while holding or wearing it repairs it automatically. Mining, smelting, breeding animals, and killing mobs all produce experience, so normal play keeps Mending gear topped up. One warning: a grindstone strips enchantments, so never grind a Mending item unless you mean to remove the enchantment. And remember that experience repairs one item at a time, so if you wear several Mending pieces, spread your play across them rather than expecting one orb to fix everything. This is the part of learning how to get mending in minecraft that matters most: the book is only half the job, and using it well is the other half.

Which Gear Deserves Mending First

Put Mending on the gear you use most and would hate to lose. For most players that means an elytra first, then a pickaxe, then a sword, then armor. Elytra are expensive to replace and break fast when flying, so Mending turns them from a luxury into a permanent tool. Your pickaxe comes next because you use it constantly, and a Mending pickaxe with Fortune or Silk Touch is a long term investment.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Do not trade with a librarian before checking its book offer, or you will lock in the wrong trade. Do not try to combine Mending with Infinity on a bow, because those two enchantments conflict and the anvil will refuse the combination. Do not let a favorite item sit at nearly zero durability while you chase experience, since one more use can break it. And do not ignore Unbreaking: Mending repairs damage, but Unbreaking slows damage down, and together they make gear last many times longer.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you get Mending from an enchanting table?

No. Mending is a treasure enchantment, so it never appears on an enchanting table at any level.

What is the easiest way to get Mending?

Rerolling a librarian villager's book trade with a lectern is the easiest reliable method, and it works in both Java and Bedrock editions.

Does Mending work on netherite gear?

Yes. Mending works on netherite tools, weapons, and armor, and it is one of the best enchantments to put on netherite.

Can a bow have both Mending and Infinity?

No. Mending and Infinity conflict, so a bow can only have one of them. Most players pick Mending for a bow they use heavily, or Infinity for a bow they use casually.

Does Mending repair gear automatically?

Yes, as long as you hold the tool or wear the armor while collecting experience orbs. If you want to know how to get mending in minecraft and keep your gear forever, this automatic repair is the payoff.

Final Thoughts

Now you know how to get mending in minecraft, from librarian rerolls to lucky fishing catches. Mending changes how you play: once your best gear repairs itself, you stop worrying about durability and start building bigger projects. Start with a librarian trading hall, fish while you gather emeralds, and check every loot chest you pass. On the {{SERVER_NAME}} Survival server, a Mending pickaxe is one of the first upgrades veteran players recommend, so join us at PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM, ask for trading tips on Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}, and get your first Mending book this week.

How to Get Netherite in Minecraft: Debris & Gear

Oct 30, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Netherite is the strongest gear material in Minecraft, and learning how to get netherite in minecraft is the step that turns a good diamond set into endgame gear. Netherite tools mine faster, netherite armor protects better, and netherite items do not burn in lava. The catch is that you cannot mine netherite ore directly. You have to brave the Nether, find ancient debris, and upgrade diamond gear piece by piece. This guide covers the whole route, from preparation to your first full netherite set, plus the mistakes that waste the most time.

Before You Go to the Nether

Do not walk into the Nether unprepared. Ancient debris spawns deep underground in a dangerous dimension, so bring diamond tools, a diamond pickaxe at minimum, and decent armor. A fire resistance potion is a lifesaver near lava lakes, and a stack of blocks helps you bridge and block off danger. Bring food, a bed is useless in the Nether since it explodes, so set your spawn safely in the Overworld before you leave.

Pack an efficiency pickaxe if you have one, since you will be clearing a lot of netherrack. Players learning how to get netherite in minecraft often underestimate how much tunnelling this takes, so bring spare pickaxes. Gold armor helps with piglins, who attack players not wearing at least one piece of gold. Keep your valuables in an ender chest or at home, because a lava death in the Nether can cost you everything you carried in.

Netherite Mining Kit

  • Hotbar Slot 2 (#1): Tnt Side
  • Hotbar Slot 3 (#2): Potion of Fire Resistance [Effect: Fire Resistance (3:00)]
  • Hotbar Slot 4 (#3): Golden Helmet
  • Hotbar Slot 5 (#4): Cooked Beef
  • Hotbar Slot 6 (#5): 64x Obsidian
  • Inventory Storage Slot 9 (#9): Diamond Pickaxe

How to Get Netherite in Minecraft, Step by Step

The short version of how to get netherite in minecraft is: mine ancient debris, smelt it into netherite scrap, combine scrap with gold ingots to make netherite ingots, then use a smithing table to upgrade diamond gear. Each step is simple on its own, but the mining part is where most players get stuck, so let us break it down properly.

First, you need diamond gear to upgrade. Netherite does not replace the crafting table route, it upgrades what you already have. Make or find a full diamond set, diamond tools, and a smithing table, which is crafted from two iron ingots and four planks of any wood. You will also need a netherite upgrade smithing template, found in bastion remnant chests, one template per upgrade, though you can duplicate templates with diamonds and netherrack.

Finding Ancient Debris

Ancient debris is the raw material for everything netherite, and it only spawns in the Nether between Y levels 8 and 22, with the best odds around Y 15. It is rare, roughly one or two blocks per chunk in that range, and it is blast resistant, which is why TNT mining works so well here.

The classic method is strip mining at Y 15: dig a long tunnel, then branch off every few blocks and check the walls. It is slow but safe and cheap. The faster method is bed mining or TNT mining: place beds or TNT at intervals, trigger them from a safe distance, and clear huge areas of netherrack at once. Ancient debris survives the blast, so you just walk through the cleared area and collect it. Bed mining is cheap but risky, since beds explode in the Nether, so wear blast protection and keep your distance.

Whatever method you pick, mine at Y 15, keep a fire resistance potion handy, and mark your tunnel so you can find your way back to your portal. That Y 15 habit is the core of how to get netherite in minecraft efficiently, since debris is densest there. Four ancient debris blocks are enough for one netherite ingot, and one ingot upgrades one piece of gear, so a full armor set plus tools takes a serious mining session. Plan for at least 36 debris for a full set of armor, tools, and a sword, and more if you want spares.

From Debris to Netherite Ingots

Smelt each ancient debris block in a furnace or blast furnace to get one netherite scrap. Then combine four netherite scrap with four gold ingots in a crafting table to make one netherite ingot. Gold is easy to find in the Nether itself, from piglin trading, bastion chests, and nether gold ore, so you rarely need to bring gold from home.

This scrap and gold recipe is the same in Java and Bedrock, and it has not changed in recent versions, so once you learn how to get netherite in minecraft this way, you know it for good. Store your scraps and ingots safely, since losing an ingot to lava before you upgrade feels terrible, and remember that netherite items themselves float in lava, but the raw ingot does not get that protection until it is applied to gear.

Upgrading Diamond Gear at the Smithing Table

Place your diamond item, one netherite ingot, and one netherite upgrade smithing template in the smithing table, and the item becomes netherite, keeping its enchantments, name, and durability state. This is the best part of the system: you do not lose Mending, Unbreaking, or any other enchantment you worked hard to get.

Upgrade order matters if you are short on ingots. Armor first is the safe choice for survival players, especially the chestplate and leggings, since knockback resistance on netherite armor also helps in fights. Tools second, starting with your pickaxe, since a netherite pickaxe mines faster and lasts longer. Sword players should upgrade the sword early too, since netherite swords hit harder than diamond.

Netherite Tips That Save You Hours

When you are working out how to get netherite in minecraft on a busy server, mine with a beacon if you can set one up near your Nether tunnel, since Haste makes clearing netherrack much faster. Use TNT in bulk rather than one block at a time, and always mine debris from a safe standing spot, never while standing on a block that could drop you into lava. Carry a fire resistance potion and a totem if you have one, and do not explore bastions unarmed, since brutes hit very hard.

Another common mistake is upgrading the wrong item first. A netherite hoe looks funny, but it does almost nothing for survival, so leave novelty upgrades until your armor, pickaxe, sword, and axe are done. And duplicate your smithing template before you run out: one template plus seven diamonds and netherrack in a crafting table gives you two templates, so you never have to raid another bastion just for templates.

FAQ

Do I need a diamond pickaxe to mine ancient debris?

Yes, you need a diamond pickaxe or better. Weaker pickaxes will break the block without dropping it.

How many ancient debris do I need for full netherite armor?

Four debris make one ingot, and one ingot upgrades one armor piece, so full armor takes 16 debris, or four ingots.

Does netherite gear burn in lava?

Netherite items float in lava and do not burn, which is a huge safety net in the Nether and near lava lakes anywhere.

Can I upgrade enchanted diamond gear?

Yes, and you should. The smithing table keeps all enchantments, so upgrade your best enchanted diamond gear rather than crafting fresh pieces.

Ready to Gear Up on {{SERVER_NAME}}?

Now you know how to get netherite in minecraft from first debris to finished gear. Grab a diamond pickaxe, head to Y 15 in the Nether, and start your first mining run. When you finish your first netherite piece, show it off in the {{SERVER_NAME}} Discord and see how other players set up their own Nether tunnels. Good luck, and watch out for lava.

How to Make an Enchanting Table in Minecraft: Full Guide

Nov 4, 2026
joynalbokhsho

An enchanting table is the single most useful crafting station in Minecraft once you have diamond gear. It turns plain tools, weapons and armor into enchanted versions that mine faster, hit harder and protect you better. If you are ready to stop relying on lucky loot, this guide shows you how to make an enchanting table in minecraft, what materials you need, how to craft it, and how to surround it with bookshelves for the best possible enchantments.

How to Make an Enchanting Table in Minecraft: Step by Step

Before you craft anything, gather the materials. Learning how to make an enchanting table in minecraft starts with three items, and none of them are hard to find once you know where to look.

You need four obsidian blocks, two diamonds and one book. Obsidian forms when water touches a lava source block, and you must mine it with a diamond pickaxe or better. Diamonds are most commonly found deep underground, around Y level minus 58 in current versions, so bring torches, food and a spare pickaxe. A book is crafted from three paper and one leather, and paper comes from sugar cane.

The enchanting table recipe

Open a crafting table and place the items in this exact pattern. Top row: leave the two side slots empty and put the book in the centre. Middle row: diamond, obsidian, diamond. Bottom row: obsidian, obsidian, obsidian. That uses four obsidian, two diamonds and one book, and it gives you one enchanting table.

Place the table somewhere safe, ideally in a room you can expand later. You will need space around it for bookshelves, so leave at least a two block gap on every side before you start decorating.

Gathering Obsidian, Diamonds and a Book

Obsidian is the slowest part of the job. Find a lava pool, pour a water bucket over a lava source block, and mine the resulting obsidian with a diamond pickaxe. Each block takes about nine seconds to mine, so be patient and watch for lava underneath. Never dig straight down into a lava pool, and keep a water bucket handy in case you catch fire.

Diamonds reward careful branch mining. Dig to the deep levels, light your tunnels well, and mine in straight lines with two block gaps between tunnels so you can spot exposed ores on both sides. A Fortune pickaxe, once you have one, increases your diamond yield, but your first enchanting table has to come before that upgrade.

Books are easy by comparison. Grow sugar cane beside water, craft three paper from three sugar cane, then combine the paper with one leather from a cow, horse or other leather dropping mob. One book is enough for the table itself, but you will need many more books for bookshelves, so start a sugar cane farm and a cow pen early. That is the full shopping list for how to make an enchanting table in minecraft, so check it twice before you head to the crafting table.

Setting Up Bookshelves for Level 30 Enchants

A bare enchanting table only offers low level enchantments. Bookshelves raise the maximum level, and fifteen bookshelves are needed for level 30, the highest tier. Place the bookshelves one block away from the table, in a ring around it, two blocks high. The game counts bookshelves that have a clear line of sight to the table, so do not block the gap with torches, carpets or other blocks.

Each bookshelf costs three books and six wooden planks. Fifteen bookshelves therefore need forty five books and ninety planks, which is why a sugar cane farm matters so much. If you cannot build all fifteen at once, build what you can and add more later, because every bookshelf raises your options.

Once the ring is complete, open the table, place an item and some lapis lazuli inside, and you will see level 30 enchantments appear. Lapis lazuli is required for every enchantment, with higher levels costing more lapis and more experience levels, so mine lapis whenever you see it underground.

How to Enchant Well and Save Experience

Enchanting is partly random, so use a few smart habits to get more value from every level. First, enchant diamond or netherite gear rather than iron, because the better base item lasts longer and deserves the experience. Second, enchant books when you are unsure what you want, because books can be stored and combined later on an anvil with exactly the item you choose.

Third, use a grindstone to remove unwanted enchantments from gear you no longer need, which returns a little experience. Once you know how to make an enchanting table in minecraft, the next skill is choosing which enchantments are worth your levels. Fourth, keep a steady experience supply. A simple mob farm, a furnace array smelting kelp or stone, or trading with villagers all give reliable experience between enchanting sessions. Finally, remember that knowing how to make an enchanting table in minecraft is only the start. Combining enchanted books on an anvil, repairing gear with Mending, and choosing the right enchantment for each tool are what turn good gear into great gear.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Do not place the enchanting table against a wall with no room for bookshelves, because you will have to move it later. Do not put torches or carpets in the one block gap around the table, because they block bookshelf power. Do not spend level 30 enchantments on stone or wooden tools, and do not enchant before you have lapis lazuli, because the table will not let you confirm the enchantment without it.

Another common mistake is enchanting everything at level 30 and hoping for the best. Sometimes a level 1 or level 5 enchantment on a book is exactly what you need for a specific anvil combination, and it costs far less experience. Enchant cheaply when you are filling gaps, and save level 30 for your main sword, pickaxe and armor.

FAQ

Do I need diamonds to make an enchanting table?

Yes. The recipe needs two diamonds, plus four obsidian and one book. You also need a diamond pickaxe to mine the obsidian, so diamond mining comes first.

How many bookshelves do I need for level 30?

Fifteen bookshelves, placed one block away from the table in a ring two blocks high, with nothing blocking the gap between the shelves and the table.

Does the enchanting table work in both Java and Bedrock?

Yes, the recipe and the bookshelf rules are the same in both versions, and the enchanting interface works the same way in both.

What does lapis lazuli do in enchanting?

Lapis lazuli is the material cost for every enchantment. A level 30 enchantment costs three lapis lazuli and three experience levels, while lower levels cost less of both.

Can I move an enchanting table after placing it?

Yes, break it with any pickaxe and pick it up. Bookshelves can be moved the same way, so rebuild the ring around the table in its new home.

Final Thoughts

Now you know how to make an enchanting table in minecraft, gather its materials, and build the bookshelf ring that unlocks level 30 enchantments. Start with the table, add bookshelves as your sugar cane farm grows, and enchant your best gear first. On {{SERVER_NAME}}, an enchanted set makes Survival nights, mining trips and Bedwars fights far easier, so get your table built and start enchanting. How to Make a Creeper Farm in Minecraft: Easy Guide

Nov 7, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Gunpowder powers rockets, TNT and firework stars, and creepers are the only mob that drops it in useful amounts. Hunting them one by one at night is slow and dangerous, so a farm is the answer. This guide shows how to make a creeper farm in minecraft, using a simple tower design that works in both Java and Bedrock and needs no redstone knowledge to build.

Why Build a Creeper Farm?

A creeper farm turns gunpowder from a chore into a background resource. Stand at the collection point, go AFK, and come back to stacks of gunpowder. That gunpowder becomes rockets for your elytra, TNT for mining, and firework stars for celebrations.

Compared to hunting creepers at night, a farm is safer, faster and fully automatic. It also keeps your base area free of wandering creepers, since the farm draws spawns into one controlled tower. Once you learn how to make a creeper farm in minecraft, you will never buy or hunt gunpowder again.

How to Make a Creeper Farm in Minecraft

The classic design is a tall tower with spawning platforms at the top and a drop chute at the bottom. Creepers spawn on the dark platforms, wander toward the edges, fall down the chute, and land in a collection area where hoppers gather their drops. Cats scare creepers off the platforms, which pushes them into the chute faster.

Materials You Need

Gather these before you start building:

  • Around 4 stacks of building blocks, stone or cobblestone works well
  • 2 stacks of slabs for the spawning platforms
  • Trapdoors, around 2 stacks, to line the platform edges
  • A few cats, tamed and sitting near the platforms
  • Hoppers and chests for the collection system
  • Water buckets for the chute, or a campfire setup for the killing floor
  • Torches to light the area around the tower and stop outside spawns
  • A stack of scaffolding or ladders to climb while building

Build the tower in an ocean or a flat area away from other spawnable ground. The fewer places mobs can spawn outside the farm, the better your rates.

Step 1: Build the Tower Base

Pick a spot at least 100 blocks from your base and other lit areas. Build a 3 by 3 pillar up to about 120 blocks high, or at least 24 blocks above the highest nearby ground. Mobs only spawn within a certain distance of the player, so height keeps the spawn area focused on your platforms.

At the top, build a central column with a 2 by 2 drop chute running down the middle. Line the bottom of the chute with hoppers feeding into chests. This is where creepers fall and where you collect gunpowder.

Step 2: Add the Spawning Platforms

Build two to four square platforms around the central column, each about 10 by 10 blocks, made of slabs. Mobs spawn on slabs only when the slab is a top slab, so use bottom slabs for the floor to block spawns where you do not want them, and solid blocks for the platform tops.

Place trapdoors open along every platform edge. Creepers see trapdoors as solid ground and walk straight onto them, then fall. This trick is the heart of the design: the creepers push themselves off the platforms without any redstone at all.


Alt text: creeper farm spawning platform with trapdoors showing how to make a creeper farm in minecraft

Step 3: Place Cats to Scare Creepers

Creepers run away from cats, so place a few tamed cats sitting on the platforms. When a creeper spawns, it spots the cat and flees toward the platform edge, straight onto the trapdoors and down the chute.

Keep the cats safe. Sit them on a spot where they cannot fall, and keep them away from the drop chute. If a cat dies, tame a replacement and sit it in the same place. Learning how to make a creeper farm in minecraft is mostly about this one behaviour: cats move creepers for free.

Step 4: The Killing Floor and Collection

At the bottom of the chute, creepers need to die without exploding. A fall of 23 blocks leaves a creeper at half a heart, so you can finish it with one punch. Alternatively, place campfires at the bottom, which slowly damage creepers without triggering explosions, and let hoppers collect the drops.

Set up hoppers under the killing floor feeding into a double chest. Check the chest after your first AFK session and you should see your first stacks of gunpowder. Add a sorting system later if you want gunpowder separated from the occasional rotten flesh or string.


Alt text: gunpowder collection chests at the base of a creeper farm in minecraft

Rates and AFK Tips

A simple two platform farm produces a few hundred gunpowder per hour while you AFK nearby. Bigger farms with more platforms produce more, but start simple and expand later.

Stand on an AFK platform about 24 to 32 blocks from the spawning platforms. Closer than 24 blocks and mobs will not spawn; further than 128 blocks and they despawn. Light up all caves and the ground around the tower, or your farm will compete with spawns outside it.

On a multiplayer server like {{SERVER_NAME}}, build the farm in a less crowded area so other players do not fill the mob cap. Check the server rules on /rules before building near spawn or in a claimed area, and use the GriefPrevention golden shovel to claim the land under your farm.

Common Mistakes

The most common mistake is building the platforms too low. If the platforms are near ground level, mobs spawn in caves and on the surface instead, and your rates collapse. Height is not optional.

The second mistake is forgetting the cats. Without cats, creepers wander randomly and many never reach the edge. A couple of tamed cats doubles the speed of the farm.

The third mistake is using the wrong slab type on platform floors. Bottom slabs block spawning, so make sure your platform tops are solid blocks or top slabs where you want creepers to appear.

FAQ

Does a creeper farm work on Bedrock?
Yes. This tower design works on both Java and Bedrock, though exact rates differ because Bedrock uses a different mob spawning system. The trapdoor and cat mechanics work the same on both.

How high should a creeper farm be?
Build the platforms at least 24 blocks above the highest nearby ground, and ideally around Y 120 or higher in an ocean. Higher platforms mean fewer competing spawns below.

Why are other mobs spawning in my creeper farm?
Trapdoors and cats only affect creepers, but zombies and skeletons can still spawn on the platforms. That is normal for a simple design. A creeper only version needs more complex filtering, so expect some bones and rotten flesh mixed in with your gunpowder.

How much gunpowder does a creeper farm make?
A small two platform farm makes roughly 200 to 400 gunpowder per hour while you AFK nearby. Add more platforms to raise the rate.

Do I need redstone for a creeper farm?
No. This design uses trapdoors, cats and gravity, with no redstone at all. Redstone only becomes useful for advanced sorting or auto killing.

Final Thoughts

Now you know how to make a creeper farm in minecraft, from the tower and trapdoors to the cats and the collection chests. Start small, test your rates, and expand the platforms once the design proves itself. Your elytra rockets will never run dry again. Come build yours on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and show off your gunpowder stockpile in the Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}.

How to Protect Your Base & Claim Land in Minecraft

Oct 22, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Nothing hurts more than logging in and finding your base raided, your chests emptied, and your builds destroyed. Learning how to claim land in Minecraft is the single best way to stop that from ever happening — and on {{SERVER_NAME}} it only takes a few minutes. This guide explains exactly how our land-claim system works, step by step, using the GriefPrevention plugin that protects every claim on the server.

Whether you are building your first dirt hut or a full town, claim your land first and build second. Here is how.

Why You Should Claim Land in Minecraft

On a multiplayer server, other players can wander anywhere. Without protection, anyone can break your blocks, open your chests, and take your items. A land claim changes that completely.

Inside your claim:

  • Only you can build, break blocks, and open containers
  • Other players cannot touch your chests, doors, animals, or crops
  • Explosions and fire cannot damage your base
  • You choose exactly who is allowed in — and what they can do

On {{SERVER_NAME}}, claims are powered by the GriefPrevention plugin, the most trusted land-protection system in Minecraft. Once your land is claimed, it stays protected 24/7 — even while you are offline.

What You Need to Claim Land

You only need two things:

  1. A golden shovel — craft one with 2 sticks and 1 gold ingot. The golden shovel is the claiming tool.
  2. Claim blocks — every player starts with claim blocks to spend, and you automatically earn more the longer you play on the server. Type /claimslist in chat anytime to see how many claim blocks you have and where your claims are.

Good to know: when you place your very first chest, GriefPrevention automatically creates a small starter claim around it, so your first items are protected right away.

How to Claim Land: Step by Step

Follow these steps to claim any piece of land:

  1. Hold your golden shovel
  2. Stand at one corner of the area you want to claim and right-click the ground — you will see a marker appear
  3. Walk diagonally to the opposite corner of your area
  4. Right-click the ground again — the claim is created instantly, with glowing corner markers showing your borders

Your claim covers everything from bedrock to the sky inside those borders. To make it bigger, stand outside the claim holding the shovel and right-click to extend a corner. Made a mistake? Use /abandonclaim while standing inside a claim to remove it and get your claim blocks back.

Tip: Not sure where a claim is? Right-click the ground with a regular stick — it shows you the claim borders and tells you who owns the land.

Claim Commands You Should Know

Type these in the in-game chat:

  • /claimslist — see your claim blocks and all your claims
  • /trust <player> — give a player full access to your claim
  • /accesstrust <player> — let a player use doors, buttons, and beds, but not build
  • /containertrust <player> — let a player open chests and use workstations, but not build
  • /permissiontrust <player> — let a player manage trust for others in your claim
  • /trustlist — see who has access to the claim you are standing in
  • /untrust <player> — remove a player's access
  • /abandonclaim — delete the claim you are standing in
  • /subdivideclaims — split your claim into smaller pieces with separate permissions, perfect for towns and shops

7 Tips to Keep Your Base 100% Safe

  1. Claim before you build — even a small starter claim beats rebuilding from zero
  2. Claim a little extra land around your base so nobody can build right up against your walls
  3. Protect your animals and farms — make sure pens and crop fields are inside the claim
  4. Be careful with /trust — only trust players you really know; /untrust anyone suspicious
  5. Use subdivisions for shared areas — give friends access to one room or plot, not your whole base
  6. Check your claim blocks with /claimslist and expand your claim as your base grows
  7. Lock down storage — keep your most valuable chests deep inside your claim, never near the border

Frequently Asked Questions

Can someone still grief inside my claim?
No. Inside your claim, only you and players you have trusted can build, break, or open containers. Explosions and fire damage are blocked too.

What happens to my claim if I stop playing?
Your claim and everything in it stay protected while you are offline, so your base is safe between sessions. Very old claims from players who never return may eventually be cleaned up by staff — stay active and you have nothing to worry about.

Can I claim land in the Nether or the End?
Claims are designed for the overworld building areas. Adventure, mining, and resource worlds are for gathering — bring what you collect back and store it inside your claim.

I ran out of claim blocks. What now?
Just keep playing — claim blocks build up automatically over time. You can also abandon claims you no longer need with /abandonclaim to get blocks back.

Protect Your Base Today

Now you know how to claim land in Minecraft and keep everything you build safe on {{SERVER_NAME}}. Grab a golden shovel, claim your spot, and build with total peace of mind. Questions or need help with a claim? Ask in chat or join our Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}} — and make sure you have read the server rules at /rules before you start building.

How to Make an Iron Farm in Minecraft: Easy Guide

Nov 4, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Iron is the backbone of every Minecraft world. You need it for tools, armor, hoppers, rails, and beacons, and mining it by hand gets old fast. An iron farm solves that problem for good by farming iron golems automatically. This guide explains how to make an iron farm in minecraft using a simple, beginner friendly villager design that works in Survival and needs no redstone wizardry.

How to Make an Iron Farm in Minecraft: The Simple Design

Iron golems spawn near villagers when a village has enough beds and workstations, and villagers that have recently been scared by a zombie spawn golems even faster. Our design uses three villagers, three beds, and three workstations in a small chamber, with a zombie in a separate glass box to keep them scared. Golems spawn on a platform above, get pushed or fall into a lava blade, and their iron ingots and poppies drop into hoppers and chests below.

You do not need a huge build. The whole farm fits in a small tower, and once it is running it produces a steady supply of iron with zero effort. Expect a few hundred iron ingots per hour from a basic three villager setup, which is plenty for most players and small servers.

Materials You Need

  • 3 villagers
  • 3 beds
  • 3 workstations (any job block, such as a composter or lectern)
  • Building blocks for the chamber and platform
  • 1 zombie (name tagged so it does not despawn)
  • Glass blocks for the zombie chamber
  • 1 lava bucket
  • Signs or trapdoors to hold the lava in place
  • Hoppers and at least one double chest
  • A water bucket for moving villagers
  • A name tag

Step 1: Build the Villager Chamber

Pick a flat spot at least 100 blocks from any other village, beds, or villagers, so your farm is the only village the game counts. Build a small enclosed room about 5 blocks wide and 3 blocks tall. Place three beds inside, one for each villager, and three workstations against the walls. Add a roof so villagers cannot escape and hostile mobs cannot drop in.

Getting villagers into the chamber takes patience. Use minecart rails, boats, or water streams to move them in, and block the entrance once all three are inside. Each villager must be able to reach a bed and a workstation, so check that none of them are stuck in a corner. When all three have claimed a bed and a job, the village is ready.

Step 2: Add the Zombie Scare Chamber

Scared villagers summon golems much more often, so a zombie chamber is the secret to high rates. Build a small glass box next to the villager chamber, separated by a wall with a small window, so villagers can see the zombie but it cannot reach them. Drop a zombie into the glass box and name tag it so it never despawns.

The zombie should stay in sight of the villagers at all times. If the villagers stop panicking, check that the zombie is still visible through the glass and that no blocks are blocking their view. A single zombie is enough, and keeping it contained means your villagers stay safe while staying scared.

Step 3: Build the Spawning Platform and Lava Collection

Above or beside the villager chamber, build a flat spawning platform made of solid blocks, roughly 8 blocks by 8 blocks, where golems can appear. Golems spawn on solid ground near the village center, so keep the platform clear of torches, slabs, and other spawn proofing. A water stream or open trapdoors can push freshly spawned golems toward the collection area.

For the kill chamber, place lava held back by signs so it sits at head height for a golem, with hoppers underneath to catch drops. Golems are tall, so the lava blade burns them while their iron ingots fall through into the hoppers. Connect the hoppers to a double chest, and check the chest after a few minutes: you should see iron ingots and poppies stacking up. If nothing spawns, the usual causes are beds or workstations that villagers cannot reach, another village too close by, or the zombie chamber being out of sight.

Rates, Troubleshooting, and Upgrades

A basic three villager farm with a zombie produces a few hundred iron ingots per hour, which covers tools, armor, and hoppers for a solo player. If rates feel low, first check that all three villagers sleep at night and work during the day, since a villager that cannot reach its bed or workstation stops counting toward the village. Also make sure no other beds, bells, or villagers are within range, since they can split the village and break spawning.

To scale up, build more villager chambers stacked in a tower, each with its own beds and workstations, feeding one shared collection system. Some players add a second zombie or an automatic sorting system for poppies, but the basic design here is enough to start. Avoid overbuilding on a shared server without checking the rules first, since very large farms can cause lag.

Java vs Bedrock Notes

The core idea works on both editions, but small details differ. Golem spawning rules, villager panic behavior, and the exact distances for village detection are not identical between Java and Bedrock, so if a design works on one edition and not the other, check an edition specific tutorial for the exact spacing before rebuilding. The layout in this guide follows the general rules that hold on both editions, and it is a safe starting point for either one.

FAQ

How many villagers does an iron farm need?

Three villagers with three beds and three workstations are the minimum for reliable golem spawning. More villagers can raise rates, but three is the sweet spot for a simple farm.

Why is my iron farm not spawning golems?

The most common reasons are villagers that cannot reach their beds or workstations, another village too close by, or a zombie that villagers cannot see. Fix those three things first before rebuilding anything.

Do iron farms work without a zombie?

Yes, but much more slowly. Villagers summon golems on their own through gossip, while a visible zombie scares them into summoning far more often. The zombie chamber is the single biggest rate upgrade you can add.

Can I build an iron farm near my base?

You can, but keep it at least 100 blocks from other beds, workstations, and villagers, including your trading hall. Nearby villages can merge with your farm and stop golem spawning entirely.

Start Your Iron Supply Today

Now you know how to make an iron farm in minecraft, from the villager chamber and zombie scare box to the lava collection system. Build the simple version first, watch the iron stack up, and expand later if you need more. If you play on {{SERVER_NAME}}, check /rules before building large farms near other players, and join us on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM to trade your spare iron with other Survival players. Share your farm on Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}} and show the server what your setup can do.

How to Make an XP Farm in Minecraft: Easy Guide

Nov 6, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Gold is one of the most useful resources in Minecraft. You need it for golden apples, powered rails, piglin trading, and golden carrots, and mining it by hand is slow. That is why learning how to make an xp farm in minecraft is one of the best upgrades you can make to your world. A good farm turns hostile mobs into a steady supply of levels while you stand in one safe spot.

This guide covers a simple mob farm design that works on Java and Bedrock. It uses a dark spawning tower, water channels, and a drop shaft, and you can build it with materials from a normal survival playthrough. You do not need a spawner, redstone skills, or a huge perimeter. Once it is running, you can walk away, collect levels, and come back to enchanted gear.

Why You Need an XP Farm

Enchanting is where a survival world really opens up. A level 30 enchantment costs 30 levels and 3 lapis lazuli, and a full set of enchanted diamond or netherite gear can take well over a hundred levels to finish. Without a farm, you grind those levels by mining, trading, or killing mobs one at a time in the dark. With a farm, the mobs come to you.

An XP farm also gives you loot. Zombies drop rotten flesh, skeletons drop bones and arrows, and creepers drop gunpowder. Bones become bone meal for your crops, arrows feed your bow, and gunpowder feeds your rockets and TNT. That is the whole reason to learn how to make an xp farm in minecraft early: it pays you back in levels and in useful drops at the same time.

How to Make an XP Farm in Minecraft: The Easy Mob Farm

The design in this guide is a classic dark-room tower farm. Hostile mobs spawn in a dark chamber high in the sky, wander into water channels, and get pushed off a ledge into a drop shaft. They fall to a killing chamber where one hit finishes them, and you collect the experience and the drops. Hoppers underneath feed everything into chests.

Here is the idea in simple terms: build a dark box with several spawning floors, add water to push mobs toward a central hole, and put a safe room at the bottom where you stand and swing your sword. The farm runs as long as you stay nearby, and you stay safe behind walls while it works.


Alt: zombies and skeletons falling through water channels in a minecraft xp farm tower

Materials You Need

Before you start, gather these materials:

  • 4 stacks of building blocks (cobblestone or stone bricks work well)
  • 2 stacks of slabs for the spawning floors
  • 2 water buckets for the channels
  • 8 trapdoors to guide mobs into the drop hole
  • 20 hoppers and 4 chests for collection
  • 1 stack of torches for lighting the area below the farm
  • A sword with Looting if you have one, since Looting increases drops
  • Scaffolding or ladders to reach the top while you build

The exact amounts depend on how tall you build. Four spawning floors is a good starting size. You can always add more floors later if you want higher rates.

Building the Farm Step by Step

1. Pick a Location

The first choice when you learn how to make an xp farm in minecraft is the location. Build over the ocean if you can, because the water below stops other mobs from spawning and stealing your mob cap. Build at least 128 blocks above the ground or the ocean surface, so nothing spawns below your farm except in the tower itself. If you build on land, light up every cave and dark spot nearby, or mobs will spawn there instead of in your tower.

2. Build the Spawning Tower

Build a square tower about 9 blocks by 9 blocks, with 4 floors inside. Each floor should be 3 blocks tall, with a 2 by 2 hole in the center. Cover the floors with slabs or leave small gaps so mobs walk toward the water. Make sure the tower is completely dark inside, with no torches and no light leaking in through gaps. Mobs only spawn in darkness, so a single light leak can cut your rates.

3. Add Water Channels

On each floor, place water at the edges so it flows toward the center hole. The water pushes wandering mobs into the hole, and they fall down the shaft. Add trapdoors around the hole on each floor. Mobs treat open trapdoors as solid ground and walk straight over them, which keeps them moving toward the drop instead of stopping at the edge.

4. Build the Drop Shaft and Killing Chamber

Below the tower, build a drop shaft about 22 blocks deep. A fall of that height leaves most mobs with half a heart, so one sword hit finishes them and you get the experience. At the bottom, place hoppers in a row feeding into double chests. Build a small safe room around the collection point with walls and a roof, so nothing can hit you while you wait.

If you are learning how to make an xp farm in minecraft for the first time, keep this version simple. Do not add extra floors, sorting systems, or automatic killers until the basic farm works. A simple farm that runs is better than a complex farm that breaks.

Collecting Levels and Enchanting

Once the farm runs, stand at the killing chamber and swing your sword. Each kill drops green experience orbs that fly to you, and the levels add up fast. A few minutes of killing usually gives you enough levels for a level 30 enchantment.


Alt: player enchanting gear at an enchanting table with experience levels from a minecraft xp farm

Keep an enchanting table and an anvil near the farm if you can. That way you spend the levels right away instead of carrying them around and risking them on death. Remember that you lose all your levels when you die, so spend them before you go exploring. Players who learn how to make an xp farm in minecraft often build their enchanting room right next to the killing chamber for exactly this reason.

Rates, Tips, and Common Mistakes

A four floor tower farm usually gives you 30 levels in about 10 to 15 minutes of killing, plus bones, arrows, rotten flesh, and gunpowder. Rates improve if you add more floors, build over the ocean, and stay at the right distance from the tower.

Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • Building too low, so mobs spawn on the ground instead of in the tower
  • Leaving a light leak in the spawning chamber, which stops spawns
  • Standing too far from the tower, so mobs despawn before they fall
  • Letting the chests fill up, which stops the whole collection system
  • Forgetting to light up caves below the farm, which fills the mob cap

If your farm feels slow, check your distance first. Stand about 24 blocks from the tower and make sure no other large dark areas nearby are stealing spawns. Also check that the tower is fully dark inside, since even a small hole can cut rates sharply.

FAQ

Does an XP farm work on Java and Bedrock?

Yes. The basic tower design works on both versions, although spawn rules and rates differ slightly. The dark chamber, water channels, and drop shaft work on Java and Bedrock, so this guide is safe for either version.

How many levels does an XP farm give per hour?

It depends on the design and your distance from the tower. A simple four floor farm can give you several full level 30 enchantments per hour of active killing. That is the normal result when you learn how to make an xp farm in minecraft with a simple tower design.

Do I need a mob spawner to build an XP farm?

No. This design uses natural mob spawns in a dark tower, so you do not need to find a dungeon spawner first. Spawner based farms are faster, but a tower farm is easier to build and works anywhere.

Can mobs hurt me at the killing chamber?

They fall with half a heart left, so one hit finishes them before they can attack. Keep the killing chamber enclosed with walls and a roof, and use a shield if a creeper or skeleton survives the fall.

What should I spend my XP on first?

Enchant your best gear first, especially a pickaxe with Fortune and a sword with Sharpness and Looting. After that, use Mending on your tools so you can repair them with the XP your farm gives you.

Start Farming XP Today

Now you know how to make an xp farm in minecraft that is simple, safe, and easy to expand. Build the tower, add the water channels and the drop shaft, and let the mobs come to you. In one good session you will have more levels than a week of mining could give you.

Want to show off your farm or get help from other players? Join {{SERVER_NAME}} on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and share your build on our Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}. Our Survival community loves seeing new farms, and you might pick up a few design tricks for your next project.

Minecraft Villager Trading Hall: Setup & Discounts

Oct 29, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Intro

A minecraft villager trading hall turns random villager trades into a reliable shop. Instead of chasing villagers around a village, you bring them into one safe building, give each one a job block, and walk down a corridor to buy enchanted books, food, tools, and blocks whenever you need them. This guide covers the best layout for a minecraft villager trading hall, which job blocks to use, how zombie discounts work, and how to keep your villagers alive.

The whole build uses simple blocks and no redstone, so it works in Survival on both Java and Bedrock. Once it is running, it is the single best investment you can make in a long-term world.

Why Build a Trading Hall

Villager trades give you things that are hard to get any other way. Librarians sell enchanted books, including Mending. Farmers buy crops for emeralds. Toolsmiths and weaponsmiths sell diamond gear. Clerics sell ender pearls. A good minecraft villager trading hall puts all of those trades in one place, so you spend minutes shopping instead of hours searching villages.

Trading also feeds your emerald economy. Sell crops, paper, or sticks to farmers, fletchers, and librarians, then spend those emeralds on the books and gear you actually want. Once the loop is running, you rarely need to mine for emeralds again.

The Best Layout for a Minecraft Villager Trading Hall

The classic layout for a minecraft villager trading hall is a straight corridor with small booths on both sides. Each booth is 1 block wide and 2 blocks long, with a bed or a workstation at the back, and a trapdoor or fence gate at the front so you can reach the villager to trade without letting it escape.

A practical size is a corridor 3 blocks wide and as long as you need, with 6 to 12 booths per side. Build the corridor first, then add booths one by one as you bring villagers in. Put lanterns or glowstone along the ceiling so the whole hall is bright, and keep the floor flat so minecarts and boats move smoothly if you use them for transport.

Leave space at one end for a storage room with chests for trade goods, and at the other end for a small breeder or holding area for spare villagers. A hall that can grow is better than one you have to rebuild, so leave empty wall space for extra booths.


Alt text: Long corridor trading hall with villager booths for minecraft villager trading hall

Getting Villagers Into the Hall

Moving villagers is the slowest part of the build, but a few tricks make it much easier. The most reliable method is a minecart on rails: push a villager into a minecart, lay rails to the hall, and push the cart along. Boats work well over water and on flat ground, and on Bedrock you can even move villagers in boats over land with a lead in some cases.

Plan your route before you start. Clear a flat path, lay rails or a water channel, and protect the route with walls or fences if it crosses open ground at night. Bring villagers in one at a time, lock each one into its booth with a trapdoor or block, and only then go back for the next one. Rushing this step is how villagers escape or get attacked.

If you have no village nearby, you can cure zombie villagers to start your population. That takes a splash potion of weakness and a golden apple per villager, but it also unlocks the discount system explained below, so it is often worth the effort.

Job Blocks: Which Villagers to Keep

Each villager needs a job block to offer trades, and the job block decides which trades you get. For a minecraft villager trading hall, these are the most useful jobs to fill first:

  • Librarian (lectern): enchanted books, including Mending, plus paper and bookshelf trades. Get several librarians and reroll their first trades until you find Mending and the books you want.
  • Farmer (composter): buys wheat, carrots, potatoes, and beetroot for emeralds, and sells food. Your emerald engine.
  • Fletcher (fletching table): buys sticks for emeralds, and sells arrows and bows. Sticks are almost free emeralds.
  • Toolsmith (smithing table): sells diamond tools and buys coal and iron.
  • Weaponsmith (grindstone): sells diamond weapons and buys coal and iron.
  • Armorer (blast furnace): sells diamond armor and buys coal and iron.
  • Cleric (brewing stand): sells ender pearls and buys rotten flesh.
  • Cartographer (cartography table): sells explorer maps that point to woodland mansions and ocean monuments.

Start with librarians, farmers, and fletchers, since they cover books, food, and emeralds. Add the smiths and the cleric later, once your emerald supply is steady. Do not fill every booth at once: build the hall, fill the key jobs, and expand as your needs grow.

To reroll a librarian's trades, break and replace its lectern before you trade with it even once. Once you trade, its trades lock forever, so check the first book offer carefully before spending a single emerald.

Zombie Discounts: How Curing Saves Emeralds

The zombie discount is the most powerful trick in any minecraft villager trading hall. When you cure a zombie villager, it becomes grateful and gives you a large permanent discount on its trades. On Java Edition, curing can be repeated up to 5 times for stacking discounts, and the discount also spreads to nearby villagers. On Bedrock Edition, the discount works too, but the stacking rules are simpler, so check your edition's behavior before planning a big discount farm.

To cure a zombie villager, trap it safely, throw a splash potion of weakness at it, then feed it a golden apple. It will shake for a few minutes and then turn back into a normal villager with discounted prices. A Mending book that cost 30 emeralds can drop to a single emerald after several cures, which is why experienced players cure their librarians before trading seriously.


Alt text: Villager and zombie in a safe chamber for minecraft villager trading hall discounts

Never let a zombie actually reach a villager you care about. The discount trick uses a separate, controlled zombie villager, not a zombie attacking your hall. Keep the curing chamber sealed with bars or glass between the zombie and the villager, and keep a name tag on any zombie you plan to reuse, so it does not despawn.

Keeping Your Villagers Safe

A trading hall is only useful if its villagers survive. Villagers die to zombies, pillagers, lightning, and their own wandering, so build for safety from the start.

First, light everything. The hall, the roof, and the area around the entrance should all be bright enough that hostile mobs cannot spawn nearby. Second, build the hall from solid blocks with no gaps, and use iron doors or trapdoors for the entrance so zombies cannot break in easily. Third, keep an iron golem or two near the hall, since golems attack zombies and pillagers on sight. Fourth, never leave a villager in an open boat or minecart overnight outside the hall.

On hard difficulty, zombies can break down wooden doors, and a zombie that reaches a villager can turn it. Solid walls, good lighting, and a golem solve most of these problems before they start.

Trading Tips That Save Emeralds

A few habits make your minecraft villager trading hall much cheaper to run. Always trade with a villager you have cured, since the discount lasts and applies to every future trade. Keep a steady supply of trade goods: a small wheat and carrot farm, a tree farm for sticks, and a paper supply from sugar cane cover the most common emerald trades.

Level up villagers you like by trading with them, since higher-level villagers unlock better trades, including the best enchanted books and diamond gear. Do not level up a librarian with a bad first book, though: reroll before the first trade, or you are stuck with that book forever.

Finally, protect your best villagers. If a librarian sells Mending for one emerald, that villager is worth more than a chest of diamonds. Keep its booth sealed, keep the hall lit, and never let it wander.
