FAQ

What is a minecraft villager trading hall?

A minecraft villager trading hall is a building that holds many villagers in individual booths, each with a job block, so you can access all their trades in one safe place instead of searching a village.

How many villagers should a trading hall hold?

Start with 6 to 12 villagers covering librarians, farmers, and fletchers, then expand to 20 or more as you add smiths, clerics, and cartographers. A corridor design makes expansion easy.

Do zombie discounts work on Bedrock Edition?

Yes, curing a zombie villager gives discounts on Bedrock too, but the stacking rules differ from Java Edition. On Java you can stack cures up to 5 times, while Bedrock uses simpler discount rules, so test one villager before curing a whole hall.

How do I stop villagers from changing jobs?

Once you trade with a villager, its job locks permanently. Before that first trade, a villager can change jobs if its job block is broken or claimed by another villager, so lock in good trades early and keep job blocks out of reach of other villagers.

Can villagers despawn or escape from a trading hall?

Villagers do not despawn, but they can escape through gaps, open trapdoors, or unsealed booths. Seal each booth, use trapdoors at the front, and check for gaps after every change to the hall.

Final Word

A minecraft villager trading hall is one of the best long-term projects in Minecraft. Build the corridor, fill it with librarians, farmers, and fletchers first, cure your key villagers for discounts, and keep the whole hall lit and sealed. Minecraft Villager Jobs: Every Job Block & Best Trades

Trading with villagers is the fastest route to enchanted gear, emeralds, and rare items in Survival, and everything starts with minecraft villager jobs. Every employed villager gets its profession from a job block, and each profession unlocks its own set of trades. This guide explains all the minecraft villager jobs, lists every job block, shows you how to assign and reroll professions, and ranks the best trades worth building a trading hall around. With the right setup, a single trading hall can supply your whole team with maxed-out gear.

How Minecraft Villager Jobs Work

An unemployed adult villager that can reach an unclaimed job block will claim it and take on that profession, shown by green particles and a new outfit. Nitwits, the villagers in green robes, never take jobs, and baby villagers must grow up first. Once you trade with a villager even once, its profession and its first trades lock in permanently. Villagers also restock their trades up to twice a day when they can reach their job block, which is why trading halls keep each block right next to its villager. Understanding this lock-in rule is the foundation of smart minecraft villager jobs planning.

Every Minecraft Villager Job and Its Job Block

There are 13 employed professions in the minecraft villager jobs system. Here is the full list:

ProfessionJob Block
ArmorerBlast Furnace
ButcherSmoker
CartographerCartography Table
ClericBrewing Stand
FarmerComposter
FishermanBarrel
FletcherFletching Table
LeatherworkerCauldron
LibrarianLectern
MasonStonecutter
ShepherdLoom
ToolsmithSmithing Table
WeaponsmithGrindstone

Unemployed villagers wear plain brown robes, and nitwits wear green robes and can never be employed.

How to Give a Villager a Job in 4 Steps

  1. Place the job block near unemployed villagers, somewhere they can path to.
  2. Wait a few seconds for green sparkles, which mean a villager claimed it.
  3. Check its first two trades. Do not trade yet if you want different ones: break the job block and place it again to reroll.
  4. Trade once to lock the profession forever.

Rerolling is the heart of minecraft villager jobs strategy, especially for librarians chasing the perfect enchanted book.

The Best Minecraft Villager Jobs for Great Trades

Not all minecraft villager jobs are equal. These are the professions worth building around:

  • Librarian (Lectern): sells enchanted books including Mending, plus name tags and glass. Reroll until you see the book you want.
  • Farmer (Composter): trades crops for emeralds and sells golden carrots, one of the best foods in the game.
  • Fletcher (Fletching Table): buys sticks for emeralds, the cheapest emerald farm in the game.
  • Armorer, Toolsmith, Weaponsmith: sell diamond armor, tools, and weapons at higher levels.
  • Cleric (Brewing Stand): sells ender pearls and bottles o' enchanting, and buys rotten flesh.
  • Mason (Stonecutter): buys clay for emeralds and sells quartz blocks that builders love.

Tips for a Perfect Villager Trading Hall

  • Keep each villager's job block reachable. If a villager cannot path to its block, it may unlink from it.
  • Cure zombie villagers for huge permanent discounts on every trade.
  • Use name tags on villagers you have locked in so you never mix them up.
  • One job block supports one villager, so build a full row of lecterns for a librarian hall.
  • Trade in bulk. Villagers level up as you trade with them, and higher levels unlock better stock, so keep buying until they reach Master.
  • Protect your hall with land claims. A golden shovel claim keeps griefers away from your villagers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a villager change jobs after I trade with it?
No. The first trade locks the profession permanently, so always reroll before you buy anything.

Why will my villager not take the job block?
Another villager may have claimed it first, it may be out of reach, the villager might be a nitwit, or you may have already traded with it.

Do minecraft villager jobs work the same on Bedrock?
Yes. The job block system works the same on Bedrock and Java, including rerolling and trade locking.

Which villager job makes the most emeralds?
Fletcher and Farmer are the fastest, since sticks and crops are cheap to farm in bulk.

How to Make a Beacon in Minecraft: Full Guide

Oct 31, 2026
joynalbokhsho

How to Make a Beacon in Minecraft: Full Guide

A beacon is one of the best late game upgrades in Minecraft. It gives you permanent buffs like Speed, Haste, and Regeneration across your whole base, and it shoots a beam of light into the sky that you can see from far away. If you want to learn how to make a beacon in minecraft, this guide covers every step: beating the Wither, crafting the beacon, building the pyramid, and choosing the best powers.

What You Need First

Learning how to make a beacon in minecraft starts with one rare item: the Nether Star. You get a Nether Star only by defeating the Wither boss, so a beacon is a true late game project. Before you summon the Wither, make sure you have strong gear: diamond or netherite armor, a good bow, a strong sword, golden apples, and milk buckets to clear the Wither effect.

To summon the Wither, place four soul sand or soul soil blocks in a T shape, then put three wither skeleton skulls on top. Wither skeleton skulls drop from wither skeletons in Nether fortresses, and the drop rate is low, so bring a Looting sword. Fight the Wither underground or far from your base, because its explosions destroy blocks and it can wreck a build in seconds.

Once the Wither is defeated, it drops one Nether Star. That star is the heart of your beacon, and it cannot be crafted any other way.

Crafting the Beacon

With the Nether Star in hand, the crafting recipe is simple. On a crafting table, place:

  • 5 glass blocks across the top row and the two side slots of the middle row
  • 3 obsidian blocks across the bottom row
  • 1 Nether Star in the center

That gives you one beacon block. The glass and obsidian are easy to gather by this stage of the game. The Nether Star is the only hard part, which is why the beacon feels like such an achievement.

Building the Pyramid

A beacon does nothing on its own. It must sit on top of a pyramid made of mineral blocks: iron, gold, emerald, diamond, or netherite blocks. You can mix block types in the same pyramid, so most players build with iron because it is the cheapest to farm in bulk.

The pyramid has four tiers, and bigger pyramids unlock more powers and a longer range:

  • Tier 1: a 3 by 3 base, 9 blocks. Unlocks Speed and Haste. Range 20 blocks.
  • Tier 2: add a 5 by 5 layer underneath, 34 blocks total. Adds Resistance and Jump Boost. Range 30 blocks.
  • Tier 3: add a 7 by 7 layer, 83 blocks total. Adds Strength. Range 40 blocks.
  • Tier 4: add a 9 by 9 layer, 164 blocks total. Adds Regeneration as a secondary power and the longest range, 50 blocks.

Place the beacon on the very top center block of the pyramid. If the pyramid is complete and the sky above the beacon is clear, the beam fires upward and the beacon activates. Note that the beam needs a clear view of the sky: glass, leaves, and water do not block it, but solid blocks do.

A full tier 4 pyramid costs 164 mineral blocks, which is 1,476 ingots. That sounds huge, but an iron farm makes it a weekend project. Many players start with a tier 1 or tier 2 pyramid and expand it over time, since you can add layers underneath without moving the beacon.

Choosing the Best Beacon Powers

Right click the beacon to open its menu. You feed it one ingot or gem (iron, gold, emerald, diamond, or netherite) to select a primary power. The best choice depends on what you do most at your base:

  • Haste II (tier 2 or higher): the classic pick for builders and miners. Haste II lets you insta mine stone with an Efficiency V pickaxe, which makes digging out huge areas dramatically faster.
  • Speed II: great for moving around a large base or a farm complex quickly.
  • Strength II: useful if your base sits near a mob farm or a raid farm where you fight often.
  • Regeneration: available as a secondary power at tier 4 only. It pairs with any primary power and slowly heals you, which is excellent for long building sessions.

For most players, Haste II is the first beacon power worth building toward. It changes how fast you can reshape your world, and once you have tried mining with it, going back feels painfully slow.

Common Beacon Mistakes

The most common mistake when learning how to make a beacon in minecraft is blocking the beam. If the beacon shows no beam, check the sky above it: even one solid block in the way stops it. Another mistake is placing the beacon before the pyramid is finished, then wondering why no powers appear. The beacon only activates when it sits on a complete pyramid layer.

Also remember that beacon effects only apply while you stand within range. Build your pyramid near the area where you actually spend time, like your storage room, your farms, or your mining entrance. A beacon at spawn does nothing for a base 200 blocks away.

Finally, do not waste netherite blocks on a pyramid unless you want the flex. The pyramid works exactly the same with iron blocks, and the power does not change with the block type. Save your netherite for gear.

Beacon Tips Worth Knowing

You can change the beam color by placing stained glass above the beacon. Stack different colors to mix custom shades, which is a fun way to mark different bases or farms on a server. The beam is visible from very far away, so many multiplayer players use it as a landmark for their base.

You can also move a beacon. Break the beacon block and rebuild the pyramid somewhere else, and the same beacon works again. The pyramid blocks are not consumed, so experimenting with placement costs nothing but time.

If you play on a server, a shared community beacon at a spawn hub or a trading area benefits everyone who passes through. On {{SERVER_NAME}}, a beacon at a community build is a great way to help new players while showing off a late game achievement.

FAQ

What do you need to make a beacon in Minecraft?

One Nether Star from the Wither boss, 5 glass blocks, and 3 obsidian blocks. Then you need 9 to 164 mineral blocks for the pyramid underneath.

How many blocks do you need for a full beacon?

A full tier 4 pyramid needs 164 mineral blocks in total: 9 plus 25 plus 49 plus 81. Iron blocks are the cheapest option and work exactly like diamond or netherite blocks.

Why is my beacon not working?

Check three things: the pyramid must be complete, the beacon must sit on the top center block, and the sky above the beacon must be clear of solid blocks.

What is the best beacon power?

Haste II is the most popular choice for mining and building, because it lets you insta mine stone with an Efficiency V pickaxe. Speed II is best for large bases, and Regeneration at tier 4 is great for general survival.

Light Up Your Base

That is everything you need for how to make a beacon in minecraft: beat the Wither, craft the beacon, build the pyramid, and pick the power that fits your playstyle. Start small with a tier 1 pyramid, expand it as your iron supply grows, and enjoy the buffs.

Ready to show off your beam? Join {{SERVER_NAME}} on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM, build your beacon where the community can see it, and share screenshots on {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}. Good luck with the Wither fight, and may your beam shine bright.

Minecraft Dimensions Guide: Overworld, Nether & The End

Oct 23, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Every Minecraft world is bigger than it looks. Beyond the forests and villages where you spawn, there are two more worlds waiting, one of fire and lava, and one floating in a starry void. These three Minecraft dimensions each have their own history, dangers and treasures, and reaching all of them is the real journey of survival mode.

This complete guide to Minecraft dimensions covers the Overworld, the Nether and The End: where each one came from, what you will find there, and exactly how to enter and find your way around each dimension. Master these three worlds and you have mastered Minecraft itself.

Minecraft Dimensions at a Glance

There are three Minecraft dimensions, and each one plays a different role in the game:

  • The Overworld is the normal world. It is green, alive, and home to villages, animals, ores and your base. Distances here are the standard measure for the whole game.
  • The Nether is a cavernous world of lava and fire that sits beneath the Overworld. It is dangerous but packed with rare resources, and distance works differently: 1 block travelled in the Nether equals 8 blocks in the Overworld, which makes it the game's fast travel highway.
  • The End is a chain of pale islands floating in a dark void, ruled by the Ender Dragon. This is where Minecraft's main story reaches its finale, and where the best loot in the game hides.
DimensionHow to enterSignature lootBiggest danger
The OverworldYou spawn thereDiamonds, villages, every basic resourceMonsters at night, lava caves
The NetherObsidian portal lit with flint and steelBlaze rods, netherite, quartz, glowstoneLava lakes, ghasts, piglin brutes
The EndEnd portal in a stronghold, filled with eyes of enderElytra, shulker shells, dragon eggThe Ender Dragon, falling into the void

The Overworld: Where Every Adventure Begins

History. The Overworld is the original of all Minecraft dimensions, the world itself, present since the game's earliest versions in 2009. Almost every major update since then has been built on top of it: villages and strongholds arrived in 2011, ocean monuments and new biomes followed, and the 1.18 Caves and Cliffs update in 2021 rebuilt its terrain completely, raising mountains up to height 320 and digging caves down to depth minus 64, with the Deep Dark and ancient cities added below in 1.19.

What you will find. Dozens of biomes, including plains, deserts, jungles, savannas, snowy tundras, swamps and vast oceans. Scattered through them are villages with traders, abandoned mineshafts, dungeons with mob spawners, jungle temples with traps, ocean monuments guarded by elder guardians, woodland mansions, pillager outposts and buried strongholds. It is the only dimension with a normal day and night cycle, weather, and beds that work safely, and it holds every basic resource: wood, stone, coal, iron, gold, redstone, lapis, emeralds and diamonds.

How it works. You never really "enter" the Overworld, because you start there, and every portal journey ends by returning to it. It is the hub that the other Minecraft dimensions connect to, and the only place where an ordinary bed sets your spawn point safely. Protect it, build in it, and treat it as home base for every expedition.

The Nether: The Fiery Shortcut Dimension

History. The Nether arrived on October 30, 2010, in the famous Halloween Update (Alpha 1.2.0). It was the first of the Minecraft dimensions beyond the Overworld, and Notch designed it as a hellish underworld that doubles as a fast travel shortcut. The 1.16 Nether Update in 2020 rebuilt it completely, adding four new biomes, bastion remnants, piglin trading and the ruined portals you now find scattered around the Overworld.

How to enter. Build a Nether portal: an obsidian frame at least 4 blocks wide and 5 blocks tall, with a 2 by 3 opening in the middle (the corners can be any block, so you only need 10 obsidian if you are short). Light the inside with flint and steel, step into the purple swirl, and wait a few seconds while the world loads. If you find a ruined portal in the Overworld, you can also repair it with the obsidian from its chest and light it the same way.

The five Nether biomes. The Nether Wastes are the classic red landscape of netherrack and lava. Crimson Forests grow giant red fungi and are home to piglins and hoglins. Warped Forests are blue and eerie, full of endermen, and one of the safest places in the Nether. Soul Sand Valleys are grey and haunted, with soul fire, fossils and fast ghasts. Basalt Deltas are volcanic fields of black basalt where magma cubes bounce between lava falls. Each biome changes what you can farm, so a serious Nether base usually sits near two or three of them.

What you will find. Lava lakes, glowstone, quartz, soul sand and ancient debris, the rare ore that becomes netherite, the strongest material in the game. Nether fortresses hold blaze rods and nether wart, both essential for brewing potions and for crafting the eyes of ender you need to reach The End. Bastion remnants guard serious treasure and piglins who will trade items for gold ingots, sometimes including ender pearls. Two survival warnings matter more than anything: water evaporates instantly in the Nether, and beds explode if you try to sleep, so use a respawn anchor charged with glowstone to set your spawn instead. One more classic trap: wear at least one piece of gold armor, or piglins will attack you on sight.

How to find fortresses and bastions. Both structures generate in long strips across the Nether, so the reliable method is to pick one direction and explore in a straight line while watching your coordinates. Mark every interesting location as you go, and build your paths out of cobblestone, because ghasts cannot blow it up. And because of the 1 to 8 distance rule, a portal at Nether coordinates 100, 200 links to Overworld coordinates 800, 1600, which is the maths behind every fast Nether highway.

The End: Home of the Ender Dragon

History. The End, often called the Ender World by players, launched with Minecraft's full release, version 1.0.0, in November 2011, together with the Ender Dragon, the game's final boss. Of all Minecraft dimensions it is the strangest and emptiest, and deliberately so. The 1.9 Combat Update in 2016 expanded it with the outer islands, end cities and the elytra, turning a one time boss trip into a whole endgame region.

How to enter. You cannot build this portal, you have to find it. Craft eyes of ender from blaze powder and ender pearls, then throw one into the air: it floats toward the nearest stronghold before dropping or shattering, so bring at least 15 to 20 eyes for the journey. Follow them, and where an eye keeps diving into the ground, dig down carefully until you break into the stronghold's stone brick halls. Explore past the libraries and prison cells until you find the End portal room, and watch out for the silverfish spawner above the portal. Place an eye of ender in each of the 12 frame blocks (a few come pre filled) and the starry portal activates. Jump in, and remember there is no way back except victory or death, so go prepared.

The dragon fight. The main island is pale end stone, ringed by obsidian pillars topped with end crystals that heal the Ender Dragon. Destroy the crystals first, shooting the open ones with a bow and towering up to the two caged crystals to break the iron bars. When the dragon perches on the exit portal, strike its head with your best sword. Slow falling potions or a water bucket will save you when it knocks you into the sky, and carved pumpkins stop endermen from attacking when you look at them. Defeating the dragon drops a huge pool of experience, opens the exit portal, and places the dragon egg on top of it.

The outer islands and end cities. After the fight, a small end gateway portal appears at the island's edge. Throw an ender pearl into it to teleport to the outer islands, a vast scatter of end stone islands with purple chorus trees. Out here you can find end cities, tall structures built from purpur blocks and lit by end rods, where shulkers float and guard the best loot in the game: enchanted diamond gear, and shulker shells for crafting shulker boxes, the backpacks of Minecraft. Beside some cities floats an End ship, and inside its treasure room hangs the elytra, the wings that let you glide and, with firework rockets, truly fly. Of all the Minecraft dimensions, only The End can give you wings.

Dimension Travel Tips and Portal Maths

A little preparation makes travelling between Minecraft dimensions far safer:

  • Link portals properly. Divide your Overworld X and Z coordinates by 8 to find where to build the matching Nether portal, so you always arrive exactly where you plan to.
  • Name your routes. Keep a note of portal coordinates for your base, villages, fortresses and the stronghold. Getting lost in the Nether is the classic beginner disaster.
  • Build a Nether hub. A small cobblestone room around your Nether portal, with paths or ice boat lanes leading out, turns scary lava country into a safe motorway.
  • Carry a dimension kit. Flint and steel (in case your portal gets extinguished by a ghast), a bow, fire resistance potions for the Nether, slow falling potions for The End, and always more food and blocks than you think you need.
  • Respawn smart. Beds only work in the Overworld. Use respawn anchors in the Nether and accept that The End has no respawn item at all.

Quick Checklist: How to Enter Each Dimension

  1. Overworld: you spawn there, and every return journey ends here.
  2. The Nether: obsidian frame (minimum 4 by 5) plus flint and steel. Wear one piece of gold armor to keep piglins friendly.
  3. The End: eyes of ender to the stronghold, then complete the 12 eye portal. Bring your best gear, a bow, a water bucket and plenty of blocks.

FAQ

How many Minecraft dimensions are there?

Three: the Overworld, the Nether and The End. Mojang has never added a fourth playable dimension, so the extra worlds you may hear about are fan ideas, mods or April Fools jokes.

How do portal coordinates work between dimensions?

The Nether is eight times smaller than the Overworld. One block in the Nether equals eight blocks in the Overworld, so divide Overworld coordinates by 8 when you build the matching Nether portal, and multiply by 8 on the way back. The End has no coordinate link at all, since its portal only connects to the stronghold.

Can you sleep in the Nether or The End?

No, beds explode in both dimensions. In the Nether, use a respawn anchor charged with glowstone to set your spawn point. In The End there is no spawn setting item, so dying there sends you back to your Overworld bed.

What happens if you fall off an island in The End?

You fall into the void and die, losing everything you carried, because items dropped in the void are gone forever. Bridge carefully, carry ender pearls for emergency teleports, and never sprint across one block wide bridges.

How do I get back from The End?

Kill the Ender Dragon. The exit portal opens in the middle of the main island, and jumping in returns you to your Overworld spawn point and rolls the game's credits. You can revisit The End any time through the same stronghold portal, and you can even respawn the dragon later using end crystals.

What should I bring for my first Nether trip?

At least one piece of gold armor, a bow for ghasts, plenty of cobblestone for bridging and marking your path, fire resistance if you can brew it, food, and a note of your portal coordinates so you can always find your way back.

15 Best Minecraft Bedrock Seeds for Survival

Oct 28, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Starting a new survival world should feel exciting, not like a long search for food and shelter. The right seed can put a village, a ruined portal or a useful cave close to spawn, so your first day is about building, not wandering. This guide collects 15 minecraft bedrock seeds for survival, grouped by what they are best for, with a short note on what to check first in each world.

A quick warning before you copy a number: Bedrock world generation can shift between updates, and structure positions can vary. The seeds below are community shared examples for recent Bedrock versions. Always test a seed in a creative copy first, with default world settings, before you commit your main survival world to it. That one check saves a lot of frustration.

How to use minecraft bedrock seeds

Using minecraft bedrock seeds takes less than a minute. Create a new world, open Advanced settings, and type or paste the seed number into the Seed field. Keep the minus sign if the seed has one, because dropping it creates a completely different world. Leave the world type on default unless the seed notes say otherwise, then create the world and look around spawn before you start mining.

On mobile, console and Windows, the steps are the same, because Bedrock is one edition across those devices. If a world looks different from the description, the most common cause is a different game version or a changed world setting, not a wrong seed.

Village starts: the easiest first days

1. Four villages around spawn: 302304127329527063

This is a strong first pick among minecraft bedrock seeds for players who want trading and food from day one. Community lists describe four villages around spawn, which means beds, crops and villagers are close at hand. Check each village for a blacksmith chest and a farming plot, then pick the village closest to trees as your base.

2. Four connected villages: -3361685360695458093

Spawn in plains and explore outward for a cluster of villages that sit close together. The appeal here is choice: you can trade in one village, farm in another, and build your base between them. Bring a bed early, because travelling between villages at night is risky without shelter.

3. Meadow villages and ruined portals: 2488740822089678280

This seed starts in a meadow with villages nearby and ruined portals within a reasonable distance. Ruined portal chests can give you obsidian and useful gear, so mark the portal location on your first explore. The nearby cherry grove is also a nice source of pink wood for building.

4. Plains villages, outpost and trial chamber: 21389

A short seed code, and a busy area: plains villages, a pillager outpost and a trial chamber are reported in this region. Treat the outpost and trial chamber as later goals, not day one targets. Gear up first, then return for the loot.

5. Plains villages, outpost and trial chamber: 21433

Similar in style to the seed above, with plains villages plus dangerous structures nearby. Use it if you like a survival world that stays interesting after the first week, when simple farming starts to feel routine.

6. Plains villages, outpost and trial chamber: 1245

Another short code with the same winning mix: villages for a safe start, plus an outpost and a trial chamber for combat loot later. Short codes are also handy on mobile, where typing a long number is easy to get wrong.

Loot and structure worlds

7. Broken structure seed: 3206668053948187953

Community creators describe this seed as packed with structures close to spawn, including points of interest for diamonds, strongholds and trial chambers. Do not rush every structure at once. Loot the safest chests first, set spawn points as you go, and keep a written list of coordinates for anything you leave behind.

8. Island village and cherry grove: -7197042685382216704

This is a self contained survival challenge: an island with a village and a cherry grove. Resources are limited by the island, so plan carefully, farm early, and build a boat route to the mainland when you are ready to explore further. It is a good pick if you enjoy a slower, more deliberate survival run.

9. Mushroom island: 1072901690525385019

Hostile mobs do not spawn on mycelium, which makes a mushroom island one of the safest places to build a base. The trade off is fewer animals and trees, so bring saplings and plan a farm. It is a calm world for builders who still want survival rules.

Easy starts for new players

10. Gentle plains start

Look for a seed with flat plains, trees and a river near spawn. A gentle start matters more than rare loot when you are learning the game. You need wood, stone, coal and food in the first day, and flat land makes a first house much faster to build.

11. River and forest start

A river gives you a safe travel route and a natural border for your base, while a forest gives you wood and apples. Build near the water, but not so close that a creeper can sneak up while you fish. A small dock and a fenced farm are a solid first week goal.

12. Mountain view start

Mountains look dramatic and give you stone, coal and great building spots, but steep ground slows early farming. If you pick a mountain world, build your first base at the foot of the slope, near water and trees, and save the peak for a later watchtower.

Worlds for a longer survival run

13. Cave and mining world

A good mining world has caves near spawn, visible coal and iron, and a safe route back to the surface. Mark cave entrances with torches and a sign, and never dig straight down. Bring plenty of torches, because a dark cave is where most early survival runs end.

14. Desert temple region

Desert temples hold loot chests, but the pressure plate trap under the floor can destroy the loot if you drop in carelessly. Dig in from the side, break the plate first, and loot from a safe distance. A desert village nearby makes this a strong combined start.

15. Island challenge: 600000222763165

This older community example is an island with limited resources, for players who want a real challenge. It is not a comfortable start, and that is the point. Try it only after a normal survival world feels easy, and keep a backup copy of the world in case a mistake costs you a key resource.

Tips for a strong survival start in minecraft bedrock seeds

No matter which of these minecraft bedrock seeds you pick, the first day routine is the same. Punch trees for wood, craft a crafting table and wooden tools, find coal or make charcoal, build a small shelter before night, and sleep in a bed as soon as you can. A bed sets your spawn point and skips the night, which is the single biggest early safety boost.

Next, secure food. Village crops, fishing and a small wheat farm will carry you through the first week. Then mine for iron, make a shield, and only then explore dangerous structures. Players who rush a trial chamber or outpost in leather armor usually regret it.

Finally, keep a notebook, in game or on paper, of coordinates for villages, portals, caves and loot you leave behind. The best minecraft bedrock seeds reward players who explore in stages, not players who sprint in every direction on day one.

FAQ

Do minecraft bedrock seeds work on every device?

Yes, if you are on Bedrock. The same seed on the same Bedrock version should build the same world on mobile, console and Windows. Java Edition uses different structure placement, so use a Java seed list for Java.

Why does my world look different from the description?

The most common reasons are a different game version, changed world settings, or a dropped minus sign in the seed code. Test the seed in a creative copy with default settings to check it before you start survival.

Can I change the seed of a world I already started?

No. The seed is set when the world is created. You need to create a new world with the seed you want, and you can upload a local world to a Realm if you play with friends.

Which seed should a complete beginner pick first?

Pick a village seed from the first section, such as 302304127329527063. Villages give you food, beds and shelter right away, which makes learning the game much less stressful.

Start your next world today

Pick one seed from this list, test it in a creative copy, and start a survival world you actually look forward to loading. If you want to play survival with other {{SERVER_REGION}}i players, join the {{SERVER_NAME}} community and share your seed finds with us. Your next base could start on one of these minecraft bedrock seeds, and your best survival story could start tonight.

Connect through the community links on {{SERVER_NAME}}, find other players on {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}, and bring your new world ideas to the Survival discussion. Happy mining, and good luck on your first night.

How to Beat the Ender Dragon in Minecraft: Boss Guide

Nov 6, 2026
joynalbokhsho

The Ender Dragon is the final boss of Minecraft, and beating it is the moment a survival world truly feels complete. It opens the End gateway, gives you the dragon egg, and unlocks the outer End islands where elytra wait. It is also a real fight: the dragon flies fast, breathes purple fire, and heals itself as long as its crystals stand. That is why learning how to beat the ender dragon in minecraft before you jump through the portal is worth the preparation.

This guide covers the full fight step by step: the gear to bring, how to destroy the end crystals safely, how to handle the dragon itself, and what to do after it falls. It works on Java and Bedrock, and it works for a first time fight with normal survival gear.

Gear You Need Before the Fight

You do not need netherite to win, but you do need solid gear. Bring a full set of diamond armor, enchanted if you can, with Protection and Feather Falling on your boots. Bring a bow with Power and plenty of arrows, and a sword with Sharpness for the close range part of the fight.

Pack these essentials too:

  • A stack of building blocks for climbing pillars and blocking dragon breath
  • A water bucket for fall damage and enderman safety
  • Ender pearls to escape a bad spot or chase the dragon
  • Slow falling potions if you have them, since the dragon can launch you into the air
  • Golden carrots or steak for healing, plus a few golden apples
  • A carved pumpkin or enderman safety plan, because the End is full of endermen
  • Beds or an ender chest with spare gear, since dying in the End is costly

If you are preparing to learn how to beat the ender dragon in minecraft for the first time, bring more gear than you think you need. You can always leave extra supplies in a chest near the portal. The one thing you cannot get back is your enchanted gear if it falls into the void, so never bring anything you cannot afford to lose.

Reaching the End and the First Minutes

To reach the End, you need eyes of ender to find a stronghold and activate its End portal. Throw an eye of ender and follow where it flies, then dig down when it starts pointing straight into the ground. Inside the stronghold, place 12 eyes of ender in the portal frame to open the way.

When you spawn in the End, you appear on a small obsidian platform, sometimes far from the main island. Do not rush. Look around, place blocks to bridge safely if you need to, and avoid looking at endermen. Drink a slow falling potion if you brought one. Your first job is to stay alive and get your bearings, not to attack the dragon.

Destroy the End Crystals First

The dragon heals from the end crystals sitting on top of the obsidian pillars around the island. As long as any crystal stands, the dragon regains health while you fight it. Destroying them is the most important step in learning how to beat the ender dragon in minecraft.

Some crystals sit on short pillars and you can shoot them from the ground. Others sit inside iron bar cages on the tall pillars, and those need a different approach. Climb the pillar with blocks, break the cage with a pickaxe, then shoot or hit the crystal. Never stand next to a crystal when it breaks, because it explodes and the blast can throw you off the island.


Alt: player shooting an end crystal on top of an obsidian pillar in the minecraft ender dragon fight

Work through the crystals one at a time, and keep moving. The dragon flies over the island while you climb, so watch for its shadow and its breath attacks. If the dragon breathes purple fire on you, step out of the cloud right away, because the lingering damage adds up fast.

How to Beat the Ender Dragon in Minecraft: The Fight

Once the crystals are gone, the dragon cannot heal, and the fight becomes a damage race. The dragon circles the island, then swoops down and perches on the exit portal in the center. That perch is your best window to deal damage.

Shoot the dragon with your bow while it flies. Aim ahead of its path, since it moves fast and your arrows take time to reach it. When it perches on the portal, run in close and hit it with your sword. This is the fastest damage you will deal in the whole fight, but be ready to run back out when it takes off again, because its wings and body can launch you into the air.


Alt: player attacking the ender dragon perched on the End exit portal in minecraft

Keep your food bar full and your health topped up. If you get launched into the air, place water below you or use a slow falling potion to land safely. If endermen start chasing you, look at the ground and move away, or put on a carved pumpkin to stop them from getting angry. Players who know how to beat the ender dragon in minecraft stay calm during the perch phases and never chase the dragon across the void.

After the Dragon Falls

When the dragon dies, it explodes into a shower of experience orbs, enough for many levels at once. The exit portal opens in the center of the island, and a dragon egg appears on top of it. Do not try to mine the egg directly, because it teleports away. Push it with a piston or let it fall onto a torch to pick it up.

Walk into the exit portal to return home and see the credits. When you come back, an End gateway portal appears on the edge of the island. Throw an ender pearl through it to reach the outer End islands, where end cities hold elytra, shulker boxes, and more loot. That is the real reward for learning how to beat the ender dragon in minecraft: the End becomes a place you can explore instead of a place you fear.

Tips, Mistakes, and Replays

The fight is very winnable with diamond gear, but a few mistakes end runs fast:

  • Looking at endermen by accident and getting swarmed
  • Standing next to an exploding end crystal
  • Chasing the dragon to the edge of the island and falling into the void
  • Forgetting food and healing items, then dying to dragon breath
  • Bringing your best gear with no backup plan if you die

If you die, do not panic. Your items stay where you died for five minutes, and you can return through the same portal if you are fast. Keep a spare set of iron gear and an extra stack of blocks in a chest near your portal so a second attempt starts quickly.

You can fight the dragon again later by placing four end crystals around the exit portal. Each replay spawns a new dragon and gives you another round of experience, so the End stays useful long after your first win.

FAQ

Can you beat the Ender Dragon with iron gear?

It is possible, but much harder. Diamond armor with Protection and a Power bow make the fight far safer. If you only have iron gear, bring extra healing items, slow falling potions, and plenty of blocks, and take your time with the crystals.

How do you destroy the caged end crystals?

Climb the pillar with blocks, break the iron bars with a pickaxe, then shoot the crystal from a safe distance or hit it and run. Never stand next to a crystal when it breaks, because the explosion can kill you or throw you into the void.

Do endermen attack you during the dragon fight?

Yes, if you look at them. The End is full of endermen, and the fight keeps your eyes moving. Wear a carved pumpkin, or keep your gaze on the ground and the dragon, and deal with any angry endermen quickly before they pile up.

What happens after you beat the Ender Dragon?

The exit portal opens, the dragon egg appears, and an End gateway appears for the outer islands. You can explore end cities for elytra and shulker boxes, and you can respawn the dragon later with four end crystals. That is the full reward when you learn how to beat the ender dragon in minecraft and finish the fight.

How long does the Ender Dragon fight take?

A well prepared fight usually takes 10 to 20 minutes. Most of that time goes to destroying the crystals. The dragon itself falls quickly once it cannot heal, especially during its perch phases on the exit portal.

Take On the Dragon Today

Now you know how to beat the ender dragon in minecraft with a clear plan: gear up, destroy the crystals, use the perch windows, and stay calm. The fight looks scary from the portal, but it is a fair fight once the crystals are gone and you know what to expect.

Want to show off your dragon egg or get help from other players? Join {{SERVER_NAME}} on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and share your victory on our Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}. Our Survival community loves seeing first dragon kills, and you might pick up a few tips for your first trip to the outer End islands.

How to Beat the Wither in Minecraft: Boss Guide

Nov 5, 2026
joynalbokhsho

The Wither is the hardest boss many Minecraft players will ever fight. It flies, it shoots explosive skulls, it drains your health, and it destroys blocks around it. But the reward is worth it: the Nether Star, which you need to craft a beacon. If you want to learn how to beat the wither in minecraft, this guide covers the gear, the arena, and the fight itself, step by step.

Do not rush this fight. The Wither is a boss you spawn yourself, so you choose when and where it appears. Prepare properly, pick a good arena, and the fight becomes very manageable.

What You Need Before the Fight

Wither Skeleton Skulls

You need three wither skeleton skulls, dropped by wither skeletons in Nether fortresses. The drop rate is low, so bring a Looting 3 sword and be patient. A wither skeleton farm makes this much faster, but a normal fortress run works if you take your time.

Soul Sand or Soul Soil

You need four blocks of soul sand or soul soil. Arrange them in a T shape: three across the top and one below the middle block. Then place one wither skeleton skull on each of the three top blocks. The Wither spawns as soon as the last skull is placed, so place that last skull only when you are ready.

Best Gear for the Wither Fight

Knowing how to beat the wither in minecraft starts with gear, not with the fight itself. Bring the best gear you can:

  • Netherite or diamond armor with Protection 4
  • A Power 5 bow with plenty of arrows for the flying phase
  • A Sharpness or Smite sword for the close range phase
  • A shield, a stack of golden apples, and healing potions
  • Milk buckets to clear the Wither effect, and a totem of undying if you have one
  • Strength and regeneration potions for the final phase

Enchanted golden apples are excellent for this fight if you have them. They give you absorption and regeneration when the Wither effect is draining your health.

How to Beat the Wither in Minecraft: Pick the Right Arena

Where you fight matters more than almost anything else. The Wither breaks blocks and flies through the air, so an open surface fight can turn into a long chase across your base. Most experienced players fight underground instead.

The classic arena is a long tunnel or chamber deep underground, near bedrock level. Dig a room about 30 blocks long with a low ceiling. The low ceiling stops the Wither from flying too high and keeps it in bow range. Build the room far away from your base, your farms, and your storage, because the fight will damage the area.

Some players fight in the End, under the bedrock at the center island, where the Wither cannot escape upward. That works too, but the underground tunnel is simpler and does not risk your End setup. Whatever arena you choose, clear it of lava, water, and anything valuable before you spawn the boss.

Spawning the Wither Safely

Build the soul sand T shape in the middle of your arena, then step back and place the last skull from a distance if you can. The Wither needs a few seconds to charge up, and then it explodes, damaging everything nearby. Use those seconds to move to your fighting position, eat a golden apple, and drink your potions.

Never spawn the Wither near your base, your villagers, or your pets. The opening explosion alone can destroy chests and kill unprotected mobs. A dedicated arena keeps the damage contained and the fight fair.

The Fight: Phase by Phase

Phase 1: Flying and Shooting (Above Half Health)

In the first phase the Wither flies and fires explosive wither skulls at you. Stay moving, strafe side to side, and shoot it with your bow. A Power 5 bow with Infinity or plenty of arrows does steady damage here. Block skulls with your shield when you need a break, and keep your distance so the explosions do not catch you.

Watch your health closely. The Wither effect turns your hearts black and drains them over time. Drink milk to clear it if you are low, or eat a golden apple and keep moving until the effect wears off.

Phase 2: Armored and Charging (Below Half Health)

Once the Wither drops below half health, it gains armor that blocks arrows and starts charging at you. Switch to your sword now. Let it charge toward you, dodge to the side, and hit it as it passes. Repeat this pattern and stay calm: rushing in for extra hits is how most players die in this phase.

Keep golden apples and potions ready through this phase. If you have a totem of undying, hold it in your off hand for safety. When the Wither falls, collect the Nether Star immediately: it is the whole reason for the fight.

If you are learning how to beat the wither in minecraft on Bedrock, note that the Bedrock Wither is stronger and faster than the Java version, with a second explosion at half health and more health overall. Bring extra healing, fight underground, and take your time. The strategy is the same, but the margin for error is smaller.

What the Nether Star Unlocks

The Nether Star crafts a beacon, one of the best items in the game. Place the star in the center of a crafting grid surrounded by glass and obsidian to make a beacon, then build a pyramid of iron, gold, emerald, diamond, or netherite blocks under it. Beacons give you Speed, Haste, Strength, Jump Boost, and other effects in a large area around them, which makes mining, building, and farming much faster.

A beacon is also a great centerpiece for a base. Many players build their first beacon near their main storage or farm area, where the Haste effect speeds up every project after it.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Spawning the Wither near your base or your villagers
  • Fighting without golden apples, milk, or a totem
  • Using a bow in phase 2, when the Wither is immune to arrows
  • Standing still while the Wither effect drains your health
  • Forgetting that the Wither destroys blocks, including obsidian over time on some versions
  • Spawning the boss before you have a safe arena ready

Avoid these mistakes and the fight is very winnable, even on your first try.

FAQ

How do I get wither skeleton skulls faster?

Use a Looting 3 sword and farm wither skeletons in a Nether fortress. Each kill has a small chance to drop a skull, and Looting raises that chance a lot. A dedicated wither skeleton farm is the fastest method for repeated fights.

Can I fight the Wither on Peaceful mode?

No. The Wither is a hostile boss and does not spawn on Peaceful. You need to play on Easy, Normal, or Hard, and Hard makes the fight noticeably tougher.

Is the Wither harder than the Ender Dragon?

Most players say yes. The Dragon follows a predictable pattern in one arena, while the Wither flies freely, destroys terrain, and applies a draining effect. Good preparation matters more for the Wither than for the Dragon.

What should I do right after the fight?

Grab the Nether Star, then craft a beacon as soon as you have the glass, obsidian, and pyramid blocks. The best way to learn how to beat the wither in minecraft is to fight it once in a safe arena, then adjust your gear for the next run. Place it somewhere useful, like near your farms or your mining area, so the effects help your everyday projects.

Ready to Take On the Wither?

You now know how to beat the wither in minecraft: gather the skulls, build a safe underground arena, bring strong gear and healing, use your bow in phase 1 and your sword in phase 2, and claim your Nether Star. Take your time, prepare well, and the toughest boss in the game becomes a fight you can win.

Have you beaten the Wither yet, or are you still hunting skulls? Come and tell us on {{SERVER_NAME}}: join on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and share your boss fight stories on our Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}. Good luck, and bring extra golden apples.

How to Cure a Zombie Villager in Minecraft: Full Guide

Oct 23, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Found a zombie villager groaning in the dark and wondered if you can save it instead of fighting it? You can — and learning how to cure a zombie villager in Minecraft is one of the most rewarding things you can do in survival. A cured villager thanks you with massively discounted trades, sometimes dropping prices all the way to a single emerald.

In this guide you'll learn how to cure a zombie villager in Minecraft step by step: the two items you need, how to trap one safely, how long the cure takes, and the mistakes that waste your golden apple. It works the same way on Java and Bedrock.

What You Need to Cure a Zombie Villager

You only need two items, and both are craftable fairly early in a survival world:

1. Splash Potion of Weakness. Brew a water bottle with a fermented spider eye (spider eye + brown mushroom + sugar) — weakness is one of the few potions that needs no nether wart first. Then add gunpowder to turn it into a splash potion you can throw. A normal drinking potion will not work; it has to be the splash version.

2. Golden Apple. Craft an apple surrounded by 8 gold ingots. Not the enchanted golden apple — the regular one is all a cure needs.

That's everything. No brewing stand upgrades, no rare loot. Once you have both items, you're ready for the main event.

How to Cure a Zombie Villager in Minecraft: Step by Step

Step 1: Find a zombie villager. About 5% of zombies spawn as zombie villagers, and villagers killed by a zombie can convert too — 50% of the time on Normal difficulty and always on Hard. Abandoned zombie villages and igloo basements are the most reliable places to find one; an igloo basement even hides a villager and a zombie villager side by side, with the cure items provided.

Step 2: Trap it somewhere safe. Lure it into a small fenced pen, a boat, a minecart, or a little room — and put a roof over it. Sunlight burns zombie villagers, and a cure wasted to sunrise is a painful lesson. A name tag also stops it despawning while you prepare.

Step 3: Throw the Splash Potion of Weakness. Splash it directly so the weakness effect lands — you'll see the potion's particles swirl around it. Timing matters: the golden apple only works while weakness is active.

Step 4: Feed it the golden apple. Right-click the zombie villager with the golden apple in hand (on Bedrock, use the Cure button that appears). You'll hear a loud crackling sound, it starts shaking, and reddish particles rise from it. The cure has begun — do not hit it again.

Step 5: Wait 3 to 5 minutes. Keep it shaded and safe while it shakes. Other zombies won't attack it, but sunlight, lava and your own stray sword swings will ruin everything. On Java, keeping iron bars or beds nearby can speed the process up slightly.

Step 6: Meet your new villager. With a burst of green sparkles, the zombie villager turns back into a normal villager and takes a profession from any job block nearby. Cure complete.

The Real Prize: Trade Discounts

Most players learn how to cure a zombie villager in Minecraft for one reason: the discount. A cured villager feels deeply grateful and slashes its trade prices — enchanted books, gear and rare items can drop to just 1 emerald each. Set your cured villager up with a lectern and you can reroll a librarian's trades until you land premium enchantments like Mending at bargain prices.

One current-version note: curing the same villager over and over no longer stacks the discount endlessly like it once did, so one proper cure per villager is the way to go.

Mistakes That Waste a Golden Apple

  • Curing in the open at dawn — it burns in sunlight mid-cure. Always roof the pen.
  • Skipping the weakness potion — the apple does nothing without weakness active first.
  • Using a drinkable potion — only a splash potion can apply weakness to another mob.
  • Trying to cure a normal zombie — only zombie villagers can be cured. Regular zombies stay zombies.
  • Standing too close with a sword out — one accidental swing during the 5-minute shake can kill your investment.

FAQ

How long does it take to cure a zombie villager in Minecraft?

Between 3 and 5 minutes of in-game time. The zombie villager shakes the whole while, and you'll hear it growl — that's normal. Keep it safe and shaded until the green sparkles appear.

What do I need to cure a zombie villager in Minecraft?

Exactly two things: a Splash Potion of Weakness and a regular Golden Apple. Throw the potion first, then feed the apple while weakness is active.

Can I cure a zombie villager on Bedrock?

Why won't the zombie villager eat the golden apple?

Almost always because weakness isn't active — either the splash missed or the effect ran out. Throw another Splash Potion of Weakness and try again straight away.

How to Get a Totem of Undying in Minecraft: Full Guide

Nov 7, 2026
joynalbokhsho

A Totem of Undying is the closest thing Minecraft has to a second life. Hold one when you take a fatal hit and it shatters instead of you, pulling you back from the edge with a burst of healing. This guide explains how to get a totem of undying in minecraft, where the only source lives, how to win the fight that guards it, and how to farm more once you know the route.

What Is a Totem of Undying?

A Totem of Undying is a rare golden item held in your main hand or offhand. When you would otherwise die, the totem is consumed and saves you. It restores you to half a heart and grants Regeneration, Absorption and Fire Resistance for a short time, which is often enough to eat, run, or fight back.

There are two limits worth knowing before you rely on one. First, a totem cannot save you from falling into the void or from the kill command. Second, it only works while you are holding it, so it does nothing sitting in a chest at home. Keep one in your offhand whenever you explore somewhere dangerous.

Totems stack in your inventory but not in your hand, so carry spares in your inventory and swap a fresh one into your offhand after each save. Knowing how to get a totem of undying in minecraft turns every risky trip into a calculated one instead of a gamble.

How to Get a Totem of Undying in Minecraft

There is exactly one way to get a totem in survival: kill an evoker. Every evoker drops one totem, guaranteed. Evokers are rare illagers that appear in only two places, woodland mansions and village raids, so the whole hunt comes down to reaching one of those two places and winning the fight.

Finding a Woodland Mansion

Woodland mansions generate only in dark forest biomes, and they are usually tens of thousands of blocks from spawn. Walking in a random direction is a waste of time. The reliable method is a woodland explorer map, sold by a master level cartographer villager for a compass and a stack of emeralds.

Trade with a cartographer until it reaches master level, buy the map, and follow it. The map points to the nearest mansion, and the mansion icon on the map shows its position relative to you. Bring a boat, plenty of food, and a bed, because the trip can take a full in game day or more.


Alt text: woodland mansion in a dark oak forest where you learn how to get a totem of undying in minecraft

Beating the Evoker

A mansion can hold several evokers, each in its own room, and they are dangerous. An evoker attacks in two ways: it summons vexes, small flying spirits that pass through walls, and it calls up rows of fangs from the floor that snap shut on anything standing on them.

Go in prepared. A shield blocks the fangs and the vexes, a bow lets you hit the evoker from range, and a stack of cooked food plus a few golden apples covers mistakes. Clear the room of vindicators and vexes first if you can, then focus the evoker itself. When it dies it drops one totem of undying, every single time.

Open every chest as you clear the mansion. Mansions hide diamonds, enchanted books, golden apples and name tags, so the trip pays for itself even beyond the totems. The same route answers how to get a totem of undying in minecraft for players who prefer exploring over building a farm.


Alt text: player fighting an evoker to get a totem of undying in minecraft

Farming Totems From Raids

If one mansion is not enough, raids are the renewable source. A raid starts when a player carrying Bad Omen, or the Raid Omen effect from an ominous bottle in newer versions, walks into a village. Evokers appear in the later waves of a raid, so you need to survive the early waves of pillagers, vindicators and witches first.

Set up a raid farm near a village with a safe fighting position, good armor and a bow, and each completed raid can drop several totems. This is the best long term method if you want a shulker box full of spares for the whole server. For most players, though, the mansion trip is the fastest first totem.

How to Use Your Totem

Hold the totem in your offhand by pressing F while it is selected in your hotbar, or drag it into the shield slot. It works from either hand, but the offhand is best because your main hand stays free for a sword or pickaxe.

A totem triggers the moment a hit would kill you, including lava, drowning and fall damage, as long as the damage itself is survivable by the totem rules. After it triggers, your health jumps to half a heart, so eat immediately and get clear of danger. Players who know how to get a totem of undying in minecraft usually keep one in the offhand during every End trip, nether run and deep cave dive.

Common Mistakes

The most common mistake is forgetting the totem is in a chest. A totem only saves you while held, so make equipping it part of your leaving home routine, just like packing food and torches.

The second mistake is trusting a single totem in a long fight. One save is one save. Against the Wither or the Ender Dragon, bring spares and swap them in between saves.

The third mistake is standing still when fangs appear. Evoker fangs telegraph their line with a small puff of smoke before they snap. Keep moving sideways and they will miss.

FAQ

Can you craft a totem of undying?
No. Totems cannot be crafted. The only survival source is an evoker drop, one per evoker.

Do evokers always drop a totem?
Yes. Every evoker drops exactly one totem of undying when killed by a player.

Can you get totems in peaceful mode?
No. Evokers are hostile mobs and do not spawn on Peaceful, and raids cannot start, so there is no survival way to get a totem on Peaceful.

Does a totem work in the offhand?
Yes. A totem works from either hand, and the offhand is the usual choice so your main hand stays free.

How many totems should I carry?
One in your offhand for everyday danger, and a few spares in your inventory for boss fights or long End trips.

Final Thoughts

Learning how to get a totem of undying in minecraft is one of the best upgrades a survival player can make. One mansion trip gives you your first totem, and a raid farm keeps you supplied forever. Pack a shield, a bow and plenty of food, find your mansion, and never explore without a golden second chance in your offhand again. Jump on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and test your luck in the next raid event with your new totem ready.

How to Tame a Cat in Minecraft: Steps, Food & Fixes

Oct 23, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Learning how to tame a cat in Minecraft is one of the most rewarding things a player can do. A tamed cat follows you everywhere, scares away creepers and phantoms, and even brings you gifts while you sleep. This guide covers everything step by step: where to find cats, the exact food they need, how the taming process works, and how to fix it when a cat refuses to tame.

What You Need to Tame a Cat in Minecraft

You only need one item: raw fish — either raw cod or raw salmon. Cooked fish does NOT work, so keep it raw.

  • Catch fish with a fishing rod in any river, lake, or ocean
  • Raw cod also drops from guardians, dolphins, and polar bears
  • Bring at least 5–10 fish — each feeding only has a chance to tame, so one fish is rarely enough

That's all. No name tag, no lead, and no special items are required to tame a cat in Minecraft.

Once you know how to tame a cat in Minecraft, the whole process takes under two minutes.

Where to Find Cats in Minecraft

Cats spawn as stray cats in villages. For every village, cats regularly wander between the houses, sit on beds and chests, and chase rabbits and baby turtles.

  • Villages in plains, desert, savanna, taiga, and meadow biomes all spawn stray cats
  • A black cat always spawns inside a witch hut in swamp biomes
  • During a full moon, cats that spawn have a higher chance of being black

Stray cats are scared of players and run away fast — which is exactly why the taming method below matters.

How to Tame a Cat in Minecraft: Step by Step

  1. Put raw cod or raw salmon in your hand
  2. Find a stray cat and stop moving — let the cat come to you. Chasing it never works
  3. Crouch (sneak) and move toward it very slowly, or simply stand still and wait until it walks close
  4. When the cat is within reach and looking at you, use the fish on it (right-click / tap the Feed button)
  5. Grey smoke particles mean the attempt failed — keep feeding
  6. When you see red hearts and a red collar appears, the cat is tamed!

Each fish you feed has roughly a 1-in-3 chance of taming the cat, so most cats tame within 2–5 fish. Be patient and don't move suddenly between feeds.

Why Your Cat Won't Tame: Common Fixes

If the cat keeps running or won't eat, one of these is usually the problem:

  • You are moving too fast — sprinting or walking straight at a stray cat always scares it off. Sneak or stand still.
  • The fish is cooked — only RAW cod or raw salmon works.
  • You are standing too far away — the cat must be close and facing you when you feed it.
  • The cat is sitting on a block — cats perched on chests, beds, or furnaces can be hard to feed; lure it down by holding fish and backing away slowly.
  • Other players or mobs nearby — noise and movement keep the cat skittish; try again when the area is calm.

Ocelots Are Not Cats Anymore

A common point of confusion: feeding an ocelot in the jungle no longer turns it into a pet cat. Since the Village & Pillage update, ocelots only gain trust when fed — they stop running away, but they never get a collar and never follow you. If you want a real pet that follows you home, tame a stray cat from a village instead. This is why guides on how to tame a cat in Minecraft always point you to villages, not jungles.

What Tamed Cats Do

A tamed cat is far more than decoration:

  • Creepers fear cats — creepers run away from cats and will not explode near them, making a cat the best bodyguard in the game
  • Phantoms avoid cats — phantoms swoop away from cats, and cats hiss at them as a warning
  • Morning gifts — when you sleep in a bed with your cat nearby, there is a chance it brings you a gift: rabbit's foot, string, feather, raw chicken, rotten flesh, rabbit hide, or even a phantom membrane
  • They follow and teleport — your cat follows you and teleports to you if you move far away, unless you make it sit (use the cat to make it sit or stand)
  • Collar colors — use any dye on your tamed cat to change its collar color

Frequently Asked Questions

How many fish does it take to tame a cat in Minecraft?
Each raw fish has about a 33% chance to tame the cat, so most cats tame in 2–5 fish. Bring 10 to be safe.

Do tamed cats despawn?
No. Once tamed, a cat never despawns and stays yours permanently.

Can you tame a cat in Minecraft Bedrock and Java the same way?
Yes — the process is identical on Java, Bedrock (mobile, console, Windows), and Education editions: raw fish, patience, and let the cat approach you.

Can baby cats be tamed?
Kittens that spawn naturally can be tamed the same way. You can also breed two tamed cats with raw fish to get a kitten that is already tamed.

Your Turn: Tame a Cat on {{SERVER_NAME}}

Now you know exactly how to tame a cat in Minecraft — find a village, hold raw fish, stay calm, and let the cat choose you. Playing on {{SERVER_NAME}}? Connect with PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM, find a village in Survival, and tame your first cat today — then show it off in our Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}.

How to Get Elytra in Minecraft: End Cities & Flight

Nov 1, 2026
joynalbokhsho

The elytra is the single biggest upgrade in Minecraft survival. Once you have it, you can glide across mountains, cross oceans in seconds, and explore your world from the sky. This guide explains how to get elytra in minecraft from start to finish, including how to reach the End, find an End city, and start flying without dying on your first trip.

What Is the Elytra and Why It Changes the Game

The elytra is a pair of wings you wear in the chestplate slot. Jump from a height and press jump again in mid-air to start gliding. You fall slowly, steer with your mouse or joystick, and gain speed by diving and pulling up again. On its own, gliding only carries you downward over distance. Add firework rockets and you can fly upward too, which turns the elytra into true flight.

There is a trade-off. While you wear the elytra, you cannot wear a chestplate, so you lose that armor protection. Most players accept the trade because the mobility is worth it, and they keep a chestplate in their inventory for hard fights. That is why learning how to get elytra in minecraft is a top goal for survival players. The elytra also has durability. It loses one durability point per second of flight, and it breaks (becomes unusable until repaired) at zero, so plan repairs before long journeys.

How to Get Elytra in Minecraft: Step by Step

The short version of how to get elytra in minecraft is simple: beat the Ender Dragon, use the End gateway portal, explore the outer End islands until you find an End city with a ship, and loot the elytra from the ship's treasure room. Each step needs some preparation, so here is the full route.

1. Beat the Ender Dragon

You cannot reach the elytra before the dragon fight, because the gateway to the outer End only appears after the dragon dies. Prepare like any boss fight: a full set of diamond or netherite armor, a strong bow with plenty of arrows, a sword, golden apples or cooked food, beds or blocks for cover, and an Ender chest if you have one. Enter the End through a stronghold portal, destroy the End crystals on the obsidian towers, then damage the dragon when it perches on the exit portal. Take your time and keep your health up. The fight is much easier with Feather Falling boots and slow falling potions.

2. Find the End Gateway Portal

After the dragon dies, a small gateway portal made of bedrock appears somewhere on the main End island, usually near the edge. It looks like a tiny floating frame, too small to walk through. Throw an Ender pearl into it to teleport to the outer End islands. Do not jump into the void looking for it. Walk around the edge of the main island until you spot the bedrock frame, then pearl through. If you are playing with friends, each player needs their own pearl trip, so bring spares.

3. Explore End Cities and Ships

The outer End is a spread of floating islands separated by void, with chorus plants growing on the end stone. End cities are tall towers made of yellow purpur blocks and white end stone bricks, and they spawn on these islands. Not every city has what you want. The elytra only appears in End cities that have a floating End ship docked beside them, in the ship's treasure room. When you spot a city, check for the ship first before fighting your way up the tower.

End cities are guarded by shulkers, box-shaped mobs that hide as blocks and fire homing projectiles. A shulker hit gives you Levitation, which floats you upward for several seconds. Levitation is dangerous near the void, because floating up and then falling can send you off an island. Bring blocks to build bridges between islands, keep your Ender pearls ready as an escape, and never bridge across the void without a safe landing plan. Loot as you climb: End cities contain good gear, enchanted diamond items, and shulker shells, which you need for shulker boxes.

4. Loot the Elytra and Put It On

In the End ship, find the treasure room at the front of the ship. The elytra hangs in an item frame on the wall. Every guide to how to get elytra in minecraft ends at this treasure room, so take a screenshot when you find it. Take it, and also grab the dragon head mounted on the ship's bow if you want it. Equip the elytra in your chestplate slot from your inventory. You now own the wings, but you still need a safe way home. Use an Ender pearl to escape danger, build a safe path back to your gateway, or keep exploring until you have the gear you came for. Remember that dying in the void loses everything you carry, so store spare gear in an Ender chest when you can.

How to Fly With Elytra

Gliding is easy, but flying well takes a little practice. Jump from a high place and press jump again to open the wings. Dive slightly to build speed, then pull up to convert that speed into height. For true powered flight, hold a firework rocket in your hand and use it while gliding. Each rocket gives a burst of speed. Simple rockets made with paper and gunpowder are best for flying, because rockets with firework stars explode and damage you.

Practice in a safe area first. Try gliding off a tall tower in your base before you fly over lava or the void. Learn how hard you can dive before pulling up, and keep an eye on your elytra durability. A good habit is to carry rockets in bulk, plus a spare elytra or Mending setup for long trips. If you run out of rockets mid-flight over the ocean, glide down to the nearest land instead of panicking.

Repairs, Enchantments and Tips

Once you know how to get elytra in minecraft, the next skill is keeping it in the air. Repair the elytra in an anvil with phantom membranes, which drop from phantoms that spawn when you skip sleep for several nights. The best enchantments for an elytra are Unbreaking III, which slows durability loss, and Mending, which repairs it using experience orbs you collect. With Mending and Unbreaking III, an elytra can last almost forever if you collect experience regularly.

A few extra tips make the whole trip safer. Players who master how to get elytra in minecraft usually keep a spare set of rockets and a Mending setup ready before any long flight. Bring a pumpkin or carved pumpkin if Endermen bother you on the main island, since wearing one stops them from turning hostile when you look at them. Carry slow falling potions for the dragon fight and for shulker-heavy towers. Build a small safe room at your End gateway so you always have a place to regroup. And if you play on a server, ask other players where the nearest looted and unlooted End cities are, because popular servers can have their closest cities already cleared.

FAQ

Can you get the elytra without beating the Ender Dragon?

No, not in normal survival. The gateway to the outer End islands only spawns after the dragon dies, and End cities only generate on those outer islands. Creative mode and commands can give you an elytra directly, but in survival the dragon fight is the required first step.

Does every End city have an elytra?

No. Only End cities with a docked End ship contain an elytra, in the ship's treasure room. Cities without ships still have good loot, including enchanted gear and shulker shells, but no wings. If you clear a city and find no ship, keep exploring to the next island.

How do you repair a broken elytra?

Use phantom membranes in an anvil, or use Mending while collecting experience orbs. A fully broken elytra (zero durability) cannot be worn for flying, but it can still be repaired in an anvil, so do not throw it away.

Is the elytra available on both Java and Bedrock?

Yes. The elytra works on Java Edition and Bedrock Edition, with the same basic steps: dragon fight, gateway, End city ship, and rockets for powered flight. Controls differ slightly between platforms, but the route is the same.

Start Flying on {{SERVER_NAME}}

Now that you know how to get elytra in minecraft, put the plan into action on your own world. Gear up, beat the dragon, and go claim your wings. If you play on {{SERVER_NAME}}, team up with friends for the dragon fight and the End trip, and share your first flight stories on our Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}. Join the server at PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and see you in the sky.
