How to Find Diamonds in Minecraft: Best Levels

Oct 31, 2026
joynalbokhsho

How to Find Diamonds in Minecraft: Best Levels

If you are learning how to find diamonds in minecraft, you are chasing the most useful ore in the game. Diamonds unlock the strongest tools before netherite, the best armor you can craft early, and the enchanting table that powers everything else. The good news is that diamond hunting is a skill, not luck. Once you know where to dig, how to dig, and what to bring, you will stop wandering empty caves and start coming home with full stacks.

Why Diamonds Still Matter

Diamond gear sits at the sweet spot of Minecraft progression. A diamond pickaxe mines obsidian, which you need for the enchanting table and the Nether portal frame. Diamond armor keeps you alive in the Nether, in trial chambers, and in late game boss fights. Even after you upgrade to netherite, you still need diamond gear as the base, so diamonds never stop being valuable. Every serious survival world runs on a steady diamond supply.

How to Find Diamonds in Minecraft: The Best Y Levels

The single biggest lesson in how to find diamonds in minecraft is depth. Since the cave and cliff world generation update, diamond ore generates most often deep underground, in the deepslate layers near the bottom of the world. The richest band sits around Y -58 to -59, just above bedrock. This is where diamond ore is most common per block mined.

That changes how you should mine. The old habit of digging at Y 11 or 12 belongs to older versions. In current Minecraft, strip mine at Y -58 or -59 for the best odds. Bring plenty of torches, because mobs spawn in the dark, and keep an eye out for lava pools, which are common at these depths. A water bucket is your best friend down here: it turns lava into obsidian and saves you from an accidental swim.

One more depth tip: diamond ore can appear anywhere below Y 16, just less often. If you find diamonds while exploring a cave at Y -20, that is normal. But if you are mining on purpose, head to the bottom and stay there.

Strip Mining: The Reliable Method

Strip mining is the classic answer to how to find diamonds in minecraft, because it is boring in the best way: steady, safe, and repeatable. Dig a main tunnel at Y -59, two blocks high and one block wide, then branch off side tunnels every two blocks. The two block gap means every ore vein in the area touches at least one tunnel wall, so nothing hides between branches.

A good strip mine session looks like this. Pack an iron pickaxe or better, a stack of torches, food, wood for emergency crafting, and a water bucket. Mine in straight lines and listen for lava and cave sounds, which tell you when a cave is near. Caves are worth peeking into, because exposed ore on cave walls is free diamonds without the digging.

Strip mining is slow, but it is honest work. An hour of focused branch mining at the right depth usually beats three hours of random digging near the surface. Put on some music, keep your tunnels straight, and let the odds do their job.

Caving: Faster and Riskier

Caving can beat strip mining when learning how to find diamonds in minecraft, especially if you enjoy exploring. Big open caves expose huge walls of deepslate at once, and every exposed diamond vein is visible without digging a single block. A single large cave system can hold more diamonds than an hour of branch mining.

The trade off is danger. Deep caves are dark, full of mobs, and often flooded with lava. Bring a shield, a bow, plenty of food, and torches to light your path as you go. Mark your route with torches on one side only, so you can follow them back out. And never dig straight down: at these depths, a single wrong block can drop you into a lava pool.

A smart hybrid approach works well for many players. Strip mine until you break into a cave, explore that cave fully, then return to your tunnels. You get the safety of mining plus the bonus ore of exploration.

Gear Up Before You Dig

When you know how to find diamonds in minecraft, the next step is multiplying what you find. That means Fortune. A Fortune III pickaxe drops up to four diamonds from a single ore block instead of one, which can triple or quadruple your haul. If you do not have Fortune yet, save your diamond ore and mine it later once you do. Mining diamond ore with a Silk Touch pickaxe lets you carry the ore blocks home and break them later with Fortune.

Your pickaxe itself should be iron or better, since stone and wood pickaxes cannot harvest diamond ore at all. Efficiency helps you clear tunnels faster, and Unbreaking keeps your pickaxe alive through long sessions. Mending, once you have a villager trading hall or an XP farm, makes your pickaxe effectively permanent.

Packing matters too. Bring a full inventory plan: torches, food, a crafting table, a furnace for smelting iron on the go, and an ender chest if you have one. Nothing stings like finding a rich vein and having no inventory space left for it.

Other Sources of Diamonds

Mining is not the only way to get diamonds. Village blacksmith chests, desert temple chests, buried treasure, and trial chamber rewards can all hold diamonds or diamond gear. Shipwreck treasure chests sometimes hold them too. These are nice bonuses while you explore, but they are random. For a reliable supply, nothing beats digging at the right depth with the right pickaxe.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

The most common mistake when learning how to find diamonds in minecraft is mining at the wrong depth. Digging near the surface wastes hours on stone that rarely holds diamonds. The second mistake is mining diamond ore without Fortune when you could wait. The third is forgetting lava safety: always keep a water bucket on your hotbar and never mine the block directly under your feet at deep levels.

Another mistake is exploring without a plan. Deep caves are mazes. Set a marker at your entrance, light your path, and leave before your food or torches run low. Diamonds are worthless if you lose them to a creeper on the way home.

FAQ

What is the best Y level for diamonds in Minecraft?

Y -58 to -59 is the richest band in current versions. That is where diamond ore generates most often, just above bedrock.

Do I need Fortune to mine diamonds?

You need an iron pickaxe or better to harvest diamond ore. Fortune is not required, but Fortune III can multiply each ore into up to four diamonds, so it is worth waiting for.

Can I find diamonds in caves without mining?

Yes. Large deep caves expose diamond ore on their walls, and caving at low Y levels is a fast way to spot veins. Light the cave well and watch for lava and mobs.

How many diamonds do I need to get started?

Five diamonds cover the essentials: three for a pickaxe and two for an enchanting table. After that, a full set of diamond armor costs 24 diamonds, and a sword costs two more.

Ready to Dig?

Now you know how to find diamonds in minecraft the efficient way: head to Y -59, branch mine or cave smart, bring Fortune, and respect the lava. Your first full diamond set is closer than you think.

Want to put that new gear to the test? Join the {{SERVER_NAME}} community on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and show off your haul with other {{SERVER_REGION}}i players on {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}. Happy mining, and may your tunnels always glint blue.

How to Breed Villagers in Minecraft: Food, Beds & Farms

Oct 24, 2026
joynalbokhsho

If your trading hall is running low on villagers, learning how to breed villagers in minecraft is the fastest way to restock it. Breeding is simple once you know the two rules that control it: villagers must be willing, and there must be free beds for the babies. This guide covers the exact food amounts, the bed rules, a foolproof manual setup, and a simple auto-breeder you can build in one afternoon.

Related guides: Minecraft Villager Jobs · How to Cure a Zombie Villager · Protect Your Base & Claim Land

How to Breed Villagers in Minecraft: The Two Rules

Everything about how to breed villagers in minecraft comes down to two conditions, and both must be true at the same time. Miss either one and you will see no hearts, no matter how long you wait.

Rule 1: Make villagers willing with food

Villagers become "willing" to breed when you feed them. Give each villager one full portion:

  • 12 carrots, or
  • 12 potatoes, or
  • 12 beetroot, or
  • 3 loaves of bread

Both villagers in the pair need their own full portion, so a breeding pair costs you 24 carrots (or the equivalent) in total. Just throw the food at their feet and they will pick it up. Trading with a villager also raises willingness, so a villager you trade with often may breed with less food, but feeding is the reliable method.

Rule 2: Provide enough beds

Every baby villager needs its own unclaimed bed within reach of the breeding pair. Count your current villagers, then place at least two more beds than that number. The beds must sit in a valid village area where the villagers can path to them. A villager claims a bed by walking up to it, so leave clear walking space around each bed and keep them within roughly 40 blocks of the pair. Since the Village and Pillage update, beds replaced doors as the breeding requirement, so old door-based designs no longer work.

The Simplest Manual Breeding Setup

For your first breeder, keep it small:

  1. Build a small enclosed room, about 5 by 5 blocks, with a door or fence gate you can lock.
  2. Place at least 6 beds inside (enough for your 2 starters plus 4 babies).
  3. Bring two villagers inside using a boat, minecart, or by pushing them down a corridor.
  4. Throw 12 carrots to each villager and step back.
  5. Hearts will appear above them within a minute or two, and a baby villager pops out shortly after.

The baby grows into an adult after about 20 minutes of real time. Move grown villagers to your trading hall and repeat the process whenever you need more.


A farmer villager sharing carrots: the simplest way to make villagers willing.

A Simple Auto-Breeder You Can Build Today

Once you understand how to breed villagers in minecraft, automating it is the natural next step. This design runs on its own as long as the chunks stay loaded:

  • Build a 9 by 5 chamber with beds lined along the walls. Aim for 10 to 12 beds.
  • Lock your two breeder villagers inside the chamber.
  • Place a farmer villager in a small carrot or potato farm attached to the chamber. A farmer automatically harvests crops and throws the extra food down to the breeders, which keeps them willing without you lifting a finger.
  • Babies are only one block tall, so they can slip through a gap made with fence posts or a half-slab opening that adults cannot fit through. Put that gap next to a water channel that carries the babies to a separate collection room.
  • Keep the whole build near your base or inside your main chunk-loading area, because breeding pauses in unloaded chunks.

On Java Edition, make sure the mobGriefing gamerule is on. If it is off, the farmer will not pick up or share food, and the whole machine stalls silently.


Bed rules matter: every baby needs its own reachable, unclaimed bed.

Breeding on Servers Like {{SERVER_NAME}}

On multiplayer servers, the same rules for how to breed villagers in minecraft apply, with two extra things to watch. First, build your breeder inside land you have claimed with a golden shovel, so nobody can break your beds or lead your villagers away. Second, remember that other players' activity can unload your chunks, so place the breeder close to spawn or your main base where the area stays active. If you play on {{SERVER_NAME}}, join with PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and ask on {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}} if you need help picking a safe spot.

Why Your Villagers Will Not Breed

If you followed the steps for how to breed villagers in minecraft and still see no hearts, check this list in order:

  1. Not enough food. The most common cause. Both villagers need a full portion each.
  2. No free beds. Other villagers may have claimed them. Add more beds than you think you need.
  3. Blocked paths. Villagers must be able to walk to the beds. Remove fences, holes, and trapdoors in the way.
  4. mobGriefing is off. On Java servers this stops farmers from sharing food entirely.
  5. Too far away. Breeding only runs in loaded chunks, so stay nearby or keep the area chunk-loaded.

FAQ: how to breed villagers in minecraft

How much food does each villager need?
12 carrots, 12 potatoes, 12 beetroot, or 3 bread loaves per villager, and both villagers in the pair need a full portion.

Do villagers still need doors to breed?
No. Since the 1.14 Village and Pillage update, beds replaced doors as the breeding requirement.

How long does a baby villager take to grow up?
About 20 minutes of real time.

Can unemployed villagers or nitwits breed?
Yes. Any two adult villagers can breed, regardless of profession.

Does trading help breeding?
Yes, successful trades raise a villager's willingness, but feeding exact food amounts is faster and more predictable.

Start Your Breeding Program

Now that you know how to breed villagers in minecraft, set up a small manual breeder this week and scale it into an auto-breeder when you are ready. A steady supply of villagers means better trades, cheaper enchanted books, and a trading hall that never runs dry. Join {{SERVER_NAME}} with PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM, build your breeder inside your claim, and share a screenshot of your setup on {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}. Happy breeding!

How to Find a Nether Fortress in Minecraft: Easy Guide

Nov 4, 2026
joynalbokhsho

A Nether fortress is the gateway to some of Minecraft's best progression. Blaze rods fuel brewing stands and Eyes of Ender, Nether wart grows only in fortress gardens, and wither skeletons drop the skulls you need for the Wither boss. The hard part is finding one, because fortresses are rare and the Nether is dangerous. This guide explains how to find a nether fortress in minecraft, how to prepare for the trip, and what to do once you reach those dark brick walls.

How to Find a Nether Fortress in Minecraft: Preparation First

Before you search, gear up properly. Learning how to find a nether fortress in minecraft is much easier when you are not fighting for your life every few minutes. Bring full iron armor at minimum, with diamond armor preferred, a shield, a bow with plenty of arrows, a good sword, and a stack of building blocks for bridging over lava lakes. Fire Resistance potions help enormously, so brew a few before you leave if you can.

Pack food, torches or a light source, a crafting table, an ender chest if you have one, and golden armor pieces if you play on a version where piglins are hostile without gold. Piglins will leave you alone if you wear at least one piece of gold armor, which saves a lot of unwanted fights while you explore. Mark your portal coordinates before you enter the Nether, either with a screenshot, a written note, or a lodestone compass, because getting lost in the Nether is a real risk.

Build a Portal and Read the Terrain

Build a Nether portal from ten to fourteen obsidian blocks, light it with flint and steel, and step through. Your portal location matters, because the Nether terrain around it decides how far you must travel. Basalt deltas and soul sand valleys are slow and dangerous to cross, while Nether wastes and warped forests are easier to move through. If your portal opens into a cliff face or a lava lake, consider building a second portal a short distance away in the Overworld to get a better Nether spawn.

Nether fortresses generate only in certain areas, and they are large structures made of dark red Nether bricks, with towers, bridges, corridors and outdoor walkways. Players who ask how to find a nether fortress in minecraft often miss one simply because they never look up and scan the horizon. Raise your render distance if your device allows it, and look for straight lines and right angles in the distance, because natural Nether terrain rarely forms those shapes.

Follow the Fortress Strip Trick

Here is the most useful searching method. Nether fortresses tend to generate in bands that run in one direction, so travelling in a straight line across those bands gives you the best chance of crossing one. Many players travel east or west in a straight line, moving a few hundred blocks at a time, then scanning the horizon before moving on again. If you travel diagonally or wander in circles, you can cross the same empty ground again and again.

A practical approach is to pick a direction, build a safe path or bridge as you go, and place torches or distinctive blocks every fifty blocks so you can find your way back. When you reach a large lava lake, bridge across it rather than turning back, because turning back wastes the whole search. Keep an eye on your coordinates and note how far you have travelled, so you know when to turn around and try the opposite direction.

There is no guaranteed distance. Some players find a fortress within a few hundred blocks, while others travel more than a thousand blocks before spotting those dark bricks. That randomness is normal, so do not assume your world has no fortress. Every world generates fortresses, and a steady straight line search will find one eventually.

What to Do Inside a Nether Fortress

Once you find a fortress, slow down. Knowing how to find a nether fortress in minecraft also means knowing how to survive inside one. Wither skeletons and blazes are both dangerous, and wither skeletons inflict the Wither effect, which drains your health over time. Fight them one at a time, keep your shield up, and retreat to a corridor entrance if several mobs gather at once. Blazes fly and shoot fireballs, so a bow is the safest weapon against them, and snowballs also work well if you brought any.

Look for a blaze spawner room, which is a small chamber with a spawner, a fence platform and stairs. This is your blaze rod farm. Kill blazes until you have at least ten rods for brewing and Eyes of Ender, and more if you plan to brew heavily. Also search the fortress for Nether wart gardens, which grow in stairwell rooms with soul sand patches. Take the Nether wart and plant it on soul sand at home, because you will need it for almost every useful potion.

Loot chests are scattered through fortress corridors and balconies. They can hold gold ingots, horse armor, saddles, diamonds, obsidian and enchanted gear, so open every chest you find and light the area as you go. Mark rooms you have cleared with torches so you do not search the same corridor twice. If you find a wither skeleton skull, keep it safe, because three skulls plus four soul sand summon the Wither boss later.

Staying Safe on the Way Home

Finding the fortress is only half the job, because you still need to get your blaze rods and Nether wart home. A safe return trip is part of how to find a nether fortress in minecraft done right, not an afterthought. The safest route back is the path you already marked, so follow your torches and bridges rather than striking out in a new direction. If you get separated from your path, climb to a high point, look for your portal's light or your torch trail, and rebuild bridges carefully over lava rather than rushing across.

Never dig straight down in the Nether, never break the block under a lavafall, and always keep a fire resistance potion or an extra golden apple in your hotbar for emergencies. If you die far from your portal, your items despawn after five minutes in loaded chunks, so return quickly along the marked route. An ender chest loaded with your most valuable loot before the trip home is cheap insurance against a fatal fall into lava.

FAQ

How far do I usually need to travel to find a fortress?

It varies a lot. Some players find one within a few hundred blocks of their portal, while others travel over a thousand blocks. Travelling in a straight line east or west, rather than wandering, gives you the best odds when you are learning how to find a nether fortress in minecraft.

Do Nether fortresses spawn in every world?

Yes, every Minecraft world generates Nether fortresses. They are just rare and spread out, so a methodical search matters more than luck alone.

What is the best loot in a Nether fortress?

Blaze rods and Nether wart are the most important finds, because they unlock brewing and Eyes of Ender. Chests can also hold diamonds, gold, horse armor and saddles.

Should I fight wither skeletons or avoid them?

Fight them only when you are ready, with good armor, a shield and healing items. Their Wither effect is dangerous, so retreat to a narrow corridor if several attack at once, and collect skulls only when you can fight safely.

Can I find a fortress without exploring on foot?

In creative mode or with external map tools you can locate structures faster, but in survival the straight line search, high render distance and torch marking described above are the reliable methods.

Final Thoughts

Now you know how to find a nether fortress in minecraft, prepare for the trip, search in a straight line, and loot blaze rods, Nether wart and chests safely. Gear up, mark your portal, pick a direction and keep moving until those dark brick towers appear on the horizon. On {{SERVER_NAME}}, Nether trips are far more fun with friends, so gather a party, head through the portal at PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM, and share your first fortress find in the Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}.

How to Make a Gold Farm in Minecraft: Easy Guide

Nov 5, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Gold is one of the most useful resources in Minecraft. You need it for golden apples, powered rails, piglin trading, and golden carrots, and mining it by hand is slow. That is why learning how to make a gold farm in minecraft is one of the best upgrades you can make to your survival world. A good farm gives you a steady supply of gold ingots, rotten flesh, and experience without any more mining trips.

This guide covers a simple, beginner friendly design that works in the Nether. It uses zombie piglins, magma blocks, and a basic collection system. You do not need a huge perimeter or a complicated redstone contraption, and you can build it with materials from a normal survival playthrough.

Why Build a Gold Farm

A gold farm solves three problems at once. First, it gives you gold ingots for crafting and trading. Second, zombie piglins drop rotten flesh, which you can trade with cleric villagers for emeralds. Third, the farm gives you a reliable source of experience points while you stand at the collection point.

Gold farms also pair well with piglin bartering. Once you have plenty of gold ingots, you can trade with piglins for ender pearls, crying obsidian, quartz, and other Nether loot. If you are preparing for the End or for a big building project, a gold farm pays for itself very quickly.

How to Make a Gold Farm in Minecraft: The Easy Design

The design in this guide is a spawning platform farm. Zombie piglins spawn on magma blocks, walk toward a lure, and fall into a killing chamber where you finish them with a sword or let fall damage do the work. Hoppers and chests collect everything for you.

Here is the idea in simple terms: build a large flat platform in the Nether, cover it with magma blocks so piglins spawn there, and add turtle eggs or a piglin lure in the middle to pull them toward a hole. Below the hole, place a collection area with hoppers feeding into chests. Stand at the collection point, and the farm runs while you wait.

Materials You Need

Before you start, gather these materials:

  • 3 stacks of magma blocks for the spawning platform
  • 2 stacks of building blocks (netherrack or blackstone work well)
  • 1 stack of trapdoors to control piglin movement
  • 20 hoppers and 4 chests for collection
  • 1 stack of slabs for the roof and safe walkways
  • Turtle eggs (for the lure) or a named piglin in a boat
  • A sword with Looting if you have one, since Looting increases gold nugget drops
  • Fire resistance potions and gold armor for safe travel in the Nether

The exact amounts depend on how big you build. A 24 by 24 platform is a good starting size. You can always expand it later if you want higher rates.

Building the Farm Step by Step

1. Pick a Safe Location

Build in a Nether wastes biome if you can, because zombie piglins spawn there in large numbers. Build high up, away from basalt deltas and other structures, and light up nearby caves and ledges if mobs are spawning outside your farm. Wear at least one piece of gold armor so piglins stay neutral while you work.

2. Build the Spawning Platform

Lay out a flat platform of magma blocks, about 24 blocks by 24 blocks. Magma blocks are important because zombie piglins can spawn on them, and the damage they deal helps weaken mobs. Leave a 3 by 3 hole in the center of the platform, and place trapdoors around the hole so piglins walk into it instead of stopping at the edge.

3. Add the Lure and the Drop

Place turtle eggs in the center above the hole, or put a piglin in a boat near the hole as a lure. Zombie piglins are drawn toward turtle eggs and will walk off the platform and fall. Below the platform, build a drop shaft about 20 blocks deep. The fall weakens the piglins so one sword hit finishes them, which gives you experience and Looting drops.

4. Build the Collection System

At the bottom of the drop shaft, place hoppers in a row feeding into double chests. Add a small safe room around the collection point with walls and a roof, so ghasts cannot hit you while you wait. Stand in this room and the farm will keep running as long as you stay within range of the spawning platform.

If you are learning how to make a gold farm in minecraft for the first time, keep this version simple. Do not add extra layers, sorting systems, or automatic killers until the basic farm works. A simple farm that runs is better than a complex farm that breaks.

Collection, Sorting, and Storage

Gold farms produce a lot of items fast. Gold nuggets stack into ingots at your crafting table, and rotten flesh piles up quickly. Set up extra chests early, or you will find the hoppers backing up and the farm stopping.

A simple fix is to add a second row of chests and check them between AFK sessions. Players who learn how to make a gold farm in minecraft often expand to two layers once the first platform runs well.

A simple fix is to add a second row of chests and check them between AFK sessions. If you have an item sorter from another project, you can connect it later to separate gold nuggets, rotten flesh, and gold swords automatically. Keep your gold swords for smelting into nuggets too, since smelted gold swords add a nice bonus to every session.

Rates, Tips, and Common Mistakes

A single layer platform farm usually produces several hundred gold nuggets per hour, plus experience and rotten flesh. Rates improve if you build more layers, stay at the right distance from the platform, and keep other spawnable areas dark or covered.

Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • Building too close to a fortress or bastion, which fills the mob cap with other mobs
  • Forgetting gold armor and angering every piglin in the area
  • Standing too far from the platform, so piglins stop spawning or despawn
  • Letting the chests fill up, which stops the whole collection system
  • Building the platform from normal blocks instead of magma blocks, which lowers spawn rates

If your farm feels slow, check your distance first. Stand about 24 blocks from the edge of the platform, and make sure no other large flat areas nearby are stealing spawns.

FAQ

Does a gold farm work on Java and Bedrock?

Yes. The basic idea works on both versions, although spawn rules and rates differ slightly. The magma block platform, turtle egg lure, and hopper collection system work on Java and Bedrock, so this guide is safe for either version.

Do I need Looting for a gold farm?

No, but Looting helps a lot. A Looting 3 sword can nearly double your gold nugget drops. If you do not have Looting yet, the farm still works, and the experience it gives you can help you enchant a better sword.

Can zombie piglins anger and attack me at the farm?

They stay neutral if you wear gold armor and do not attack them first. Once you start hitting them at the collection point, nearby piglins may become angry, so keep the killing chamber enclosed and use a shield if you need one.

How much gold does a simple farm make?

A single layer farm typically makes enough gold for regular trading, golden apples, and powered rails. That is the normal result when you learn how to make a gold farm in minecraft with a single layer design. If you need gold for a huge project, add a second layer or run the farm during longer AFK sessions.

Start Farming Gold Today

Now you know how to make a gold farm in minecraft that is simple, safe, and easy to expand. Build the platform, set up the lure and collection system, and let the zombie piglins do the rest. In one good session you will have more gold than a week of mining could give you.

Want to show off your farm or get help from other players? Join {{SERVER_NAME}} on PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM and share your build on our Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}. Our Survival community loves seeing new farms, and you might pick up a few design tricks for your next project.

Minecraft Color Codes: Complete Chart for Java & Bedrock

Oct 23, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Minecraft Color Codes: Complete Chart for Java & Bedrock

If you have ever seen rainbow text in Minecraft chat or glowing signs at a server spawn, you have already seen minecraft color codes in action. These short codes color and style text in chat, on signs, in books, and even in server MOTDs. This guide gives you the complete minecraft color codes chart for both Java Edition and Bedrock Edition, with every color, every formatting code, and copy-and-paste examples you can use right away. Learning minecraft color codes takes five minutes, and once you know the pattern you will never need to look them up again.

What Are Minecraft Color Codes?

Every color or style in Minecraft text starts with the section sign (§) followed by one character. Codes 0 to 9 and a to f set one of 16 colors, while codes k to o apply formatting like bold or italic, and r resets everything back to normal. That single pattern is the whole system behind minecraft color codes, and it works the same on Java and Bedrock.

The Complete Minecraft Color Codes Chart

This table lists all 16 minecraft color codes with each code character, official color name, and common uses.

CodeColorCommon uses
§0BlackSpooky signs
§1Dark BlueTeam colors
§2Dark GreenMoney text
§3Dark AquaWater themes
§4Dark RedWarnings
§5Dark PurpleMagic themes
§6GoldPremium ranks
§7GrayDescriptions
§8Dark GrayMuted labels
§9BlueCool accents
§aGreenSuccess messages
§bAquaBright headers
§cRedAlerts
§dLight PurplePlayful signs
§eYellowAttention grabbers
§fWhiteDefault text

Minecraft Formatting Codes

Colors are only half the story. These formatting companions to minecraft color codes change the style of the text itself.

CodeEffectNotes
§kObfuscatedScrambles characters into "magic" text
§lBoldMakes text thicker and bolder
§mStrikethroughDraws a line through the text
§nUnderlineUnderlines the text
§oItalicSlants the text
§rResetClears all color and formatting

Combine them freely: §6§l makes bold gold text. Always end styled text with §r so the formatting does not leak into your message.

How to Use Minecraft Color Codes on Java Edition

The tricky part on Java is typing the § symbol, since most keyboards have no key for it. The reliable methods are simple: copy § from this page and paste it where needed, or on Windows hold Alt and type 0167 on the number pad. Once the symbol is in your chat box, add the code character right after it with no space, like §6Hello. Vanilla Java chat, signs, and books all accept minecraft color codes typed this way.

How to Use Minecraft Color Codes on Bedrock Edition

Bedrock players use the exact same § codes. Copy the symbol from a website or another message, then long-press to paste it into chat or onto a sign. Because Bedrock runs on phones, tablets, and consoles, copy-and-paste is the universal method, and it works for books as well. If a code shows up as plain text instead of coloring your words, the server or Realm has formatting disabled, which brings us to the fixes below.

Where Minecraft Color Codes Work (and Where They Do Not)

Minecraft color codes are accepted in most places where you type text, but not everywhere:

  • Chat and commands on most servers
  • Signs and hanging signs, on both editions
  • Book and quill titles and pages
  • Server MOTD in server.properties, for server owners
  • Many plugin servers use & instead of §, so ask staff which symbol to use
  • Anvils do not apply color codes when renaming items in vanilla Minecraft; colored item names need a plugin

Fixing Common Minecraft Color Codes Problems

The code appears as plain text. The server stripped the formatting, or you used & on a server that expects § (or the reverse). Try the other symbol.

You see boxes or question marks. Your font or device cannot render §. Copy the symbol from this page instead of typing it.

Colors bleed into the next line. You forgot §r at the end. Add §r after your styled text to reset it.

Nothing works on a Realm. Realms allow minecraft color codes in chat and on signs, so re-copy the symbol and try again.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do minecraft color codes work on Realms?
Yes. Realms support them in chat, on signs, and in books exactly like a normal single-player world.

Can I use color codes in my username?
No. Player names cannot contain formatting codes in vanilla Minecraft.

Do color codes work in minigame lobby chat?
On most servers, yes, if the chat plugin allows formatting. Check /rules if your colors get stripped.

Are color codes cheating?
No. They only change how text looks and give no gameplay advantage.

Try Them on {{SERVER_NAME}}

Now that you know every minecraft color codes trick, try them out. Style your chat messages, make your shop signs pop, and label your base with colored signs on the {{SERVER_NAME}} Survival server. Connect with PLAY.{{SERVER_NAME}}MC.COM, then share your best-looking signs on our Discord at {{DISCORD_INVITE_URL}}.

How to Make Potions in Minecraft: Brewing Guide

Nov 2, 2026
joynalbokhsho

Potions are one of the most useful tools in Minecraft survival. A single bottle can heal you in a fight, let you run faster, breathe underwater, or turn invisible. This guide explains how to make potions in minecraft from your first brewing stand to your first useful potion, with the exact recipes that new players actually need.

If you have never brewed before, do not worry. Learning how to make potions in minecraft takes one trip to the Nether and a few minutes of practice. Once you understand the base potion, the rest is just adding one ingredient at a time.

What You Need Before You Brew

Before you start, gather this gear. You need a brewing stand, which is crafted from one blaze rod and three cobblestone blocks. Blaze rods drop from blazes in Nether fortresses, so bring decent armor and a bow for that trip. You also need glass bottles, crafted from three glass blocks, and a water source to fill them. Cauldrons can also fill bottles, but a water bucket or a nearby river is simpler.

The fuel for brewing is blaze powder, made by crafting a blaze rod. Each piece of blaze powder fuels 20 brewing operations, so one rod goes a long way. The most important ingredient is nether wart, which grows in Nether fortresses and can be planted on soul sand back home. Without nether wart, you cannot make the awkward potion that most useful potions start from. Plant a small nether wart farm on soul sand near your base so you never run out.

How to Make Potions in Minecraft: Step by Step

Here is the core loop for how to make potions in minecraft. Every potion follows the same pattern: fill bottles with water, brew a base potion, then add an effect ingredient.

1. Set up the brewing stand

Place the brewing stand and put blaze powder in the fuel slot on the left. Put three water bottles in the three bottle slots at the bottom. You can brew one, two, or three bottles at once, and brewing three at once costs the same ingredients as brewing one, so always fill all three slots when you can.

2. Brew an awkward potion

Add nether wart to the ingredient slot at the top. Wait for the brewing arrow to finish. Your water bottles become awkward potions. An awkward potion has no effect on its own, but it is the base for almost every useful potion in the game. This is the step that trips up new players, because skipping it and adding an effect ingredient straight to a water bottle usually gives a mundane potion that does nothing useful.

3. Add an effect ingredient

Now add the ingredient for the effect you want. Glistering melon slice makes a Potion of Healing. Sugar makes a Potion of Swiftness. Blaze powder makes a Potion of Strength. Golden carrot makes a Potion of Night Vision. Pufferfish makes a Potion of Water Breathing. Magma cream makes a Potion of Fire Resistance. Spider eye makes a Potion of Poison, and a fermented spider eye added to most potions turns it into a corrupted version, for example Poison becomes a Potion of Harming.

4. Strengthen or extend the potion

Once you have a basic effect potion, you can change it again. Redstone dust extends the duration, for example a 3 minute Swiftness potion becomes 8 minutes. Glowstone dust upgrades the effect level, for example Healing I becomes Healing II, but it usually shortens the duration. You cannot use both redstone and glowstone on the same potion, so pick duration or power based on the job. For boss fights, power often wins. For exploring, duration usually wins.

5. Make splash or lingering potions if you need them

Add gunpowder to a potion to turn it into a splash potion, which you throw instead of drinking. Add dragon's breath to a splash potion to make a lingering potion, which leaves a cloud on the ground. Splash potions are great for healing teammates or throwing harming potions at enemies. Most solo players can skip lingering potions until late game, because dragon's breath requires beating the Ender Dragon.

Best Potions to Brew First

If you are just starting, brew these five first. They cover healing, movement, and survival, and they are cheap to make once you have a nether wart farm.

First, Potion of Healing. It restores health instantly, which makes it the best emergency potion in the game. Brew awkward potion plus glistering melon slice, then add glowstone for Healing II if you want a bigger instant heal.

Second, Potion of Swiftness. Sugar plus awkward potion gives you a speed boost for running, exploring, and escaping danger. Add redstone for the 8 minute version, which is perfect for long trips.

Third, Potion of Fire Resistance. Magma cream plus awkward potion lets you swim in lava for several minutes. This is essential for Nether exploring, Bastion looting, and building in lava areas. It is also a lifesaver if you fall into lava by accident.

Fourth, Potion of Water Breathing. Pufferfish plus awkward potion lets you breathe underwater, which makes ocean monument raids and underwater building far easier. Pair it with Night Vision from a golden carrot for the best underwater experience.

Fifth, Potion of Strength. Blaze powder plus awkward potion increases your melee damage, which helps in boss fights, raids, and PvP. Strength II from glowstone is a serious damage boost, but it only lasts 90 seconds, so save it for the fight itself.

Players who master how to make potions in minecraft usually keep a small brewing room stocked with nether wart, blaze powder, redstone, glowstone, and the ingredients above, so brewing a new batch takes seconds instead of a farming trip.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

The most common mistake is forgetting fuel. The brewing stand does nothing without blaze powder in the fuel slot, even if all the other slots are correct. The second mistake is brewing only one bottle at a time. Always brew three, since the ingredient cost is the same. The third mistake is adding glowstone and redstone in the wrong order or trying to use both. Pick one, and remember that adding a new ingredient after redstone or glowstone can reset or change the potion in ways you did not expect, so check the result before you brew a full batch.

Another mistake is drinking the wrong potion in a fight. Players learning how to make potions in minecraft should keep their stock organised from the start, because a mixed-up chest causes mistakes at the worst moment. Splash potions of Harming look similar to Healing potions at a glance, so label your chests and keep harming potions away from your healing stock. Finally, remember that undead mobs react backwards to healing and harming. Healing potions damage zombies and skeletons, while Harming potions heal them, which is a fun trick for fighting undead mobs.

FAQ

Do you need to go to the Nether to make potions?

Yes, for most useful potions. You need blaze rods for the brewing stand and fuel, and nether wart for the awkward potion base. A few potions, like Mundane potions, can be made without Nether items, but they have no useful effect. Plan one Nether trip with good gear, grab extra blaze rods and nether wart, and you are set for a long time.

What is the difference between redstone and glowstone in brewing?

Redstone extends a potion's duration. Glowstone increases its power level, usually while shortening its duration. You can only apply one of them to a given potion, so choose based on what you need: longer exploration potions get redstone, combat potions often get glowstone.

Can you brew potions on both Java and Bedrock?

Yes. The brewing stand, awkward potion, and main recipes work the same on Java Edition and Bedrock Edition. The brewing stand interface looks slightly different between versions, but the ingredient order and results are the same.

Why did my potion do nothing?

You probably brewed a mundane or thick potion by adding an ingredient to a water bottle without making an awkward potion first, or you added an ingredient that does not change that base. That base step is the key to how to make potions in minecraft work every time.
